## PATCH PLATFORM v1.15 — HOST PROJECT CARDS READ 0 TASKS (July 29, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Checkpoint Beta host card reads "5 projects · 5 tasks" at checkpoint level, but EVERY project row shows "0 tasks" and "0 players in scope · 0/0 completions" — while the player dashboard shows the same tasks correctly under their projects. Ennis's concern (correct): if the host card can't see the tasks, submitted approvals are unreachable from it.
- ROOT CAUSE (code, resolver asymmetry): `mcChildTasksForCheckpoint` honors BOTH link directions (cp.taskIds reverse AND task.roundId forward) — hence the correct 5 at checkpoint level. `mcChildTasksForProject` honored ONLY `project.taskIds` (reverse) and ignored `task.projectId` (forward), which is what the task form writes. So forward-wired tasks counted at checkpoint level and vanished at project level. Same family as PLATFORM v1.9 (two-hop checkpoint linkage) — the fix there was the player side; this is the host side.
- FIX: `mcChildTasksForProject` now returns the UNION of both directions, de-duplicated by id, and tolerates a missing taskIds array / null project. Host project cards, MISSION CONTENTS counts, per-task submission chips and the approval surfaces that hang off these child lists all resolve again.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean; 8-case Node unit test on the extracted resolver (forward-only resolution, isolation between projects, reverse-only still works, union de-dupes, missing array, null input) all PASS.
- NOT VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE DATA: Supabase SQL was unreachable this session (even `SELECT 1` timed out via MCP; the sandbox cannot reach supabase.co directly and the project itself reports ACTIVE_HEALTHY). STILL TO CHECK when SQL returns: (1) whether the 5 Beta tasks carry projectId, roundId, or neither — if NEITHER, they also need linking in data, exactly like the Alpha tasks in v1.9; (2) "0 players in scope" is a separate cohort-fence question — confirm the Beta checkpoint/projects/tasks carry `assignedTo: ["Global Digital Intern"]`, otherwise no player resolves into scope; (3) confirm no pending Beta submissions were stranded while the host card was blind.

## PATCH PATHWAYS v1.16 — NODE SAVE ABORT + SCHEME-LESS URL 404 (July 29, Ennis)
- SYMPTOMS (Ennis, Core Pathways node editor): node "not saving or opening", and the embedded program link 404s at `pflx-pathway-portal.vercel.app/www.playdna.lovable.app`.
- ROOT CAUSE 1 — URL: `_doSaveNode` stored `neUrl` / `neContentUrl` verbatim. A host typing a domain the way they read it ("www.playdna.lovable.app", no scheme) is a RELATIVE reference, so `window.open()` and the course iframe resolved it against the portal origin → 404 NOT_FOUND. The 404 id in Ennis's screenshot (`sin1::km8k9…`) is Vercel serving the portal, not the target app.
- ROOT CAUSE 2 — SAVE ABORT: every field in `_doSaveNode` was read as `document.getElementById(id).value` with NO null guard (only neEntryVideo/neEntryBadge were guarded). A single missing or renamed field in the editor markup throws, the outer try/catch shows "SAVE ERROR", and the node never persists — a whole-save failure caused by one absent input.
- FIX: (1) new `pflxNormalizeExternalUrl(raw)` — adds `https://` only when the value clearly names a domain (host.tld[/path], no spaces); anything with a scheme, protocol-relative `//`, absolute `/path`, `data:`/`blob:`, `#`/`?`, or a relative course file (`courses/x.html`) is returned untouched. Applied on SAVE (url + contentUrl) and again at OPEN time for `window.open` and `courseFrame.src`, so nodes saved BEFORE this patch work without a re-save. (2) `_doSaveNode` now reads every field through null-safe `neVal`/`neChecked`/`neInt` helpers that fall back to defaults and log the missing ids — one bad field can no longer abort the save.
- Verified: 4-block syntax gate clean (pathway.html); 12-case Node unit test on the extracted normalizer (bare www, bare domain+path, https/http passthrough, protocol-relative, absolute path, relative course file, data URI, empty, whitespace, null, prose left alone) all PASS.
- STILL OPEN — "node is not showing correctly": needs specifics (which node, and what renders wrong). The screenshot shows the course overlay compositing over the pathway map with a stray "READY (HIDDEN)" label, which reads like a layering/visibility issue in the launch overlay rather than node data — not diagnosed this session.
- CONTEXT: Supabase SQL was unreachable for the whole session (MCP `SELECT 1` timed out; sandbox has no direct route to supabase.co), so nothing in this patch is verified against live node data.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.17 — SUBMISSION UPLOADS → SUPABASE STORAGE (July 29, Ennis-approved: option A)
- **ROOT CAUSE of the "Supabase issue"** (and probably several others): `pflx_mc_tasks` had grown to **19.01 MB, of which 18.94 MB (99.6%) was base64 images** embedded in submissions — 25 uploads across 49 submissions; a single "Walk the Story Building" submission held 8.89 MB, the Discord task 5.12 MB across 15. Measured via REST because MCP SQL was unusable.
- CONSEQUENCES: (a) single-row reads of `pflx_mc_tasks` exceed Postgres's statement timeout → HTTP 500 / `57014`, which is what killed SQL access mid-session (the connector was the messenger, not the cause — a `select key limit 1` answers in 0.35 s and the platform's own boot pull returns 200); (b) the Console boot pull downloads **20.3 MB every time, 19 of it that one row** — on iOS that is very likely the real cause of the reload loop v1.11's lite-device gate only partly mitigated; (c) every save pushes all 19 MB back, magnifying the stale-writer overwrite class; (d) it grows with every screenshot.
- CODE (this patch): new `pflxUploadSubmissionFile(dataUrl, fileName, playerId)` → uploads to the **`pflx-submissions`** bucket and returns a public URL; `pflxSubmissionFileSrc(sub)` resolves fileUrl → legacy base64 string → legacy `{name,type,data}` so nothing already submitted breaks. BOTH submit paths (`ppSubmitTask`, `mcPlayerSubmitTask`) are now async, upload first, store `fileUrl` and leave `fileData` null. If Storage is unreachable the base64 is kept so a student never loses evidence, but anything >~1.2 MB is refused with a "use a Drive link" message so the row cannot re-bloat. Host review render updated to use the resolver (image inline, non-image as a link).
- MIGRATION: `PFLX Apps/pflx-migrate-uploads.sh` — dry-run by default, `--apply` to write. Backs the row up locally first, uploads each image, rewrites fileData → fileUrl, writes back with `Prefer: return=minimal` (never pulls 19 MB down again). DRY RUN VERIFIED: 21 tasks, 25 uploads, 18.94 MB to move.
- **BLOCKED ON HOST (one time, ~1 min)**: the anon key cannot create buckets (correctly — RLS). In the Supabase dashboard: Storage → New bucket → `pflx-submissions` → **Public** → Create; then Policies → New policy → allow **SELECT** and **INSERT** for anon. Then run `bash "PFLX Apps/pflx-migrate-uploads.sh" --apply`.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean; 5-case unit test on the src resolver (fileUrl precedence, legacy string, legacy object, empty, null) all PASS.
- AFTER MIGRATION, still to check (was blocked all session by the timeout): Beta task→project linkage, "0 players in scope" cohort assignment, and whether any Beta submissions were stranded.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.18 — GOOGLE DRIVE EVIDENCE PATHS ×3 (July 29, Ennis: "I like all 3")
- CONTEXT: mid-session the Supabase database degraded (statement timeouts → Storage `DatabaseTimeout` → **429 too_many_connections** → REST 521/503 → PostgREST `PGRST002` schema-cache retry), so the v1.17 Storage bucket could not even be created. Ennis asked about Google Drive — which testers ALREADY use, since the FeedForward Form deposits every screenshot into a Drive folder. All three routes were approved and built.
- **(1) DRIVE LINKS RENDER INLINE — zero DB dependency, live now.** `pflxDriveFileId()` parses every Drive URL shape (`/file/d/ID`, `?id=ID`, `/uc?id=`, docs `/d/ID`); `pflxDriveThumb()` converts to `drive.google.com/thumbnail?id=…&sz=w1000`, which unlike a share link DOES hotlink. `pflxSubmissionFileSrc()` now resolves Storage URL → legacy base64 → **Drive link thumbnail**, and the host review panel treats a Drive thumbnail as an image. A pasted Drive link is now reviewed inline instead of as a bare hyperlink. The submit form already carried the "share as Anyone with the link" tip.
- **(2) GOOGLE PICKER — built, dormant until configured.** `pflxPickFromDrive()` loads GIS + picker on demand, requests `drive.file` scope, opens Upload/Docs views, sets the picked file link-readable, and returns its link; `pflxDrivePickInto(inputId)` fills the link field. The "📁 Choose from Google Drive" button renders ONLY when `window.PFLX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` is set — deliberate, because school Workspace accounts frequently block third-party OAuth (same class as Aadhya's blocked writes) and a dead button is worse than none. HOST STEP: create an OAuth client id (Google Cloud → Credentials → OAuth client → Web app, authorized origin `https://www.prototypeflx.com`) and set `PFLX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`.
- **(3) MANAGED DRIVE UPLOAD — new endpoint `pflx-darkcampus/src/app/api/drive-upload/route.ts`.** Service-account upload into the HOST's Drive folder: no student OAuth at all, so school restrictions cannot block it. DEPENDENCY-FREE — the RS256 JWT is signed with node `crypto`, so `googleapis` (~50 MB) stays out of package.json. GET returns `{configured}` as a readiness probe; POST takes `{dataUrl, fileName, playerBrand}`, enforces a 15 MB cap, uploads multipart, sets anyone-with-link reader, returns `{link, thumbnail}`. `tsc --noEmit` clean. HOST STEP (Vercel → pflx-darkcampus env): `GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL`, `GOOGLE_SA_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID` — and the folder must be SHARED WITH the service account as Editor or uploads 404.
- **UPLOAD CHAIN (both submit paths):** Supabase Storage → managed Drive endpoint → keep base64 locally as a last resort (never lose a student's evidence), with the >1.2 MB refusal from v1.17 still guarding the row. This means uploads keep working even while Supabase Storage is down.
- Beta guide updated with "Attaching evidence — Drive first" guidance.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean; 11-case Node unit tests (Drive id parsing ×4, thumbnail build, resolver precedence Storage > base64 > Drive link, non-Drive ignored, docs links, empty/null) all PASS; darkcampus `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.19 — INCOMING MESSAGE / CALL ALERTS (July 29, Ennis)
- GAP: the floating X-Bot dock glowed green on unread (`fab.classList.toggle('newmsg')`) but made NO sound and raised NO popup, and an inbound call surfaced only as a bare blocking `confirm()` — a player on another tab never knew either had happened.
- NEW `window.pflxIncomingAlert(kind, who, body)` — rings via `pflxPlaySfx` ('notification' for chat, 'alarm' for a call) and raises a styled banner above the dock: **"NEW MESSAGE" + brand name + preview** (cyan, 7s) or **"INCOMING CALL" + caller + mode** (green, 30s). Click opens the chat dock.
- Wiring: `_pcRefreshBadge` alerts once per NEW message id (`_pcSeenMsgIds`) and never on the first pass after load (`_pcAlertPrimed`), so re-renders and message history cannot spam; suppressed while the chat tab is open. `_pcCallIncomingInvite` fires the call banner BEFORE its confirm, with the confirm deferred 120ms so the banner paints and the sound starts (confirm() freezes rendering).
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean.
- CONTEXT — this is item B of Ennis's DarkCampus↔PFLX identity/reward plan. Remaining: (A) link members properly — only 4 of ~45 are in `dc_member_links`, which is WHY X-Bot cannot credit Kaitlin; (C) Discord/Slack DM reminders (X-Bot posts to channels only today); (D) deadline-aware response fines (only a generic 3-day inactivity rule exists). A/C/D all need Supabase back.
- ACCOUNT LINKING — RECOMMENDED DESIGN (Ennis asked "what is a sure way… a Discord connector?"): fuzzy brand-name matching is why only 4 linked. Ship TWO verified mechanisms: (1) **Discord OAuth2 `identify` connector** — one click, no bot scopes, and critically Discord accounts are PERSONAL so a school Workspace admin cannot block it the way they can Google; Slack equivalent is Sign in with Slack (OIDC). (2) **One-time link code** — PFLX shows a code, the student types `/link CODE` in Discord/Slack, X-Bot reads the author id from the message and links it: verified, needs NO OAuth app, works today, same flow for both platforms. FORCE IT with a blocking "Link your accounts to continue" modal on DarkCampus entry (players only, hosts skip), a PFLX dashboard nag, and a Beta onboarding task.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.14 — VERIFIED ACCOUNT LINKING (July 29, Ennis-approved)
- WHY: v1.13's fuzzy brand-name automatch linked only 4 of ~45 members. That single gap blocks FOUR approved features — X-Bot crediting outstanding interns (Kaitlin), bridged @mentions that actually ping, DM reminders, and per-cohort channel gating. Linking is the keystone; it was built first by agreement.
- NEW `/api/link-account` (pflx-darkcampus `beaed54`), writing into the SAME `dc_member_links` registry v1.13 already reads, with merge-not-replace upserts:
  · `issue_code` — mints a 5-char code (ambiguity-free alphabet, no O/0/I/1), 30-min TTL, one live code per player.
  · `claim_code` — the scanner calls this when it sees the code; the platform payload supplies the AUTHOR id, so the link is VERIFIED (the member proved control) rather than guessed. Works identically for Slack.
  · `discord_oauth` — `identify` scope ONLY, no bot permissions. Chosen because Discord accounts are PERSONAL, so a school Workspace admin cannot block it the way Google OAuth is blocked (the class of failure behind Aadhya's missing writes). Needs DISCORD_CLIENT_ID / DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET / DISCORD_REDIRECT_URI.
  · `manual_link` — host override.
  · GET `?playerId=` — link state + `oauthReady`, for the blocking "link to continue" modal.
- `xbot-scan.ts`: `detectLinkCode()` + `LINK_CODE_RE` spot "/link CODE", "link CODE" or a bare code while ignoring ordinary chat ("here is a link to my work" does NOT match). 6-case logic test PASS; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- HOST DECISIONS (July 29): **PFLX avatar is always canonical** — Discord/Slack avatars are deliberately NOT imported even though OAuth could supply them. **Default network = PFLX Darkcampus Discord/Slack.** **AUTO-AWARD and AUTO-TAX are ON** — X-Bot grants communication badges and applies fines without waiting for host approval.
- ⚠️ AUTO-TAX RISK, flagged and accepted: automatic deduction means a regex false-positive costs a student real currency with no human in the loop. RECOMMENDED RAILS before enabling in production (not yet built): per-player daily fine cap, an X-Bot message stating the reason and how to appeal, a host reversal action with audit trail, and a shadow-mode dry run (log what WOULD be fined for 48h) before it goes live. Auto-AWARD carries far less risk and can go first.
- REMAINING in the approved sequence: blocking link modal on DarkCampus entry + PFLX nag · @mention autocomplete with bridged pings (`<@id>` / `<@U…>`, needs links) · Project chat → Project channel routing (default PFLX Darkcampus) · Virtual Theater multi-source curated queue (YouTube backbone; LinkedIn/Instagram/TikTok cannot supply automated feeds — LinkedIn is identity + company-page posting only).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.20 — SPEC ITEM 1: APPROVE-ALL LABELLING + CONFIRM + UNDO (July 29, Ennis)
- REPORTED as data loss ("approved one user's submission, all disappeared"). INVESTIGATED FIRST: **no data was lost.** All 49 submissions intact; the three onboarding tasks read 13/13, 15/15, 14/14 approved; balances correct with no double payment (KAITLIN/BIJO/RUM each 50 XC from the Discord task).
- REAL CAUSE — mine: PLATFORM v1.14 made the task-level ✓ Approve delegate to the per-player pipeline, approving EVERY pending entry on that task. On a 15-person task that empties the pending list in one click. Correct behaviour, alarming presentation, unlabelled.
- FIX: (1) the button now reads **"✓ Approve all N pending"** whenever N>1; (2) batches of 4+ raise a confirm naming up to 8 players, stating the per-player XC, and pointing at the per-player ✓ chip for single approvals; (3) every batch is journalled to `window._mcLastApprovalBatch`; (4) new **`pflxUndoApprovals()`** reverses the last batch — entries back to 'pending', task completion flag recomputed, and XC clawed back through the SAME PflxDataBus path that paid it so every surface and the ledger stay consistent. Badges are deliberately NOT revoked (removing an earned badge is a host decision). The success toast tells the host how to undo.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean; 4-case label test (batch label, single, mixed statuses counting only pending, none-pending) PASS.
- SPEC: full communication/integration spec written to `PFLX Apps/PFLX_COMMS_SPEC_v1.md` — token grammar (@ # ! + $ % ^ /), account linking as foundation, shortcut XC/badge requests, tag→PFLX-DM→deep-link loop, branded reactions/polls/event confirmations, MC→Project channel routing, GitHub, broadcast queue, auto-tax rails, 11-item build order, and the platform constraints (LinkedIn/Instagram/TikTok cannot supply automated feeds; YouTube is the backbone).

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.15 — SPEC ITEM 2: LINK ENFORCEMENT (Aug 9, Ennis-approved)
- SYMPTOM: linking stuck at 4 of ~45 members since v1.14. Read as an adoption problem — it was not.
- ROOT CAUSE: **`detectLinkCode()` was never called.** v1.14 shipped the detector in `xbot-scan.ts` and the `claim_code` action in `/api/link-account`, but nothing wired them together. A member could type `/link ABC12` in Discord and the code would sit unclaimed until its 30-min TTL expired, with no error and no reply. The primary linking mechanism has been dead since the day it shipped.
- FIX (pflx-darkcampus `b1cbe7c`):
  · `api/xbot-scan`: claims link codes inside the comms-channel loop using Discord's `author.id` (verified by the platform, not typed by the member), logs to `autoHandled`, never gates to a host, and `continue`s so a code is not also scanned as conversation. Added `author.id` to `RawMessage`. Fires only in the 11 `COMMS_CHANNELS`, so the gate copy names **#general-chat** rather than promising "any channel".
  · NEW `components/LinkGate.tsx`: blocking entry modal for players, hosts never gated. Issues a code, polls `GET /api/link-account` every 5s, self-dismisses on claim. Copy states plainly that only the account id is read and the PFLX avatar/brand are untouched.
  · NEW `api/link-account/discord/start` + `/callback`: keeps `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID` server-side (the client never sees it), `identify` scope, `state = base64url(playerId|returnUri)`. Dormant until the env vars are set — verified live returning 503, and the button stays hidden via `oauthReady`.
  · `MembersPanel`: link-coverage bar — linked/total, %, and "N member(s) invisible to X-Bot", colour-stepped at 40/80%.
- ID-SPACE BUG found while wiring: `dc_member_links` is keyed on the roster id, but `dc_auth` frequently carries a synthetic one — the SSO fast path mints `sso-<brand>` (`page.tsx`) and the iframe adopt path mints `platform-<timestamp>` (`PflxBridge`). Gating on those would have nagged members who ARE linked. `linkPlayerId` now resolves the canonical id from `/api/players` by normalised brand and returns "" for an unresolved synthetic id (no gate rather than a wrong gate). `GET /api/link-account` also accepts `?brand=` as a fallback — verified live: `?brand=Kaitlin` resolves to `player-import-1784088654295-23`, linked true.
- SCHEMA MISMATCH fixed: `link-account` wrote `brand`, the host MembersPanel and automatch read `brandName`, so code-claimed rows would have shown a blank name in the host table. `upsertLink()` now keeps both spellings in sync, stamps `updatedAt`, and **strips undefined/empty keys from the patch** — previously spreading `{brand: undefined}` over an existing row could blank a field the host had set by hand.
- ESCAPE HATCH — deliberate, flagged to Ennis before push and approved. The spec said "blocking"; it blocks, but after 15s offers "Continue unlinked for now" → session-only skip + persistent amber warning strip + `dc_link_skip_count` in localStorage. A failed `/api/link-account` fetch is likewise treated as linked. REASONING: a hard block with no exit means one broken scanner locks ~45 interns out of their comms platform mid-programme — and the scanner is precisely the component that was found to have never been wired up. Revisit once coverage is high.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on all touched files (remaining warnings in `terminal/page.tsx` are pre-existing). Live: `/api/link-account` → `{"oauthReady":false,"total":4,"linked":4}`; `/discord/start` → 503 (route deployed, unconfigured); `/discord/callback` → 307. NOTE: `next build` cannot run in the Cowork sandbox — `node_modules` holds the macOS-arm64 `lightningcss` binary, unusable on linux-arm64. Not a code fault; Vercel builds from a clean install.
- HOST ACTIONS: (1) set `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID` / `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET` in Vercel → pflx-darkcampus to switch on one-click OAuth linking (redirect URI `https://pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app/api/link-account/discord/callback`); (2) tell testers to post their code in **#general-chat** — other channels are not scanned; (3) watch the coverage bar in Host Settings → Members. Coverage is the gate on spec items 3, 4, 6, 8 and 11.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.16 — SPEC ITEM 3: BRIDGED @ AND # MENTIONS (Aug 9, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: the @/# autocomplete pickers had existed since v1.13 and looked like they worked, but a mention meant NOTHING once it crossed the bridge. `@KAITLIN` was relayed to Discord as the literal string "@KAITLIN" and pinged nobody. Members believed they had tagged a teammate; the teammate never heard about it.
- ROOT CAUSE: `fanOut()` sent ONE string to every target. Discord and Slack ping syntax are mutually unreadable (`<@1234>` vs `<@U04AB>`, `<#5678>` vs `<#C04AB|name>`), so a single message body physically cannot serve both targets of the same channel. Nothing ever translated the display form into either.
- FIX (pflx-darkcampus `1b3636f`):
  · NEW `lib/mentions.ts` — `buildMentionIndex()` + `renderForTarget(text, platform, index)`. Discord `<@id>`/`<#id>`; Slack `<@U…>`/`<#C…|name>` plus `<!here>`/`<!everyone>` (Discord takes the literal). Returns `{ text, pinged[], unlinked[] }`.
  · `fanOut()` gained an optional per-target `render` callback; omit it and behaviour is byte-identical to before. The send route now renders once PER DESTINATION.
  · `/api/players` reports `linked` per member, matched on id OR normalised brand — necessary because the v1.13 automatch, the v1.14 code claim and the host panel do not agree on which field holds the name (`brandName` vs `brand`).
  · `MentionInput`: `@everyone`/`@here` pinned to the top of the picker; an unlinked member is labelled **"not linked — won't ping on Discord/Slack"** at the moment of selection, so the member learns before they send rather than never.
  · X-Bot posts a link nudge when a mention resolved to nobody — ONCE per brand, ledgered in `dc_link_nudges`, or every thread becomes a wall of bot notices.
- MATCHING DECISIONS worth keeping: longest-brand-first, so "@Global Digital" is not swallowed by a shorter "@Global"; brand names are regex-escaped, so "C++ Club" does not compile into a broken pattern; the leading-boundary guard leaves `ennis@KAITLIN.org` untouched; already-rendered `<@111>` is idempotent under a second pass.
- UNLINKED MEMBERS degrade to plain readable text rather than `<@undefined>`. This is the direct payoff of v1.15 — and the reason coverage is the gate on everything downstream.
- Verified: 22-case unit test on the extracted resolver, ALL PASS (both platforms, prefix trap, regex-hostile brand, email, channels with/without a target on that platform, broadcasts, mixed message, case-insensitivity, idempotence, unlinked/pinged lists). `tsc --noEmit` clean. eslint introduces no new findings — MentionInput's 13 React Compiler errors are pre-existing and unchanged (verified by stashing the file and re-running: same 13). Live: `/api/players` now carries `linked`, and the 4 known links resolve to CALLIA, FATHIMA, KABIR, KAITLIN.
- ⚠️ ROSTER OBSERVATION, not fixed, flagged for Ennis: `/api/players` returns **137 members** (135 player, 2 admin) against ~45 expected beta interns. Two duplicate brand names remain — `NEUROFLUX` ×2 and a literal placeholder `BRANDNAME?` ×2. The July 19 dedupe merged 10 accounts; this is a different and larger population, likely accumulated imports. Worth an audit before coverage percentages are read as meaningful — 4/137 and 4/45 tell very different stories.
- NEXT in the build order: item 5 (shortcut XC/badge requests, no dependencies) or item 4 (PFLX tag → DM → deep link, depends on linking coverage).

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.17 — SPEC ITEM 4: TAG → PFLX-CHAT DM → DEEP LINK (Aug 9, Ennis)
- GOAL (spec §5): being tagged should reach the person, then walk them back to the exact message.
- FIX (pflx-darkcampus `5726475`):
  · NEW `lib/xbotDm.ts` — `dmTaggedPlayers()` writes an X-Bot DM into `pflx_chat_threads` carrying the message, the author, the channel and a deep link. Finds-or-creates the X-Bot↔member DM thread; read-modify-write touches ONLY that thread, so a concurrent writer elsewhere in the array is not clobbered (persistence guardrail). The source message id is stored on the DM, so a re-scan cannot DM the same person twice.
  · DELIBERATELY PFLX Chat, not a Discord DM — it needs no account link, so the UNLINKED member (the one most likely to miss things) still hears about it, and the DM itself carries the prompt to link. This is the one bridge feature that works at today's 4/137 coverage.
  · `send` route: DMs everyone tagged in a DarkCampus post, resolved against the full ROSTER rather than the link table, so unlinked members are included.
  · `xbot-scan`: the inbound direction. Discord sends mentions as `<@id>`, so this is the reverse lookup — platform id → `dc_member_links` → PFLX player. Only linked members are reachable this way, because Discord cannot address an account it does not know.
  · `terminal/page.tsx` honours `/terminal?channel=…&message=…`, selects the channel, hands the id to `MessageFeed`, and clears the query string so a refresh does not re-jump. `MessageFeed` scrolls to the message and flashes it; the deep link deliberately beats the usual jump-to-bottom.
- BUG FOUND BY THE TESTS, not in production: `matchedBrands()` double-matched a brand that is a prefix of a longer one — "@Global Digital" also matched "@Global", which would have DM'd the wrong player. `renderForTarget` was immune because it rewrites the text as it goes; `matchedBrands` now consumes each hit for the same reason.
- Verified: 12-case DM/mention suite ALL PASS (unlinked included, prefix trap, email, playerId carried, Discord `<@id>` and `<@!id>` forms, `<@&role>` ignored); the 22-case item-3 suite re-run and still ALL PASS. `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint no new findings. Live: `/terminal?channel=…&message=…` → 200.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.27 / v1.28 — ROSTER SYNC HARDENING (Aug 9, Ennis)
- WHY: the NEUROFLUX merge reverted TWICE in production. Cause: TWO roster write paths, only one guarded. `mcCloudPush` → `pflx_mc_players` goes through `_mcMergeQueueWithCloud` (read-merge-write, July) and held correctly; `mcCloudSync` → legacy **`users`** row never got that treatment and posts `mcPlayers` WHOLESALE through the X-Coin iframe. Proof: ten legacy keys (`users`, `checkpoints`, `projects`, `seasons`, `startupStudios`, `cohortGroups`, `sessions`, `jobs`, `pflxRanks`, `projectPitches`) rewritten inside a 0.7s burst, twice, each time undoing the merge.
- v1.27 (`104edeb`): `mcCloudSync` now read-merge-writes the roster — reads the current `users` row and merges via `_mcMergePlayers` before posting; on a cloud read failure it sends local rather than dropping the edit. `_mcMergePlayers` now refuses TOMBSTONED incoming records — tombstones existed since July 15 but this merge path never consulted them, so a stale device re-added deleted players on its next sync. Shrink/empty guards could not catch it because resurrection GROWS the array.
- v1.28 (`66ccdd3`): per-record RECENCY tiebreak. v1.27 held the NEUROFLUX merge and the 101,950 balance through a live sync, but ARYANA/KIYAN reverted to "BrandName?" on that same sync — `_mcMergePlayers` chose its winner by lifetime XC then activity length, so two copies with IDENTICAL totals fell through to "keep local", i.e. the stale tab. A newer per-record `updatedAt` now wins outright (stamped beats unstamped); the earnings-safety pass still runs regardless of who wins, so recency can never cost coins or badges.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean on both; 15-case unit test against the LIVE extracted `_mcMergePlayers` ALL PASS (resurrection refused, balance preserved, higher lifetime XC wins, badges union-never-shrink, incoming-only filtering, tiebreak both directions, stamped-vs-unstamped, recency does not destroy XC or badges). PFLX_PATCH 26 → 28, build 2026.08.
- ⚠️ Brand renames only stick once a client RELOADS onto patch 28 — an old tab has no recency logic.

## INVESTIGATION — "APPROVALS DISAPPEAR WHEN I APPROVE 1" (Aug 9) — NO DATA LOSS, CAUSE NOT YET PROVEN
- Audited every task carrying submissions. **Nothing is missing**: 42 approved + 11 pending across 10 tasks; zero submissions with a null `status` or null `playerId`. The three Alpha tasks read 15/15, 14/14, 13/13 approved.

The host card correctly reads "IN PROGRESS · ✓ n/42".

A host approves, then a tab holding pre-approval `pflx_mc_tasks` pushes it back. `_mcMergeTasks` merges submissions newest-wins, so an entry carrying NO timestamp could beat a stamped one. ## DATA — 15 MB TASKS ROW MIGRATED TO STORAGE (Aug 9) — ROOT CAUSE OF "MISSION CONTROL IS NOT PERSISTENT"
- THE ACTUAL FAULT, found after the pointer backfill did not change the UI: `mcRenderTasks()` renders from **localStorage**, which is filled by the boot cloud pull — and `pflx_mc_tasks` was **15.94 MB, essentially all of it base64 inside 31 uploads**. That pull was failing/timing out in the browser, so the Console silently fell back to a stale localStorage copy holding only the 3 Alpha tasks. Everything the testers reported follows from that one fact: no Beta tasks in the host dash, "not persistent", old/deleted tasks reappearing, Approvals reading 0 while the header read 3, and approvals not sticking (a client that cannot read the row cannot reliably write it).
- The cloud data was CORRECT throughout — verified 20 tasks / 17 with checkpointId in both the canonical and legacy rows, preserved even through a live client push. The database was never the problem; loading it was.
- ACTIONS (Ennis: "DO A … you can do it so I dont mess it up"):
  · Created Storage bucket `pflx-submissions` (public, 15 MB file cap) via SQL.
  · Migration `pflx_submissions_bucket_policies`: public SELECT + anon INSERT/UPDATE on `storage.objects`, scoped to that bucket only.
  · Ran `pflx-migrate-uploads.sh` dry-run, then `--apply`.
- RESULT: **31 uploads moved, 0 failed. Row 15.94 MB → 78 kB (a 204× reduction).** 20 tasks, 17 with checkpoints, all 51 submissions intact, 23 now carrying `fileUrl`, 31 objects in the bucket. Write-back HTTP 204. A public object URL verified live: HTTP 200, 497,043 bytes.
- BACKUPS: `/Users/macbookpro/Documents/pflx_tasks_backup_20260809-212939.json` (full pre-migration row, host machine) plus `backup_tasks_fix_20260809_pflx_mc_tasks` in `app_data`.
- ⚠️ ONE LEFTOVER, harmless: MARIQUE's submission on "Download and Install Discord" still holds a `fileData` of **182 characters** — a truncated/corrupt PNG, far too short to be a real image. The script correctly skipped it. Worth asking her to re-upload rather than "restoring" it.
- WHY THIS KEPT COMING BACK: this is the same row identified on July 29. The v1.17 migration was written then and never ran because the bucket did not exist; the row grew from 19 MB → shrank → regrew to 15.94 MB in the meantime. It is now structurally incapable of regrowing, because uploads route to Storage first (v1.17 chain: Storage → managed Drive → base64, with >1.2 MB refused).

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.18 — SPEC ITEM 5: /xc AND /badge SHORTCUT REQUESTS (Aug 9, Ennis)

(2) multi-word brands truncated silently — a mention inside a command is now explicitly ONE token, with roster resolution done by the caller where the authoritative brand list lives. `@Global Digital nice work` is genuinely ambiguous without the roster; documenting that beat guessing.

- FIX (pflx-darkcampus `6ef92d3`): NEW `lib/engagement.ts`. Three primitives sharing one problem — PFLX has concepts Discord and Slack do not — so each DEGRADES rather than breaks.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.30 — SOUND ENGINE, LOGIN MUSIC, BADGES, XC STEPPER, TICKER RE-POLL (Aug 9, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: five separate reports surfaced today via live Discord player/host complaints (screenshots) and an uploaded login-music track: (1) Sound Engine's Per-Tab Audio / SFX Library / Track Library sections rendered empty after opening the Sound tab. (2) No way to apply one song to multiple pages at once — testers had to set each page's dropdown individually. (3) Login-screen music silently failed to play. (4) Edit Player showed badges as the generic word "Badge" instead of the badge's real name. (5) Edit Player's XC field required typing a raw number, no quick +/− control.
- ROOT CAUSE:
  · Sound Engine: `buildAdvancedSoundPanel()` rebuilt the panel HTML on every open but never re-invoked the render functions for the three list sections afterward — a timing/ordering bug, not a data bug.
  · Apply-to-multiple: never built — Per-Tab Audio only ever supported one page at a time.
  · Login music: `sePlayLoginMusic()` called `.play()` directly; browsers block autoplay-with-sound until a user gesture, and the resulting promise rejection was silently swallowed with no retry.
  · Badges: PFLX stores a player's badges two ways — full record objects, and plain ids awarded automatically via task/checkpoint completion. `renderBadgeListHtml` only handled the object shape, so id-only badges fell through to a hardcoded "Badge" placeholder.
  · XC field: was a bare `<input type="number">` — functional but slow for hosts adjusting XC live during a session.
- FIX (`c57b454`, `88ce657`):
  · Sound Engine: after `panel.innerHTML = html`, added calls to `seRenderTabTracks()`, `seRenderSFXList()`, `seRenderTrackLibrary()` (each guarded with `typeof` + try/catch) so the three sections always populate on open.
  · Apply-to-multiple: new checkbox + apply bar in the Per-Tab Audio card; `seRenderTabTracks()` renders a per-row `.se-tab-apply-check` when `SE.applyMultipleMode` is on; new `window.seToggleApplyMultiple` / `window.seApplyToMultiple`.
  · Login music: `sePlayLoginMusic()` now catches the rejected `play()` and arms a one-time click/keydown/touchstart listener (`seArmLoginMusicGestureRetry()`) that retries playback on the user's first interaction, then self-disarms (`seDisarmLoginMusicGestureRetry()`); `seStopLoginMusic()` also disarms it so it can never fire after login.
  · Badges: new `pmBadgeNormalize()` / `pmBadgeIdToName()` helpers; `renderBadgeListHtml` now maps every badge through `pmBadgeNormalize` before rendering, so both shapes resolve to a real name.
  · XC stepper: new `xcStepperFld()` / `wireXcStepper()` replace the raw number input in Edit Player with −10/−1/+1/+10 buttons; wired alongside the modal's other field wiring.
  · Also in this patch: the bottom ticker now re-polls each sub-app 600ms after that app's iframe fires `load` (in addition to the existing 60s interval), so a slow-loading X-Coin/Arena/DarkCampus/Pathway frame doesn't miss its first poll.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean on the patched file. No per-function unit harness run for these UI fixes this pass (unlike the July/Aug data-merge patches) — deferred to live tester feedback in #system-updates.
- PFLX_PATCH 29 → 30, build 2026.08.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.20 — X-COIN FEED TICKER SILENT: TWO INDEPENDENT ROOT CAUSES (Aug 9, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: reported as one complaint — "X-Coin Feed is not updating the bottom ticker or the X-Coin feed channel in DarkCampus/Discord/Slack" — but two unrelated bugs in two separate repos, each hiding the other.
- ROOT CAUSE 1 (pflx-xcoin-app): the platform shell polls every sub-app iframe with `{type:'pflx_ticker_request'}` and expects `{type:'pflx_ticker_events', source:'xcoin', events:[...]}` back. X-Coin's `PflxBridge.tsx` never implemented that handler — `buildTickerEvents()` existed but was module-private and nothing wired it to the bridge, so the shell's request went unanswered and the bottom ticker never showed X-Coin activity.
- ROOT CAUSE 2 (pflx-darkcampus): the badge→Discord/Slack feed sync ran ONLY from a client-side `setInterval` inside the terminal page component. With no server-side cron, the sync silently stopped the moment nobody had that browser tab open — which is most of the time.
- FIX 1 (pflx-xcoin-app `62abe8b`): exported `buildTickerEvents` from `Ticker.tsx`; added a `pflx_ticker_request` handler in `PflxBridge.tsx`'s `handleMessage()` that builds the events and posts `pflx_ticker_events` back to `window.parent`.
- FIX 2 (pflx-darkcampus `dc62953`): `badge-feed/route.ts` GET handler now checks `?cron=1` first and, if present, runs `syncFromLedger()` server-side and returns early (existing `?id=` share-page and default-latest-50 behavior unchanged for normal callers); marked `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` so Vercel can't statically cache the route (the same class of bug the X-Coin app itself hit and fixed previously); added a third Vercel Cron entry (`vercel.json`) hitting `/api/badge-feed?cron=1` every 10 minutes.
- Verified: X-Coin fix — `node --experimental-strip-types` confirmed `PflxBridge.tsx` type-strips clean (only unresolved `react` import, no syntax errors); deployed, Vercel `dpl_tjNausky9GGSMYweYFVuoTotJaUN` READY. DarkCampus fix — real `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` via osascript, exit code 0; deployed, Vercel `dpl_HBGaW3ousWvp6FUEFzsh1F7L6KQY` READY; live-verified `curl https://pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app/api/badge-feed?cron=1` → `{"success":true,"posted":0,"bridgedTo":[]}`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — both fixes are live and self-sustaining (the cron no longer depends on any browser tab being open).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.31 — LOGIN BRAND FIELD CRASHED ON EVERY KEYSTROKE, DESKTOP ONLY (Aug 9–10, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: PFLX Error Log overlay showed `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'innerHTML')` firing once per character typed ("x3" after typing "THE") in the login screen's "Select Your Brand" field. The native dropdown still opened and filtered correctly — the crash was silent to a player, visible only via the error-log overlay/console.
- ROOT CAUSE: the v1.11 touch brand picker (July 25) attached its `input` listener to `#brand-select` UNCONDITIONALLY, before checking `isTouch`, and that listener called `renderSuggest()` on every keystroke regardless of device. But `renderSuggest()`'s `box` element (the custom suggestion dropdown) is only ever created further down, inside the touch-only branch, after `if (!isTouch) return;`. On a non-touch device that branch never runs, so `box` stays `undefined` forever — yet the listener still called `renderSuggest()`, which immediately does `box.innerHTML = ''` and throws. Confirmed by running the exact extracted block in Node with `isTouch=false`: reproduces the identical `TypeError` on the first keystroke; with `isTouch=true`, no error and the suggestion box is created as designed.
- FIX (`0b8bfb9`): moved the `isTouch` computation above the listener registration and gated the `renderSuggest()` call on it (`if (isTouch && typeof renderSuggest === 'function') renderSuggest();`). Desktop keeps its existing live-uppercase behavior and the native `<datalist>` dropdown untouched; only the crash-prone call is now skipped on non-touch devices.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean. 2-case unit test against the LIVE extracted v1.11 block (sed-extracted, not reimplemented) in a mocked-DOM Node harness: desktop/non-touch — no throw, suggest box never created (matches native-datalist-only design); touch — no throw, suggest box created and populated. Same harness run against the PRE-FIX block first, to confirm it reproduces the reported crash exactly (desktop throws `Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'innerHTML')` on keystroke 1) — proves the fix targets the actual reported bug, not a lookalike.
- PFLX_PATCH 30 → 31, build 2026.08.
- NOTE: the screenshot's reported line number (18464) didn't match this file's line for the throwing statement (`box.innerHTML=''`, line 18484) — the tester's browser tab was almost certainly still on an earlier cached build from before several of today's patches landed (footer read "PATCH 29"), not a different bug. The crash signature, the field, and the "x3" keystroke count all match this root cause exactly, and the reproduction above confirms it independent of the line-number discrepancy.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.32 — MOBILE PASS 1: HOME BASE CROWDING (Aug 10, Ennis)
- CONTEXT: Ennis asked for a general mobile-optimization pass ("needs a lot of work"), scoped via follow-up to layout/crowding + touch interactions on the player-facing app, with no specific tester reports yet — his own read of the platform. Rather than guess blind across a 64K-line file, audited live at phone width first: injected a same-origin iframe at 386×844 (the sandbox's actual browser window would not resize below desktop size, so a same-origin iframe was used to get a true narrow viewport) into a fresh page over prototypeflx.com, then measured real DOM overflow instead of eyeballing screenshots alone. Logged in via the CodeCrafter host test account to reach Home Base.
- SYMPTOM: on a phone-width viewport, the Home Base profile card showed the player's name and brand line hard-clipped mid-word ("CODECRAFT…", "instructor · Global Digital Inte…") with no wrap and no ellipsis; the Launch Apps card grid rendered a 2-up layout that ran off the right edge of the screen (app tiles cut off, only the first fully visible); and the "Roster synced" toast notification rendered on top of the top toolbar's icon buttons for its whole visible duration.
- ROOT CAUSE: three instances of the same CSS mechanism — CSS Grid/Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, meaning they refuse to shrink below their own content's intrinsic width even when their track/container is narrower. `.player-header` (`grid-template-columns: 110px 1fr`) never got a phone breakpoint, so its `1fr` identity column stayed pinned to the player-name text's full unwrapped width (247px) instead of letting the name wrap. `#home-app-hub-grid` (`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px,1fr))`, set via inline style in JS) computed 2 columns at ~390px viewport width and its buttons carried the same min-width:auto floor, so even forcing 1 column with `!important` wasn't enough on its own — the surrounding `.dashboard-card` and the tile `<button>` itself both had to be freed to shrink too. The toast bug was unrelated: `.pflx-toast` is `position:fixed; top:20px` with no awareness of the 64px-tall toolbar sitting above it at a lower z-index.
- FIX (`3279c95`): new `@media (max-width: 480px)` block (grouped with the platform's existing 768px/1024px responsive rules) — `.player-header` stacks to a single centered column, avatar shrinks 110→84px, `.player-name` drops to 20px with `overflow-wrap`/`word-break`; `.player-identity`, `.dashboard-card`, and `#home-app-hub-grid > button` all get `min-width: 0` to remove the shrink floor; `#home-app-hub-grid` forced to `grid-template-columns: 1fr !important` (the only way to override its inline style without touching the JS that sets it); `.pflx-toast` repositioned to `top: 72px` with `left/right: 12px` (full-width, 8px clear of the toolbar) instead of a fixed top-right 220px box.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean. Every rule was verified LIVE before shipping, not just reasoned about — injected the exact CSS as a `<style>` tag into the mobile-width iframe against the running production page, re-measured `getBoundingClientRect()` on the real elements after each change, and confirmed by iteration: first pass fixed the header but left `.dashboard-card` still overflowing (506→494px, still short of the 386px viewport) because the `min-width:auto` floor existed at TWO more nesting levels than first assumed; added `.dashboard-card`/button `min-width:0` and re-measured clean (`dashboardCard.fits: true`, `appGrid` collapsed to a real single column). Toast fix verified the same way — fired a live toast post-fix and confirmed `toolbarBottom (64) < toastTop (72)`, no overlap. Screenshots taken before/after at each step.
- SCOPE: this is pass 1 of the requested mobile work, covering Home Base only. NOT yet audited: X-Coin, DarkCampus, Pathway Portal (separate repos/apps), Mission Control host screens, or Sound Engine — all still open per Ennis's stated "everything" scope. ## PATCH PLATFORM v1.33 — MOBILE PASS 2: MISSION CONTROL SIDEBAR (Aug 10, Ennis)
- CONTEXT: continuing the "full mobile hardening pass" Ennis asked for after v1.32 ("Both — full mobile hardening pass", "Everything, screen by screen", "Just review the code" — explicitly code-review-driven, not waiting on tester reports). Grepped `.mc-layout`/`.mc-sidebar` and every `sidebar-toggle`/`hamburger`/`drawer`-style name across the file first — zero matches — confirming Mission Control had no mobile handling and no existing collapse mechanism to extend, unlike the Home Base fix which was pure CSS. Confirmed severity live before designing anything: same same-origin-iframe technique from v1.32 (386×844 over prototypeflx.com, logged in as CodeCrafter host), navigated into Mission Control via `navigateTo('mission-control')`.
- SYMPTOM: `.mc-sidebar` is a permanently-fixed 230px column (180px under the existing 1024px tablet breakpoint) with NO phone breakpoint at all. At a 386px-wide viewport this left `.mc-content` only ~200px, and `.mc-stat-grid`'s stat cards still didn't fit inside that — measured `contentEl.scrollWidth: 306` vs `clientWidth: 200`, `statGrid.scrollWidth: 278` vs `clientWidth: 144` — the dashboard stat cards (players/checkpoints/tasks/approvals) were clipped and needed horizontal scrolling to read, with the sidebar's branding block alone consuming most of the visible screen.
- ROOT CAUSE: `.mc-sidebar` was designed once, for desktop, and never revisited — no `@media` rule below 1024px beyond the 180px tablet shrink, and (per the grep above) no toggle/drawer pattern anywhere in the codebase to reuse.
- FIX (`ee9bb03`): built Mission Control's first off-canvas sidebar drawer. New `@media (max-width: 768px)` block: `.mc-sidebar` becomes `position: fixed`, slid off-screen via `transform: translateX(-100%)` with a `0.25s` transition; a new hamburger button (`.mc-mobile-sidebar-toggle`, top-left, phones only) and a dimmed `.mc-sidebar-backdrop` were added to the Mission Control view's markup; `.mc-content` gets `width: 100%` so it no longer shares space with the sidebar; `.mc-stat-grid` forced to 2 columns and `.mc-table` made horizontally scrollable at this width (matches the existing tablet-width stat-grid pattern). New JS `window.mcToggleMobileSidebar(forceOpen)` toggles a `mc-sidebar-open` class that both the sidebar-transform and backdrop-visibility rules key off of; a delegated click listener auto-closes the drawer when any `.mc-nav-btn` is tapped, without touching `mcNav()`'s own tab-switching/rendering logic at all.
- BUG CAUGHT LIVE BEFORE SHIPPING: first draft put the open/closed class on `.mc-layout`, matching the CSS as `.mc-layout.mc-sidebar-open .mc-sidebar-backdrop`. Live-injected onto the running page, the sidebar itself opened correctly but the backdrop never appeared — `getComputedStyle` showed `display:none` no matter what. Root cause: the hamburger button and backdrop are DOM *siblings* of `.mc-layout` (inserted just before it in the markup), not descendants, so a `.mc-layout.mc-sidebar-open .mc-sidebar-backdrop` descendant selector could never match. Fixed by moving the toggled class to `.mission-control-view` — the shared ancestor of the toggle button, backdrop, and `.mc-layout` alike — and updating both the CSS selectors and `mcToggleMobileSidebar()` to target it. Also added an explicit `height: auto` to the drawer's `.mc-sidebar` rule (the base rule's `height: 100%` would otherwise fight the fixed-position `top`/`bottom` offsets).
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean. Verified live against the running production page (not just reasoned about) for both states: CLOSED — `.mc-content` renders full-width (384px) with `scrollWidth === clientWidth` (no overflow) and `.mc-stat-grid` fits its 2-up layout (346===346); OPEN — sidebar slides to `x:0`, backdrop covers the full viewport (`384×774`, `display:block`), confirmed via `getBoundingClientRect()`/`getComputedStyle()` plus before/after screenshots of both states. One test-harness-only gotcha hit and worked around: this sandboxed browser's compositor doesn't tick CSS transitions on a background iframe, so `transform` reads as an identity matrix until the stuck transition is force-completed via `Animation.finish()` — confirmed via `element.getAnimations()` showing a permanently `running`, `localTime:0` transition; not a real-browser issue, just an artifact of testing inside a backgrounded iframe.
- SCOPE: pass 2 of the mobile hardening work — Mission Control host screens only. Still open: X-Coin, DarkCampus, Pathway Portal (separate repos), Sound Engine panel.
- PFLX_PATCH 32 → 33, build 2026.08.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.35 — QUICK SETTINGS BADGE/FINE-TAX/PLAYER PICKERS THREW SyntaxError ON EVERY TOGGLE (Aug 10, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis screenshotted the PFLX Error Log firing `Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input (line 1)` the moment he checked a Digital Badge checkbox in the new Quick Task form (Mission Control → Tasks → + New Task → Quick). The checkbox itself still visually toggled (native browser behavior happens before the handler runs), but the chip UI and any downstream state update were unreliable.
- ROOT CAUSE: all four v1.34 shared Quick-form widgets (`mcQL*` links, `mcQBadge*` badges, `mcQFine*` fine/tax, `mcQPlayers*` players) build their `onchange`/`onclick` inline handlers by concatenating `JSON.stringify(scope)` / `JSON.stringify(id)` directly into an HTML attribute string that is ITSELF delimited with double quotes (`onchange="..."`). `JSON.stringify('qtask')` returns the literal text `"qtask"` — quote characters included — so the first `"` it produced closed the `onchange="` attribute early. The browser then parsed the leftover text as bogus extra attributes, and the actual `onchange` attribute value was left truncated to just `mcQBadgeToggle(` (confirmed exactly via a jsdom repro — see Verified). Inline event-handler attributes are compiled into real functions lazily, on first fire, not at render time — so the corruption was invisible until a user actually clicked a checkbox or chip-remove ✕, at which point the browser tried to compile the truncated fragment as a function body and threw `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input` (Chrome's wording for the same defect jsdom reports as `Unexpected token '}'`). This existed in 8 places across the 4 widgets, all built with the same code-generation pattern.
- WHY THE V1.34 TEST SUITE MISSED IT: the 17-case jsdom harness called the widget's `window.mcQ*Toggle(...)` functions directly to verify state/render logic, which is exactly how it should test business logic — but it never went through the actual HTML-attribute-parsing + lazy inline-handler-compilation path a real click triggers, so the malformed-attribute defect was invisible to it. Not a gap in rigor so much as a gap in what that harness was built to catch — needed a second, browser-fidelity-focused test.
- FIX (this patch): wrapped every `JSON.stringify(...)` call used inside an inline `onchange="..."`/`onclick="..."` attribute with `escapeHtml(...)`, so the embedded `"` characters are emitted as `&quot;` (which the HTML parser correctly decodes back to `"` before handing the attribute value to the JS compiler). Fixed all 8 sites: `mcQLUpdate` (label + url oninput), `mcQLRemove`, `mcQBadgeToggle` (checkbox onchange + chip-remove onclick), `mcQFineToggle` (checkbox onchange + chip-remove onclick), `mcQPlayersToggle` (checkbox onchange). No other Quick-form code paths use this JSON.stringify-into-attribute pattern.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean. New jsdom regression test that (unlike the v1.34 suite) sets `runScripts: 'dangerously'` and drives a REAL native checkbox `change` event through jsdom's actual HTML/attribute parser — not a direct function call — for `mcQBadgeToggle`: (1) run against the PRE-FIX code first, confirms the exact reported failure (`rendered onchange attr: mcQBadgeToggle(`, then `SyntaxError` on dispatch) — proves the repro targets the real bug; (2) run against the POST-FIX code, confirms the attribute now round-trips as `onchange="mcQBadgeToggle(&quot;qtask&quot;,&quot;badge-self-directed-player&quot;,this.checked)"`, the change event fires cleanly with no error, and the chip renders `Self Directed Player` correctly.
- PFLX_PATCH 34 → 35, build 2026.08.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.36 — LEGACY-KEY SYNC SILENTLY DROPPED WHENEVER X-COIN PANEL NEVER OPENED (Aug 10, Ennis)
- CONTEXT: while scoping a no-deploy "direct admin bridge" so ad hoc data changes (add a player, approve a submission, flip a setting) don't need a code deploy, found and fixed a real, already-live data-integrity bug in the mechanism connecting Mission Control's canonical `pflx_mc_*` rows to the legacy flat `users`/`tasks`/`checkpoints`/`projects` rows that X-Coin, DarkCampus's `xbot-scan`, and other readers still consume.
- SYMPTOM: this is almost certainly the actual mechanism behind "Approvals reset with old data" (reported earlier this session) and the NEUROFLUX merge that reverted twice (per the `_mcMergePlayers` comment trail, Aug 9) — both previously treated as isolated incidents.
- ROOT CAUSE: `mcCloudSync()` (the function that mirrors MC's collections into the legacy flat Supabase keys) only had one delivery path: `postMessage` into the X-Coin iframe, picked up by `PflxBridge.tsx`'s `pflx_cloud_save` handler, which then calls `saveData()`. That path silently does nothing whenever the X-Coin panel hasn't been opened in the current session — the iframe sits at `src="about:blank"`, `PflxBridge` never mounts, nothing is listening for the message, and there is no queue or retry on the receiving end (`pflx_cloud_save` messages are not queued the way `pflx_data_request` is). No error, no console warning — the legacy rows just go stale while `pflx_mc_*` keeps updating normally, for as long as a host never happens to open X-Coin that session. Separately, even when the message DID land, `PflxBridge.tsx`'s own `saveData()` call is a blind replace, not a merge — so a stale/partial push could still clobber the row outright. Only `'players'`→`'users'` had gotten a read-merge-write fix (Aug 9, via `_mcMergePlayers`), and even that fix still only ever *sent* over the same fragile iframe relay.
- FIX (`preview.html`): `_syncOne()` inside `mcCloudSync()` now writes `users`/`tasks`/`checkpoints`/`projects` **directly to Supabase** via the same `window.pflxSupabase()` client MC already uses for `pflx_mc_*` and tombstones — persistence for these four no longer depends on the X-Coin iframe being loaded at all. Each write is read-merge-write: reads the current cloud row, merges with `_mcMergeTasks`/`_mcMergeById`/`_mcMergePlayers` (extending the existing Aug 9 pattern to checkpoints/tasks/projects, which never had it), then upserts. New `_mcPlayerToXCoinUser()` replicates `PflxBridge.tsx`'s MC-shape→X-Coin-shape mapping (`brand`/`xc` → `brandName`/`xcoin`) inline, since MC now writes `users` itself and nothing else applies that mapping on this path anymore. The iframe postMessage is kept as a best-effort secondary notify (only fired when X-Coin has actually signaled `pflx_store_ready`) so an already-open X-Coin tab still refreshes live — but nothing depends on it landing. Every other `syncMap` key without a merge fn (seasons/jobs/pitches/studios/cohortgroups/pflxranks/sessions) keeps the old relay-only behavior, now gated on `_xcoinStoreReady` with a console warning instead of a silent no-op when the bridge isn't ready.
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean. New Node test extracting the ACTUAL `mcCloudSync`/`_syncOne`/merge-helper code (not a reimplementation) against a mocked Supabase client and iframe, 13 cases: direct Supabase write happens for tasks even with the X-Coin bridge NOT ready; merge keeps both the newer local field AND a cloud-side approval the local copy didn't have; no postMessage sent when the bridge isn't ready (proves persistence no longer depends on the iframe); players write in X-Coin's shape (`xcoin`/`brandName`, not `xc`/`brand`) with `totalXcoin` taking the monotonic-max value; a key with no merge fn (seasons) warns instead of silently dropping when the bridge isn't ready, and still uses the unchanged legacy relay when the bridge IS ready. All 13 PASS.
- HOST NOTE: this does not require any host action — it's a same-shape persistence fix, nothing a tester would see change. Worth quietly watching for whether "reverted" reports stop.
- PFLX_PATCH 35 → 36, build 2026.08.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.37 — JOB FORM CRASHED ON OPEN: escapeAttr WAS NEVER DEFINED (Aug 10, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis screenshotted the PFLX Error Log firing `Uncaught ReferenceError: escapeAttr is not defined (line 40058)` when trying to make a job from the Job Board panel.
- ROOT CAUSE: `mcShowJobForm()` (the New/Edit Job form opener) called `escapeAttr(cp.id)` / `escapeAttr(p.id)` / `escapeAttr(cg.id)` while populating the Checkpoint dropdown, Source Project dropdown, and Cohort checkboxes — `escapeAttr` was never defined anywhere in the file. Every other place in the codebase that escapes a value for an HTML attribute uses `escapeHtml` (which already handles `"` correctly for attribute contexts, per the v1.35 fix this session). This looks like a leftover reference from code written assuming a helper that was never actually added — the very first statement inside the checkpoint-dropdown loop threw, so the form never finished opening no matter which job (new or existing) was being created.
- FIX: replaced all three `escapeAttr(...)` calls with `escapeHtml(...)`, matching the pattern used everywhere else in the file (e.g. the Quick-form player picker's `value="' + escapeHtml(p.id) + '"`).
- Verified: 13-block syntax gate clean; confirmed no remaining `escapeAttr` references anywhere in the file. New Node test against the ACTUAL extracted `mcShowJobForm` function, 10 cases covering both real code paths: opening for a NEW job (idx -1, the exact case that crashed) — no throw, all three dropdowns/checkboxes populate, form becomes visible, and values containing `"`/`&` render HTML-escaped rather than raw; and opening to EDIT an existing job (idx >= 0) — no throw, fields pre-fill, the job's saved cohort renders pre-checked. All 10 PASS.
- PFLX_PATCH 36 → 37, build 2026.08.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.39 — COLLAPSIBLE SIDEBARS ACROSS MISSION CONTROL, X-COIN, DARKCAMPUS (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: Ennis flagged that the fixed left sidebar in every sub-app hurts
  mobile UX badly in portrait ("the App seems to work better in landscape
  on my iPhone") and asked for it to be collapsible with a toggle, freeing
  up viewing room — desktop included, not just mobile.
- SCOPE NOTE: Mission Control already had a <768px off-canvas drawer for
  its sidebar (v1.33, shipped Aug 10, hamburger + backdrop +
  `mcToggleMobileSidebar()`). X-Coin and DarkCampus had NO collapse
  mechanism at all — fixed-width sidebars, zero responsive handling. This
  patch (a) adds a manual DESKTOP/tablet collapse to Mission Control on
  top of its existing phone drawer, and (b) builds the collapse feature
  from scratch for X-Coin and DarkCampus.
- MISSION CONTROL (`preview.html`, PFLX_PATCH 38→39): new
  `.mc-sidebar-collapsed` class on `.mission-control-view` (separate from
  the existing `.mc-sidebar-open` phone-drawer class so the two systems
  never fight), toggled by `window.mcToggleDesktopSidebar(forceCollapsed)`.
  Collapsed → `.mc-sidebar { display:none }`; `.mc-content` is `flex:1` on
  the same `.mc-layout` row so it reclaims the width automatically, no
  extra layout rule needed. A small "‹" button sits on the sidebar's edge
  to collapse; a fixed "☰" button appears top-left to re-expand when
  collapsed. Both are hidden under 768px via `!important` so they never
  double up with the existing phone hamburger/drawer, which keeps owning
  visibility there. Preference persists to `localStorage`
  (`pflx_mc_sidebar_collapsed`) and restores on load.
- X-COIN (`SideNav.tsx`, no dedicated repo version counter — footer says
  "SYS v1.0.0" but isn't bumped per patch): new `sidebarCollapsed` state,
  synced from `localStorage` (`pflx_xcoin_sidebar_collapsed`) in a
  `useEffect` — added AFTER the existing `isEmbed`/`soundOn` hooks and
  BEFORE the `if (isEmbed) return null;` line specifically to respect this
  file's own documented Rules-of-Hooks constraint (a prior bug here was
  exactly "Rendered fewer hooks than expected" from an early return above
  a hook). Collapsed → the component returns just a fixed "☰" button
  instead of the 230px `<nav>`; expanded → the same `<nav>` as before plus
  a small "‹" collapse button on its edge. No `<SideNav/>` caller (10+
  pages) needed touching — the same "return null instead of hiding via CSS"
  trick `isEmbed` already used here works for any flex layout, since the
  node leaves the DOM entirely.
- DARKCAMPUS (`ChannelSidebar.tsx`, only one caller — `terminal/page.tsx`,
  inside a `flex-1 flex` row so the message feed reclaims width for free):
  same pattern — `collapsed` state synced from `localStorage`
