## PATCH PLATFORM v1.40 — COHORT/PLAYER PICKER FRESHNESS + MISSING-PLAYER BACKFILL (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis: "Cohorts are not showing all Cohorts and Players are not showing all players. I have a Player 'Vybe' that is logged into PFLX yet Mission Control is not identifying her profile." Screenshots showed the Quick Task/Project Cohorts checklist missing several real cohort groups (Falcon Studios, Falcon Studios MS, Global Digital Intern, DD Studio 7 were all absent from what should have been a 10-group list) and the Players list missing "Vybe" (brand VYBE, id player-1786104211856-6ryhl) entirely, despite her being logged in.
- ROOT CAUSE (two independent bugs):
  1. **Stale cohort registry, no live refresh.** `mcShowQuickTaskForm`/`mcShowQuickProjectForm` (and the Advanced Task/Project forms) render the Cohorts checkbox list straight from the in-memory `mcCohortGroups` array with zero freshness check at render time. Cohort-group changes made on another host's session only reach a given browser via the initial page load — there was no realtime subscription and no boot-time cloud fetch for the `cohortGroups` row, unlike players. A tab left open across a session drifts arbitrarily stale.
  2. **Two parallel player rosters, only one of which the login/roster-sync system reads.** `PLAYERS` (the identity/login roster) is kept fresh via `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud()` + a realtime subscriber, but BOTH only read/watch individual `pflx_player_<id>` cloud rows. `mcPlayers` (Mission Control's own roster, shown in Player Management, cloud key `pflx_mc_players`) is a separate array. `mcSavePlayerForm()` — the "Add Player" handler inside Player Management — pushed new players into `mcPlayers` only and never called `window.pflxIdentityPersistNewPlayer()`, so a player added there (Vybe's case, confirmed via direct Supabase query: she existed in `pflx_mc_players`/`users` but had no `pflx_player_player-1786104211856-6ryhl` row) was fully visible in Player Management but invisible to the login screen, `_mcRoster()` (which prefers `PLAYERS` whenever non-empty), and therefore every Cohorts/Players picker built on top of it.
  3. Separately confirmed: "Player Pool" and "Season Pass" were already first-class concepts in the permissions layer (`cohort_overrides` keys `PlayerPool`/`SeasonPass`) but were never added as entries in the `cohortGroups` registry that the Cohorts pickers actually read from — so they had no way to appear there even when fresh.
- FIX:
  - `mcSavePlayerForm()` (new-player branch): after pushing to `mcPlayers`, also push into `PLAYERS` (if not already present) and call `pflxIdentityPersistNewPlayer(newPlayer)` so every player added via Player Management gets an individual cloud row going forward.
  - Added `window.pflxFetchCohortGroupsFromCloud()` (mirrors the existing player roster fetch) — pulls the `cohortGroups` row, merges by id, dispatches `pflx-cohorts-updated`. Wired into the same 600ms boot-fetch timer as the player roster pull.
  - Extended the existing realtime roster channel (`pflx-roster`, already subscribed to all of `app_data`) to also branch on `row.key === 'cohortGroups'`, merging live and dispatching `pflx-cohorts-updated` — no new subscription needed.
  - `pflx-cohorts-updated` listener: re-renders any OPEN Quick Task/Quick Project Cohorts checkbox list (preserving whatever the host already has checked) and re-scopes their Players list; also re-renders the Cohort Groups admin panel if it's the active view.
  - `pflx-roster-updated` listener: now also re-renders any open Quick Task/Quick Project Players list (previously only refreshed Player Management views).
  - Added `_mcBackfillMissingPlayerRows()` — a self-guarded, idempotent one-time-per-boot pass that diffs `mcPlayers` against `PLAYERS` and, for anyone present in the former but missing from the latter, pushes them into `PLAYERS` and calls `pflxIdentityPersistNewPlayer()`. Triggered 4s after boot and again (debounced, self-guarded) at the tail of every `mcLoadData()` call, so it retries safely if `mcPlayers` wasn't populated yet at the first attempt. This is a permanent safety net against future drift between the two rosters, independent of the `mcSavePlayerForm` fix above.
- DATA (Supabase surgery, single transaction each, verified after):
  - Backfilled Vybe's individual row: inserted `pflx_player_player-1786104211856-6ryhl` from her existing `pflx_mc_players` record (on conflict do update). Verified via SELECT — row now exists, brand VYBE.
  - Added two new entries to the `cohortGroups` key (guarded `NOT EXISTS` on id, so safe to re-run): `cg-seed-playerpool` (name `PlayerPool`, color `#38bdf8`) and `cg-seed-seasonpass` (name `SeasonPass`, color `#fb923c`) — names deliberately match the exact strings already used on player records (`p.cohort: "PlayerPool"`) and in `cohort_overrides`, since the picker's scoping logic matches on `g.name`/`g.id` literally, not a fuzzy label. Group count went 10 → 12, verified via SELECT. Mirrored the same two entries into the legacy `pflx_mc_cohortgroups` wrapped key for consistency (10 → 12 items, verified).
  - Confirmed via SQL scan that Vybe was the ONLY player in `pflx_mc_players` missing an individual row at the time of this patch — the client-side backfill function exists as an ongoing safety net for any future recurrence, not because more were found.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). jsdom unit tests against the real extracted code: (1) `_mcBackfillMissingPlayerRows` — first run backfills a missing player into `PLAYERS` and calls the identity-persist stub exactly once; second run is a confirmed no-op (guard holds) — PASS. (2) `pflx-cohorts-updated` listener — re-render includes newly-added PlayerPool/SeasonPass groups, preserves a pre-existing checked checkbox, and re-scopes both `qtask` and `qproject` player lists — PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — the Supabase backfill/seed already ran, and Vybe + the two new cohort groups will appear next time Mission Control is reloaded (or within a few seconds live, if Realtime is enabled on `app_data`). Renaming "PlayerPool"/"SeasonPass" to friendlier display labels (e.g. "Player Pool") can be done anytime in Settings → Cohort Manager, but changing the stored `name` would need a matching update wherever `cohort_overrides`/player records use the unspaced form — flagged here rather than done silently.
- BACKLOG (deferred by Ennis's own sequencing choice — see conversation): Topics/Titles for Project tasks (next), then the Season/Program/Checkpoint timing model + deadline-precedence + lateness tax, then the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards + background music. Each to ship as its own patch.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.41 — PROJECT TOPICS (GOOGLE-CLASSROOM-STYLE TASK GROUPING) (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: Ennis: "I also want a way to add Titles or 'Topics' much like Google Classroom into Tasks within a Project. So this might be a Project function. This would give a Project a more in depth organized view of the overall tasks in the Project." First installment of the larger Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project architecture request, shipped standalone per Ennis's own "one piece at a time" sequencing choice.
- FEATURE:
  - New data model: `project.topics = [{id, name}]` — host-authored labels scoped to one Project (a Topic in one Project has no relationship to a same-named Topic in another). `task.topicId` — optional reference from a Task into one of its Project's topics.
  - **Advanced Project form**: new "Topics" editor (below Description, above the existing Subtask checklist) — add/rename/remove rows, same interaction pattern as the Subtask editor. Saved into `project.topics` on `mcSaveProjectForm()`. Quick Project form has no Topics UI of its own but now explicitly preserves whatever Advanced set (`existing.topics || []`) so saving from Quick never wipes them.
  - **Task forms** (both Quick and Advanced): a new "Topic" dropdown appears directly under the Project picker, populated from whichever Project is currently selected, and hides itself entirely when that Project has no topics defined (zero UI noise for projects not using this). Changing the Project selection live-repopulates the Topic list (`mcTaskOnProjectChange` / extended `mcQTOnProjectChange`) and clears any stale selection. Saved as `task.topicId` in both `mcSaveTaskForm()` and `mcSaveQuickTaskForm()`.
  - **Display**: both places that list "Tasks in this Project" — the host's Mission Control Project card mini-panel, and the Player Portal's full Project Detail view — now render tasks grouped under their Topic (in the order Topics were defined, then a trailing "No Topic" bucket for anything untagged or referencing a since-deleted topic), instead of one flat list. A Project with no topics defined renders exactly as before — no header, no visual change. New shared helper `_mcGroupTasksByTopic(tasks, topics)` used by both renderers so the grouping rule only lives in one place.
  - Deleting a Topic in the editor never touches the tasks tagged with it — they just fall back into the "No Topic" bucket next render. Renaming a Topic (same id) is picked up everywhere automatically since every reference is by id, not name.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). jsdom unit tests against the real extracted code: (1) `_mcGroupTasksByTopic` — no-topics case returns one unnamed flat group; with topics defined, an empty topic is correctly omitted, tagged tasks land in their topic in order, and untagged + stale-topic-reference tasks both correctly fall into a trailing "No Topic" bucket preserving original order — PASS. (2) Topics editor round-trip — render → rename a row → add a new row → read back reflects the rename and the addition; a whitespace-only topic name is correctly dropped rather than saved as a ghost topic — PASS. (3) Task-form Topic picker — selecting a Project with topics populates and restores a prior selection, and the Topic row correctly shows/hides based on whether the selected Project has any topics — PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required. Open any existing Project in the Advanced Project form to add its first Topics — existing Projects/Tasks are unaffected until a host opts in.
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's sequencing — see conversation): next up is the Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project timing model (10-week Programs, 2-week Checkpoints, deadline-precedence rule, non-blocking Checkpoint conclusion) with a Project calendar view and Discord reminders, then the lateness tax, then the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup (leaderboards + background music).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.42 — CHECKPOINT COMPLETION HONORS EACH TASK'S OWN DUE DATE (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis, refining the Season/Program/Checkpoint architecture request: "if the task within a Project has a sub deadline which is before the checkpoint then it will count towards the current checkpoint. So if that current checkpoint has a task inside of a project which supercedes the Checkpoint, and yet the task remains during the current Checkpoint....then the tax and late fines apply and the Checkpoint is indicated as not complete. Checkpoints in a complete status means that it is still accessible with all attachments, such as tasks, will remain complete or incomplete if not done. Rewards will apply when ever the Checkpoint is fully complete. The Checkpoint is automatically submitted as complete when all tasks are complete and the reward popup should happen again... They will receive the reward popup when successfully complete with leaderboards, etc." In plain terms: a Project can run longer than the Checkpoint it's attached to, but any of that Project's tasks that are individually due WITHIN the current Checkpoint's window must still count toward that Checkpoint's completion — they shouldn't get a free pass just because their parent Project keeps running for weeks after.
- ROOT CAUSE: `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress(cp, player)` — the single shared per-player progress calculator used by 5 call sites (player-side Checkpoint detail, host progress rollup, the Checkpoint-progression gate, the host per-checkpoint roster table, and `_mcRollupAwards`'s automatic reward-payout check) — pulled in EVERY task from EVERY Project attached to a Checkpoint (`mcChildProjectsForCheckpoint` → `mcChildTasksForProject`), with no check at all against the task's own due date vs. the Checkpoint's end date. A task due long after the Checkpoint closed (because its Project runs longer) was already being counted toward that Checkpoint's total/approved tally — the opposite problem from what Ennis described, but the same underlying gap: task-vs-Checkpoint date scoping simply didn't exist.
- FIX: added a single guard inside `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress`'s internal `push(t, viaProject)` closure (~line 30886): `if (t.dueDate && cp.endDate && t.dueDate > cp.endDate) return;` — a task due AFTER the Checkpoint's end date is excluded from that Checkpoint's scope entirely (it belongs to a later Checkpoint, or is open-ended); a task due ON OR BEFORE the Checkpoint's end date counts toward it regardless of how much longer its parent Project keeps running, exactly matching Ennis's rule. Tasks with no due date, or Checkpoints with no end date, are unaffected (full backward compatibility — legacy data with no dates behaves exactly as before).
  - This single change automatically fixes completion/reward behavior everywhere without touching any of the 5 call sites individually, because they all read through this one function.
  - Notably, NO new reward-payout code was needed: `_mcRollupAwards(playerId)` (~line 35697) already implements exactly what Ennis asked for — it's an existing, automatic, per-player, idempotent mechanism that fires after every submission approval, checks `pr.approved === pr.total` via this same progress function, and pays out via `PflxDataBus.award(...)` with a `completionAwards: {playerId: timestamp}` idempotency map plus a `🏆` toast the moment a Checkpoint (or Project) becomes fully complete for that player. It was one bug — this scoping gap — away from being correct; no parallel completion-tracking system was built.
  - Login-time popup re-display, leaderboards, and the "incomplete" report variant described in Ennis's message are a separate, larger, not-yet-built feature (the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint report screen) — still queued as the last item in the agreed build order (Data model → tax → calendar → Discord → this popup). This patch only fixes the underlying completion/reward SCOPING logic those future screens will read from.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). Node vm unit test against the real extracted function (Checkpoint ending 2026-08-15, an attached Project due 2026-09-30, one task due 2026-08-10 inside the window and one task due 2026-09-20 outside it): (1) with the in-window task approved and the out-of-window task untouched, progress correctly reads 1/1 total/approved — i.e. the Checkpoint is complete despite its Project running 6 more weeks — PASS. (2) flipping that same in-window task back to 'submitted' correctly drops the Checkpoint back to incomplete (0/1 approved) — PASS. (3) a legacy no-due-date scenario (task and Checkpoint both lacking dates) is unaffected and counts exactly as before — PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — this activates automatically for every Checkpoint/Project/Task that has due dates set. Checkpoints or tasks left without an end/due date behave exactly as before this patch (no scoping applied).
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order — see conversation): next up is the Program entity (Season → Program → Checkpoint data model, mirroring how `mcSeasons`/`mcCohortGroups` sync today), then the automatic lateness tax (reusing `pflxModifiers`) that deducts XC when a Checkpoint/Project/Task concludes with in-scope work still incomplete, then a Project calendar view, then Discord reminders, then finally the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards and background music.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.43 — PROGRAM ENTITY: SEASON → PROGRAM → CHECKPOINT (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: from Ennis's Season/Program/Checkpoint architecture description, and his own agreed build order ("New entity: Season → Program → Checkpoint" → tax → calendar → Discord): "Programs as amalgams with a season, structured like a 10-week after-school program with Checkpoints on 2-week increments." First installment of that architecture, shipped standalone per Ennis's own "one piece at a time" sequencing.
- FEATURE:
  - New data model: `mcPrograms` — a full MC collection following the exact same conventions as `mcSeasons`/`mcCohortGroups` (cloud key `pflx_mc_programs`, wired into `mcSaveData`, `mcLoadData`, `_mcCollectionFor`, `_mcApplyCollection`, and `MC_CLOUD_TYPES` so it gets the same boot-pull + Realtime + push/merge machinery every other collection gets automatically — no bespoke sync code needed). Each Program: `{id, seasonId, name, startDate, status (draft/active/completed), durationWeeks, checkpointCadenceWeeks, description, createdAt, updatedAt}`.
  - **"Programs in this Season" widget** — added to the Season form (Advanced), directly below the existing "Checkpoints in this Season" widget, following the identical both-ways-linking convention (truth stays `program.seasonId`, exactly like `checkpoint.seasonId`). Lists every Program scoped to the season being edited; "+ NEW PROGRAM" reveals an inline form (name, start date, duration in weeks, checkpoint cadence in weeks, status, description) — no separate page or modal needed since Programs have few fields. Each Program row shows its linked checkpoint count and three actions: EDIT (re-opens the same inline form pre-filled), DELETE (unlinks, doesn't delete, any checkpoints it already generated — they keep their dates/tasks/season, only the `programId` back-reference clears), and **GENERATE CHECKPOINTS**.
  - **GENERATE CHECKPOINTS** — the cadence action: given a Program's `startDate`, `durationWeeks`, and `checkpointCadenceWeeks`, computes `count = round(durationWeeks / checkpointCadenceWeeks)` and creates that many real Checkpoint records, each dated as a sequential non-overlapping N-week window starting from the Program's start date, named "`<Program name> — Checkpoint <n>`", and pre-linked with both `seasonId` (the Program's season) and the new `programId` back-reference. A 10-week Program at a 2-week cadence generates 5 Checkpoints in one click; they immediately appear in both this widget's linked-checkpoint count and the existing "Checkpoints in this Season" list, and open normally in the Checkpoints tab for further editing (tasks, projects, rewards, etc. — generation only stamps name/dates/links, everything else is a normal blank checkpoint a host fills in).
  - **Checkpoint form**: new "Program" dropdown (Checkpoints tab, Advanced form) alongside the existing "Season" dropdown — lists every Program platform-wide (labeled with its Season name when it has one) so a host can link, relink, or clear a Checkpoint's Program by hand at any time, independent of whether it was cadence-generated. Saved as `checkpoint.programId`.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). Two jsdom/vm unit test passes against the real extracted code: (1) Programs-in-Season widget, 10 scenarios — create a Program persists all fields correctly; GENERATE CHECKPOINTS on a 10wk/2wk-cadence Program produces exactly 5 checkpoints with correct sequential non-overlapping date windows and correct sequence-numbered names; every generated checkpoint carries both `programId` and `seasonId`; editing a Program updates in place (no duplicate row); deleting a Program removes it but leaves its already-generated checkpoints fully intact, only clearing their `programId`; an uneven ratio (10wk/3wk cadence) rounds sensibly to 3 checkpoints instead of erroring or truncating — all PASS. (2) Checkpoint-form Program dropdown, 5 scenarios — a Program with a Season shows a "(Season name)" suffix, one with no Season shows a bare name, the checkpoint's currently-linked Program is pre-selected and no other Program is, and the save path correctly reads the selected value into `programId` — all PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — existing Seasons/Checkpoints are completely unaffected until a host opens a Season's Advanced form and adds a Program. GENERATE CHECKPOINTS is a deliberate, confirm-gated action (never runs automatically) so it's always the host's choice when to actually create the checkpoint records.
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order — see conversation): next up is the automatic lateness tax (reusing `pflxModifiers`) that deducts XC when a Checkpoint/Project/Task concludes with in-scope work still incomplete — the v1.42 date-scoping fix is what it will read from. After that: a Project calendar view, then Discord reminders (`dcChannelEnabled`/`dcChannelId`), then finally the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards and background music. Also still open, for a later pass: `season.signupOpensAt`/`signupClosesAt` fields for the "main signup window for Programs" Ennis described — not part of this patch, since the Program entity itself was the agreed first deliverable.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.44 — AUTOMATIC LATENESS TAX ON CHECKPOINT CONCLUSION (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: from Ennis's Season/Program/Checkpoint architecture and his own agreed build order — "Checkpoint concludes on schedule + tax applied (recommended)" and "Fully automatic (recommended)" reusing `pflxModifiers`. Direct continuation of his deadline-precedence clarification already implemented in v1.42: "...the tax and late fines apply and the Checkpoint is indicated as not complete."
- FEATURE:
  - New function `pflxCheckpointLatenessSweep()` — for every Checkpoint whose `endDate` has already passed (and isn't a draft/`inactive` checkpoint), checks every non-admin player's progress via the same `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress()` used everywhere else (so it automatically honors the v1.42 fix — a task due within the Checkpoint's window counts, one due after its Project's longer run doesn't). Any player short of 100% approved on their in-scope work gets `window.pflxModifiers.fireEvent('checkpoint_incomplete', {playerId, targetType:'checkpoint', targetId})` fired for them — a NEW trigger name, dispatched through the exact same event-driven modifier system already powering `checkpoint_completed`/`task_approved` auto-bonuses. No new penalty mechanism was built; this only fires the event, exactly once per player per checkpoint.
  - **Non-blocking conclusion, exactly as Ennis specified**: a Checkpoint concludes on its scheduled `endDate` regardless of completion state, stays fully accessible either way (nothing about this patch locks or hides anything), and a player who later catches up still receives the completion reward through the existing `_mcRollupAwards` path (unchanged) — the lateness tax and the completion reward are independent: being late doesn't block ever finishing, it just costs XC for missing the original deadline.
  - **Idempotency** lives on the Checkpoint record itself — `cp.latenessTaxedAt = {playerId: timestamp}`, cloud-synced with the rest of the checkpoint (same pattern as `_mcRollupAwards`'s `completionAwards` map) — so the sweep converges correctly no matter how many times or which device runs it; each player is only ever evaluated once per checkpoint. A player with nothing assigned isn't marked at all (no wasted ledger entries); a fully-complete player is marked but never taxed.
  - **Host-gated**: the sweep is a no-op on `!mcIsHost()`, so a player's own device can never fire XC deductions for other players — mirrors how the reward payout in `_mcRollupAwards` only ever runs from a host approval action.
  - **Trigger points**: runs 500ms after every `mcLoadData()` (host session boot/reload), and again on the existing 180-second cloud-health tick (`_mcHealthIv`) so a host dashboard left open catches a Checkpoint the moment it crosses its end date without needing a reload.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 14-scenario jsdom/vm unit test against the real extracted sweep function (with `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress` stubbed per-scenario, since its own date-scoping logic was already unit-tested in v1.42): fires the trigger exactly once for an incomplete concluded checkpoint with the correct player/target payload, marks it idempotent (a second sweep run does not re-fire), never taxes a fully-complete player (but still marks them processed), never touches a checkpoint that hasn't concluded yet, never touches a draft/`inactive` checkpoint even with a past-due date, skips (and leaves unmarked) a player with nothing assigned, excludes admin accounts, and confirms a non-host session never fires or marks anything at all — all 14 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS REQUIRED (first time only, unlike v1.42/v1.43): the sweep only FIRES the `checkpoint_incomplete` event — for it to actually deduct XC, a Tax-type modifier must exist in X-Coin's modifier admin with `autoApply: true` and `triggerEvent: 'checkpoint_incomplete'` (the same place `checkpoint_completed`/`task_approved` auto-bonuses are already configured; MC's own local Modifiers panel is a different, older, simpler feature and does not support `triggerEvent`/`autoApply`). Until that modifier exists, the sweep still runs and marks players processed, it just has nothing to apply — safe either way, no retroactive gap once the modifier is added (only checkpoints concluding AFTER that point will be taxed, since already-processed players are skipped from then on).
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order — see conversation): next up is a Project calendar view showing task/Project/Checkpoint timeframes, then Discord reminders (`dcChannelEnabled`/`dcChannelId`), then finally the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards and background music. Also still open: Project-level and individual Task-level lateness tax (this patch only covers the Checkpoint-level conclusion Ennis explicitly described — a Project or standalone Task passing its own due date independent of any Checkpoint is a related but separate trigger, deferred to keep this patch scoped to what was agreed).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.45 — MASTER CALENDAR: SEASON → PROGRAM → CHECKPOINT → PROJECT → TASK (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "Next. Make sure this calendar works on every level: Seasons, Programs, Checkpoints, Projects, and Tasks." Step 3 of Ennis's agreed build order ("Data model → tax → calendar → Discord"), now scoped explicitly wider than the original "Project calendar view" note — a single cross-cutting timeline spanning the whole hierarchy, not just Projects/Checkpoints.
- FEATURE:
  - New sidebar tab **Calendar** (host-only, top of TASK MANAGEMENT — sits above Checkpoints since it spans every level, not just one) → new panel `mc-panel-calendar` → `mcRenderMasterCalendar()`. Deliberately a NEW, separate view from the existing Tasks-tab Calendar view (`_mcRenderTasksCalendar`, single-level/tasks-only) — that one is untouched.
  - **Month grid** (reuses the same prev/next-month, weekday-header, day-cell structure already proven in the Tasks calendar) plots every dated item across all 5 levels:
    - **Seasons** — `startDate`/`endDate` → a start marker (▶) and end marker (◀).
    - **Programs** — `startDate` → start marker; since a Program has no `endDate` field of its own, its implied end is computed as `startDate + durationWeeks×7 − 1 days` (reusing `_mcAddDaysISO`, the same helper the v1.43 GENERATE CHECKPOINTS action uses) → end marker.
    - **Checkpoints** — `startDate`/`endDate` → start/end markers.
    - **Projects** — `startedAt`/`dueDate` → start/end markers when both are set; a Project with only a `dueDate` (no `startedAt`) shows a single plain point chip instead, matching how it's treated everywhere else in MC (`p.dueDate || p.endDate || p.deadline`).
    - **Tasks** — `dueDate` only (tasks are due-date items, not ranges) → a single chip, colored by the task's own priority (same `MC_PRIORITY_META` colors as the existing Tasks calendar, for visual consistency between the two calendar views).
  - Each type gets its own distinct color (Seasons blue, Programs purple, Checkpoints gold, Projects pink, Tasks by priority) so five overlapping timelines stay readable at a glance.
  - **Legend = filter toggles**: five pill buttons above the grid (one per type) show/hide that type and persist the choice (`localStorage: pflx_mc_calendar_filters`) — a host running a busy month can hide Tasks and just see the Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project skeleton, or vice versa.
  - **Click-through**: every chip is clickable and jumps to that item. Checkpoint/Project/Task reuse the existing `mcJumpToItem` navigation (nav to that tab + highlight the row). Season now does the same (a `data-mc-season-id` attribute was added to season cards, which didn't have one before). Program is a new case in `mcJumpToItem` — since a Program has no top-level list of its own (it only lives inside its parent Season's Advanced form, per v1.43), clicking a Program chip navigates to Seasons, opens the OWNING season's form (resolved via `program.seasonId`, not the calendar's current context), then highlights the specific program row inside it (a `data-mc-program-id` attribute was added to program rows for this).
  - Day cells cap at 4 visible chips with a "+N more" overflow, matching the existing Tasks calendar convention — deliberately NOT rendering a Season/Program's full range across every day it spans (a 10-week Program would otherwise flood 70 day-cells with 70 identical chips); start/end markers say what a host actually needs to know (when does this begin, when does it conclude) without the noise.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). Two jsdom/vm unit test passes against the real extracted code: (1) Master Calendar aggregation, 17 scenarios — all 5 types render with correct markers (legend shows all 5 toggles; Season/Checkpoint/ranged-Project show both ▶/◀ markers; Program's implied end date from `durationWeeks` lands on the correct day; a Project with only a `dueDate` renders as a plain point chip with no arrow; a Task renders with its priority color), filter toggling hides exactly the targeted type and marks it "(hidden)" in the legend while leaving others untouched, `mcToggleCalFilter` flips and un-flips correctly, an item entirely outside the displayed month is excluded from that month's grid, and 5 same-day items correctly overflow to a "+1 more" indicator — all PASS. (2) `mcJumpToItem`'s new branches, 5 scenarios — 'season' navigates to the Seasons tab, 'program' navigates to Seasons then opens the CORRECT owning season's form (verified against a Program whose season is NOT the first in the list, so the owning-season lookup is actually exercised rather than coincidentally right), an unknown program id is a safe no-op with zero navigation, and the pre-existing 'checkpoint' behavior is unchanged (regression check) — all PASS.

Also noted for a later pass: the Master Calendar currently shows markers only (start/end), not a continuous range bar — if Ennis wants a true Gantt-style spanning view later, that's a bigger UI lift (absolute-positioned bars across the day grid) deferred out of this patch to keep it shippable.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.46 — AUTOMATIC PROJECT DISCORD/SLACK REMINDERS (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: from Ennis's original Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project architecture description — "Projects as duration/management-focused with Discord messaging (timely reports/reminders 'like a Google Calendar invite')." Step 4 of the agreed build order (Data model → tax → calendar → Discord), now that the Master Calendar (v1.45) is live.
- FEATURE:
  - New function `pflxProjectReminderSweep()` — for every Project with the existing `dcChannelEnabled` toggle on (Advanced Project form → "Auto-create private DarkCampus channel" section) and not yet `completed`, checks a fixed set of day-offset thresholds against its `startedAt`/`dueDate` and fires an automatic reminder the moment each threshold arrives: **starts tomorrow**, **starts TODAY**, **due in 3 days**, **due tomorrow**, **due TODAY**, and **now OVERDUE**.
  - Reuses the EXISTING `pflxEmitProjectEvent(projectId, 'reminders', message)` bridge rather than posting to Discord directly — `'reminders'` was already one of DarkCampus's anticipated `feedOptions` keys (alongside alerts/overviews/tasks/offers) sitting unused until now. This means a reminder automatically respects whichever channel a host has linked via `dcChannelId` AND whatever feed types that channel has toggled on in DarkCampus — no new delivery mechanism, no new webhook, no new channel picker. It also mirrors to the channel's connected Slack/Discord exactly like task-completion and deadline-hit events already do, once those webhooks are provisioned.
  - **Idempotent, fire-once-ever per threshold** — tracked in `project.remindersSent = {tierKey: timestamp}`, cloud-synced with the rest of the project record (same convention as `cp.latenessTaxedAt` from v1.44 and `completionAwards` from before that). Re-running the sweep never re-sends a reminder that already went out.
  - **Catch-up is intentional**: if a host hasn't opened Mission Control in a while and multiple thresholds have already passed for a Project, all of them fire together the next time the sweep runs (each still only once) — better a burst of context on return than a silently-missed deadline.
  - **Host-gated**: no-op on `!mcIsHost()`, so a player's own device never fires reminders for other people's projects — same pattern as the v1.44 lateness sweep.
  - **Trigger points**: 700ms after every `mcLoadData()` (host session boot/reload) and on the same 180-second cloud-health tick already re-running the lateness sweep, so a host dashboard left open catches a threshold the moment it arrives.
  - Updated the Advanced Project form's channel-link helper text to say plainly that this toggle now also drives automatic deadline reminders, since it previously only described task-completion/@tag notifications.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 13-scenario jsdom/vm unit test against the real extracted sweep function: fires exactly the due-3d reminder (and no others) when a due date is precisely 3 days out, routes through the `'reminders'` feedType, marks the fired tier on the project record and saves once; a second sweep run does not re-fire the same tier (idempotent); a Project checked late fires every already-passed threshold together in one catch-up pass; a Project without `dcChannelEnabled` is never reminded; a `completed` Project is never reminded even if overdue; start-date and due-date reminders fire independently of each other; and a non-host session never fires or marks anything at all — all 13 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required for Projects that already have "Auto-create private DarkCampus channel" enabled (the default) — reminders start firing automatically as thresholds arrive. Actual delivery to a real Discord/Slack channel still depends on that channel's webhook being provisioned in DarkCampus (unchanged, pre-existing requirement — same as every other notification type this bridge already carries).
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order — see conversation): the last remaining item is the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards (Digital Coin Images, Tax Images, XC gained/lost, level/Evo rank progress, Startup Studio stats, top-earners/most-minutes/most-tasks/Battle Arena/Signature Badge/Executive Badge leaderboards) and background music — the last item in the original bundled request, not yet scoped in detail. Also noted for a later pass, if wanted: extending this same reminder-tier pattern to Checkpoints directly (currently Checkpoint conclusion only triggers the v1.44 lateness tax, not a Discord reminder) — deferred since Ennis's own wording scoped Discord messaging specifically to Projects.

(2) `mcJumpToItem`'s updated 'program' branch, 4 scenarios (including regression coverage for 'season') — now navigates straight to the Programs tab, and correctly highlights ONLY the top-level tab's row when an identical `data-mc-program-id` also exists in a hidden nested-widget copy — all PASS.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.48 — NODE SUBMISSIONS ROUTE THROUGH THE UNIFIED APPROVALS QUEUE (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "Modules created with the Module Builder will be able to interact and automatically reward through the node. Nodes that use another link type will use the nodes submission functions. This will use the same method as Mission Control and approvals will be submitted to the hosts."
- INVESTIGATION FIRST: traced the full Module→Node→Console pipeline before touching anything. Found the Module Builder's connector contract (viewer.html → pathway.html → `pflx_module_completion` → Console's `mcApprovals` queue → host approve/reject → `PflxDataBus.award` clamped to the node's own `xcReward`/`taggedBadges`) already works end-to-end for the ~2 nodes that have a `coursePackage` (i.e. an actual built Module) attached. The gap was every OTHER node — the ones using the existing generic "submission" mechanism (link/screenshot/html/description, configured per-node in pathway.html's node editor) instead of a Module. Those submissions were going to a completely separate surface (the Console's Home Approvals Card, via the shared X-Coin `submissions` cloud row) and paying out from the selected badge's catalog value — not from the node's own configured reward, and not visible anywhere in the Mission Control tab's Approvals Queue alongside Module completions.
- FEATURE — non-module node submissions now use "the same method as Mission Control":
  - `pathway.html`'s node-submission handler (the `subSubmitBtn` click handler in the node detail panel) now snapshots the node's `xcReward`/`taggedBadges` directly into the submission record it sends — `reward: { xc, badgeIds }` plus `nodeTitle`/`pathwaySlug`/`submission: {link, description}` — mirroring the exact shape of a Module Completion Record. This is captured AT SUBMIT TIME so approval always pays what the node was actually configured for, with no separate lookup against Console's (sometimes stale) cached pathway catalog.
  - Console's `pflx_node_submission` listener (and a matching reconciliation pass inside the existing 15s cloud-feed pull, for the case where a host wasn't online when the player submitted — a "catch-up" pass, same idiom as the v1.44 lateness sweep and v1.46 reminder sweep) now pushes these into `mcApprovals` as a new type, `node_submission`, instead of the old X-Coin-shared `submissions` queue. Dedup is by the original submission id (`subId`) so a submission is never double-queued.
  - The Mission Control tab's Approvals Queue renders `node_submission` items exactly like `module_completion` items (🛰 icon, submission link/description, "Awards N XC on approval" preview) and hosts approve/reject them from the same Approve/Reject buttons.
  - Approving pays XC + badges via `PflxDataBus.award` using the node's own snapshotted reward — the SAME automatic reward-through-the-node math Module completions use, not the badge-catalog-derived amount the old path used.
  - Rejecting simply marks it rejected — no payout, same as Module completions.
  - Either action mirrors the resolved status back onto the shared X-Coin `submissions` cloud row (`_pflxMirrorNodeSubStatus`) so X-Coin's own admin view (and anything else reading that row) still sees it as resolved — this preserves a behavior the old path already had, so nothing downstream silently stops working.
  - The Home Approvals Card (Console's homebase widget) no longer shows node-tagged submissions at all — they're exclusively in the Mission Control tab's queue now, so there's exactly one host-facing place for every node's activity, module or not.
- Files: `pflx-pathway-portal/pathway.html` (submission record now carries `reward`/`nodeTitle`/`pathwaySlug`/`submission`), `pflx-platform/preview.html` (`_pflxIngestNodeSubmission`, `_pflxMirrorNodeSubStatus`, the `pflx_node_submission` listener, the cloud-pull catch-up pass, the Home card's coinsub filter, and `node_submission` handling added to `mcRenderApprovals`/`_mcApprovalAllowed`/`mcApproveItem`/`mcRejectItem`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean on both files (preview.html 13/13, pathway.html 4/4). 43 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted code, all PASS: (1) `_pflxIngestNodeSubmission`/`_pflxMirrorNodeSubStatus` — 15 scenarios covering correct ingestion, subId dedupe, non-node and already-resolved submissions correctly ignored, fallback submission shape, and cloud-row status mirroring. (2) `mcApproveItem`/`mcRejectItem` for `node_submission` — 12 scenarios covering correct XC+badge payout from the node's own reward, a no-reward node approving cleanly with zero payout, rejection paying nothing, cloud-row mirroring on both actions, and multiple pending items not cross-contaminating. (3) Home Approvals Card filtering — 4 scenarios confirming node-tagged submissions never render there while plain X-Coin badge submissions still do. (4) `pathway.html`'s submission builder — 12 scenarios confirming the posted `pflx_node_submission` message carries the node's real `xcReward`/`taggedBadges` as `reward.xc`/`reward.badgeIds`, degrades safely to `{xc:0, badgeIds:[]}` for an unconfigured node, and the player's real link/description input (not raw upload data-URLs) lands in `submission`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required. Existing node submissions already sitting in the cloud `submissions` row as `pending` will be swept into the Mission Control Approvals tab automatically the next time any host session loads (via the cloud-pull catch-up pass) — nothing manual needed, and nothing is lost.
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order): the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards and background music remains the last unscoped item.

## PATCH PORTAL — NODE COVER IMAGES NO LONGER DEFAULT-CROP TEXT OUT OF THE CIRCLE (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — on the "Professional Entrepreneurship" pathway, the COURSE node's cover image showed "Part of the name is cut out and black" (screenshot: a wide website-screenshot cover image with its headline text sliced off mid-word by the node's circular mask).
- ROOT CAUSE: every node cover image renders via `<img class="node-image" ... style="object-fit:${n.imageFit||'cover'}">` inside a `border-radius:50%` circle (pathway.html ~5464/7534). `object-fit: cover` scales a rectangular image to fill the circle's bounding square and then crops whatever spills past the edges — for a wide screenshot with a horizontal headline, that means slicing straight through the text. This was also the value every code path defaulted `imageFit` TO the moment an image was uploaded (`openImageUpload`, pathway.html:8211) or a node was created from a pitch with an image (:7423) — so essentially every uploaded cover image ended up with `imageFit: 'cover'` baked in, even though the node editor already ships a "Contain (fit whole image)" option (`imgFitSelect`/`neImageFit`) that never crops anything — hosts just had no reason to know they needed it.
- FIX: flipped every `imageFit` default from `'cover'` to `'contain'` across all 8 call sites in `pathway.html` (the two node-render paths, the pitch-node-with-image default, the upload-time default, the node-editor's populate/save handlers, and both image-preview renders) — nothing was removed, "Cover" and "Stretch" are still selectable per-node exactly as before, and any node with an ALREADY-explicit `imageFit` value (cover, contain, or fill) keeps that exact value untouched. Only the behavior for images that never had an explicit choice made changes — from "silently crop, hope nothing important is near the edge" to "always show the whole image, never crop."
- SCOPE, per Ennis: fix the rendering so this can't happen to ANY node again (not just re-crop the one broken image). Confirmed and implemented that way.
- CAVEAT — the ALREADY-BROKEN "Professional Entrepreneurship" node itself: this node's image almost certainly has `imageFit: 'cover'` explicitly stored on it already (from going through the same upload flow before this fix), so the new default does NOT retroactively change already-saved nodes — only new/unset ones. To fix that specific node's display: open it in Edit Mode → the image upload panel → change "Image Fit" from Cover to Contain (or click the node's 📷 image and use the Adjust Image dialog's fit dropdown) — 10 seconds, no code/data change needed. Flagged rather than guessed at via a direct Supabase edit, since I can't visually confirm the result without seeing the live page.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (4/4 blocks). 5-scenario jsdom/node unit test against the real extracted render expression (both duplicate render-path occurrences): unset `imageFit` → `object-fit:contain`; explicit `cover`/`fill` values are preserved unchanged; a node with no image renders nothing — all PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: for the "Professional Entrepreneurship" course node (and any other existing node whose cover image already looks cropped), switch its Image Fit to Contain via the node editor as described above. No action needed for any node that already looks fine.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.49 — PROGRAM FORM: COVER IMAGE, DIGITAL BADGES, COHORT-SCOPED ROSTERING (Aug 12, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "Add a image upload mush like Seasons and Checkpoints and Projects. Add a Digital Badge import (multi-select), add a Cohort multi select. If Cohort is connected then Program will roster with only selected cohort in every sub category."
- FEATURE — the top-level Programs tab form (`#mc-program-tab-form`) now matches Season/Checkpoint/Project's editing surface:
  - **Cover Image**: same upload/preview/remove pattern as Project — `mcUploadProgramBanner()` downscales via `_mcDownscaleImageDataUrl(file, 1600, 900, 0.82)` then uploads to Supabase Storage via `pflxUploadBannerToStorage(dataUrl, 'program')` (new `kind:'program'` folder in the `pflx-banners` bucket), falling back to an inline dataURL if storage is unreachable. `mcRemoveProgramBanner()` uses the same `'__REMOVED__'` sentinel Project uses so an empty banner field on save always means "preserve existing," never "wipe it."
  - **Digital Badges**: a `.mc-program-badge-cb` checkbox list populated from `mcGetAllBadges()` (the unified badge catalog), saved as `program.rewardBadges` (array of badge ids) — same shape as Project's `rewardBadges`.
  - **Cohorts**: an "All Cohorts" checkbox (default checked) + a `.mc-program-cohort-cb` checkbox list populated from `mcCohortGroups`, saved as `program.cohortIds` (array of `mcCohortGroups[].id` values) — same convention Project uses, chosen over Checkpoint's raw-name `assignedTo` convention because the checkbox-list UI pattern is simpler and better precedented, and because Program needed ITS OWN resolver anyway to bridge into Checkpoint's convention (see below).
- FEATURE — cohort scoping cascades down to a Program's Checkpoints ("Program will roster with only selected cohort in every sub category"):
  - New resolver `_pflxProgramCohortNames(program)` (preview.html, right before `mcSeasonGenerateCheckpoints`) converts `program.cohortIds` (group ids) into a flat, deduped array of raw cohort NAME strings by resolving each `mcCohortGroups[].id` → its `.cohorts` list (or its own `.name` if the group has no sub-cohort list). This exists because Checkpoint's `assignedTo` field is name-based, not id-based — Project's and Checkpoint's cohort conventions have drifted apart historically, and this resolver is the bridge between them.
  - `mcSaveProgramTabForm()` now reads `rewardBadges`/`cohortIds`/`bannerImage` into the saved program object, then — if `cohortIds` is non-empty — walks every `mcCheckpoints` entry with `cp.programId === obj.id` and sets `cp.assignedTo = _pflxProgramCohortNames(obj)`, saving `mcSaveData('checkpoints')` only if something was actually touched. Empty `cohortIds` (All Cohorts) leaves existing checkpoints untouched, same "don't clobber a host's tighter per-item scope" rule Project's Task-cascade already follows.
  - `mcSeasonGenerateCheckpoints()` (used by both the top-level Programs tab's "Generate Checkpoints" action and the nested Season-form widget) was updated in the same pass to seed newly-generated checkpoints' `assignedTo` from `_pflxProgramCohortNames(pg)` instead of a hardcoded `'all'`, so cohort scoping is inherited at CREATION time too, not just on a later edit-and-save.
  - `mcShowProgramTabForm()` restores an existing program's saved `rewardBadges`/`cohortIds`/`bannerImage` selections when reopening the form for edit (checks the right boxes, toggles the cohort list visibility, shows the banner preview) — same restore pattern Project's show-form function uses.
- SCOPE note: the simpler nested "Programs in this Season" widget inside the Season form (added v1.43, a quick-view surface) was intentionally left UNCHANGED — it still edits `mcPrograms` via its own lighter save path. The full editing surface (banner/badges/cohorts) lives only in the top-level Programs tab form, which is what Ennis's screenshot showed and where he's actively working.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only — `PFLX_PATCH` 48→49, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08). No `pathway.html` changes this patch.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 21 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted code, all PASS: (1) `_pflxProgramCohortNames` — 6 scenarios covering empty/missing input, multi-cohort group resolution, single-name fallback, cross-group dedup, and a silently-skipped unresolvable group id. (2) `mcSaveProgramTabForm` — 15 scenarios covering badge/cohort checkbox reads, the Checkpoint cascade (linked checkpoints updated, a checkpoint on a DIFFERENT program left alone, All-Cohorts leaving existing checkpoints untouched), the banner preserve/remove/upload sentinel behavior (3 cases), and the existing season/name required-field guard clauses still working unchanged.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required. Existing programs with no `cohortIds`/`rewardBadges`/`bannerImage` saved will simply show "All Cohorts," no badges checked, and no cover image the next time the form is opened — nothing is lost, the new fields are purely additive.
- BACKLOG (per Ennis's agreed build order): the Gimkit/Blooket-style end-of-Checkpoint/Project report popup with leaderboards and background music remains the last unscoped item.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.51 — MISSION CONTROL SIDEBAR: COLLAPSE/EXPAND FIX + DRAG-TO-RESIZE (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — "IM able to collapse the side panel but I cant bring it back. Hide button is hiding as well. I should be able to resize the side panel." Once the Mission Control left sidebar was collapsed, there was no working way to bring it back short of a page reload.
- ROOT CAUSE: the v1.38 desktop/tablet collapse feature's "show sidebar" button (`.mc-sidebar-expand-btn`) was styled `position: fixed; top: 14px; left: 14px;` — coordinates measured from the VIEWPORT. The app's own top `.toolbar` also sits at the top of the viewport, is 64px tall, and carries `z-index: 100`. The expand button's `z-index: 56` put it well underneath. So the moment a host collapsed the sidebar, the only way to bring it back was rendered — `display:flex` was correctly toggled — but it was sitting directly behind the opaque toolbar the entire time: invisible and unclickable. Every other floating control in Mission Control (`.app-refresh-btn`, `.mc-sidebar-collapse-btn` itself) uses `position: absolute` relative to `.mission-control-view` (which starts BELOW the toolbar in the page's grid layout) — the expand button was the one outlier still using `position: fixed`.
- FIX: changed `.mc-sidebar-expand-btn` from `position:fixed` to `position:absolute`, matching the pattern every other MC floating control already uses successfully. It now renders inside `.mission-control-view`'s content area, safely below the toolbar, at every collapse/expand cycle.
- FEATURE — sidebar is now resizable, per Ennis's request: added a thin drag handle (`#mc-sidebar-resize-handle`) along the sidebar's right edge. Dragging it live-resizes `.mc-sidebar`'s width between 180px and 440px (matching new CSS `min-width`/`max-width` — previously `min-width` was pinned equal to the default `width` of 230px, which would have silently blocked any resize). Uses Pointer Events (`pointerdown`/`pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`) so mouse, touch, and pen all drag identically. The chosen width persists to `localStorage` (`pflx_mc_sidebar_width`) and is restored on next load, same pattern the existing collapse-state persistence (`pflx_mc_sidebar_collapsed`) already uses. Double-clicking the handle snaps back to the 230px default as a quick escape hatch. The handle (along with the existing collapse/expand buttons) stays hidden under 768px, where the sidebar is still the off-canvas mobile drawer instead.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 50→51, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 14 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted `mcToggleDesktopSidebar`/`mcInitSidebarResize` code, all PASS: collapse/expand toggling and persistence in both directions, drag-driven width changes, clamping at both the 180px floor and 440px ceiling, restoring a valid saved width on load, ignoring an out-of-range/corrupt saved width (falls back to the CSS default instead of breaking layout), the double-click reset, and a double-init guard that confirms calling the init function twice (e.g. on a re-render) doesn't double-bind the drag listeners and double the drag delta. The `position:fixed`→`position:absolute` stacking-context fix itself is a pure CSS/layout change and isn't something jsdom can render — verified by tracing the toolbar's `z-index:100` against every other floating MC control's positioning pattern instead.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Any host whose sidebar is currently stuck collapsed will see the (now-visible, now-clickable) expand button the next time they load Mission Control — no data or state needs fixing.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.52 — LAUNCH APPS TILES: DUPLICATE HOVER TOOLTIP FIXED (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — "There seems to be a glitch on this app selection. Its blinking. There is also no need for the popup description because the description already appears on hover" (re: the "Launch Apps" tile grid on the Home Base screen — Mission Control / X-Coin / Core Pathways / Battle Arena / DarkCampus). Screenshot showed a dark floating popup box overlapping the Mission Control tile's own on-card description text, both showing the identical description at once.
- ROOT CAUSE: `pflxRenderHomeAppHub()` (preview.html, home app hub tile builder) set BOTH `tile.title = app.desc` (the browser's own native OS tooltip) AND rendered a custom `.pflx-app-hub-desc` overlay div that fades in on hover — same text, both wired to the exact same hover state. The native tooltip has its own independent show/hide timing controlled by the browser (not our code) and repositions/redraws on nearby paint changes; the custom overlay was ALSO transitioning opacity/transform on that same hover. The two fought for the same screen space and timing, producing the overlapping double-text "blinking" Ennis saw.
- FIX: removed `tile.title = app.desc` — the on-card `.pflx-app-hub-desc` overlay already fully covers "the description appears on hover," so the native tooltip was pure redundancy causing the glitch. Nothing else about the tile changed — hover transform/box-shadow/border-color behavior and the on-card overlay's fade-in/out are untouched.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 51→52, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 7 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted `pflxRenderHomeAppHub()`, all PASS: all 5 tiles render, no tile carries a `title` attribute anymore, the on-card description overlay still exists and still carries the real text, it's hidden by default, and it correctly shows/hides on simulated hover/unhover.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.53 — LAUNCH APPS TILES: HOVER FLICKER LOOP FIXED (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis, after v1.52's duplicate-tooltip fix — "On hover its appearing and reseting the hover effect over and over" on the same "Launch Apps" tile grid. The hover lift/glow effect was rapidly toggling on and off by itself while the mouse sat still over a tile.
- ROOT CAUSE: `pflxRenderHomeAppHub()`'s hover handler applied `tile.style.transform = 'translateY(-2px)'` directly to `tile` — the EXACT SAME element whose `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` listeners drive the whole effect. A CSS `transform` moves an element's actual on-screen box, not just how it paints — the instant a tile lifted 2px on hover, its edge (most often the bottom edge, since the cursor is frequently resting near where the mouse first crossed in) moved out from under the cursor, firing `mouseleave`. That reset the transform, the tile dropped back down 2px, the cursor was inside it again, firing `mouseenter` — an infinite self-triggered oscillation exactly at whatever boundary the host's mouse happened to be resting near. This is a well-known class of CSS bug: never transform the same element that owns the hover hit-test.
- FIX: split the tile into two layers — `tile` itself (the actual `<button>`, hit-tested, owns mouseenter/mouseleave, never moves) and a new inner `.pflx-app-hub-inner` wrapper (icon + label only) that receives the lift transform instead. `tile`'s box-shadow and border-color hover changes stay directly on `tile` since neither affects hit-testing (a shadow or border-color change doesn't move an element's box) — only the transform needed to move to a non-hoverable layer. The on-card description overlay (`.pflx-app-hub-desc`, already `pointer-events:none` from v1.52) is unaffected either way.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 52→53, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). 11 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted `pflxRenderHomeAppHub()`, all PASS — including the direct regression test: hovering never applies a transform to `tile` itself (only to the separate inner wrapper), and a simulated 20-cycle rapid enter/leave burst (worst-case replay of the flicker loop) confirms the tile still ends up with zero transform applied, every time.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.54 — LAUNCH APPS TILES: HOVER JITTER DEBOUNCED (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis, after v1.53's transform fix — "its still blinking." The Launch Apps tile hover effect (glow/lift/description) was still visibly flashing on and off.
- INVESTIGATION — this time verified in a real browser instead of reasoning about it: built a standalone repro of the exact extracted `pflxRenderHomeAppHub()` code and drove it with Playwright (headless Chromium) rather than just jsdom. A static, unmoving cursor never flickered (confirms v1.53's fix was real and correct) — but simulating natural hand/trackpad micro-jitter (±1-2px moves) with the cursor resting near ANY tile's edge reproduced 30 real `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` firings from 30 tiny moves, in BOTH the pre-v1.53 and post-v1.53 code equally. That's the actual root cause: a cursor rented near a boundary crosses it many times a second from ordinary micro-jitter — true of any hover element, not something the v1.53 transform fix could touch, since it happens even when nothing on the page visually moves at all.
- FIX: debounced the hover-out. `mouseleave` no longer hides the glow/lift/description immediately — it schedules the hide 80ms out via `setTimeout`, and `mouseenter` cancels that pending hide if it fires first (standard tooltip/dropdown debounce pattern). A genuine "moved to a different tile" leave still hides after 80ms, imperceptible to a host. A jitter blip that re-enters within 80ms never gets the chance to visually flicker at all — the pending hide is canceled before it ever executes.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 53→54, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks); 13 jsdom/vm unit-test scenarios against the real extracted code, all PASS — immediate show-on-hover, hide is deferred not instant, re-entry within the debounce window cancels the pending hide with zero visible flicker, a genuine departure still hides ~110ms later, and 10 rapid sub-window enter/leave cycles never drop the overlay to hidden even once. (2) A real-browser Playwright test (not jsdom) replaying the exact ±1-2px jitter pattern that reproduced the bug: sampling the description overlay's visible opacity every 10ms across the whole jitter burst showed exactly 2 total visual transitions (show once, hide once at the very end) despite 30 real internal enter/leave events firing — i.e., zero perceptible flicker, confirmed against actual browser layout/paint, not a simulation.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.55 — MC SIDEBAR TOGGLE & RESIZE HANDLE: OVERFLOW-CLIPPING FIXED (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — "The toggle is hiding" (screenshots showed the Mission Control sidebar collapse button reduced to a thin sliver at the panel's edge, mostly cut off).
- ROOT CAUSE: `.mc-sidebar` has `overflow-x: hidden`. Both `.mc-sidebar-collapse-btn` (`right: -14px`) and `.mc-sidebar-resize-handle` (`right: -3px`, added in v1.51) were deliberately positioned to straddle/poke past the sidebar's own right edge for a floating-button visual effect. `overflow-x: hidden` clips any child content past the parent's box — so the portion of each control sitting outside the sidebar's own width was silently sliced off, leaving only a sliver visible/clickable. This is a pre-existing bug on the collapse button (present since it was introduced at v1.38, well before this session) — the resize handle added in v1.51 inherited the same flaw by using the same "poke past the edge" pattern. Not caused by the v1.51 resize-handle work itself; both are fixed together for consistency.
- FIX: pulled both controls fully inside the sidebar's own box — `.mc-sidebar-collapse-btn` `right: -14px` → `right: 10px`; `.mc-sidebar-resize-handle` `right: -3px` → `right: 0`. Both now render and hit-test entirely within the clipped bounds instead of being cut off.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 54→55, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) Real-browser Playwright test (`repro_sidebar.html`, built with the fixed CSS values) — measured actual boxes via `boundingBox()`: sidebar `{x:0,y:0,w:231,h:500}`, collapse button `{x:192,y:14,w:28,h:28}` (right edge 220, inside 231), resize handle `{x:224,y:0,w:6,h:500}` (right edge 230, inside 231) — both fully within the clipped sidebar bounds. `document.elementFromPoint()` hit-tests at all 4 corners of the collapse button all correctly resolved to the collapse-btn element, confirming it's fully clickable everywhere, not just on a visible sliver.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.56 — CORE PATHWAYS PLAYER CARD: STALE AVATAR OVERWRITE FIXED (Aug 12, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — "My avatar in the player card didn't update." Screenshots showed the toolbar (top-right, "MR. JOHNSON") correctly showing his uploaded photo, while the Player Card popup in Core Pathways showed a fallback "T" logo instead. Ennis later clarified the card in question was the one INSIDE `pathway.html` (`#playerCard` / `initPlayerCard()`), not the toolbar's own profile dropdown or the Battle Arena `PlayerCard.tsx` component (both were checked and ruled out first).
- ROOT CAUSE: `pathway.html`'s `initPlayerCard()` merges identity from local storage (`pflx_pathway_user` / `pflx_user`) and then does a live Supabase fetch of `app_data` key `'users'` to refresh stats. That fetch UNCONDITIONALLY overwrote `user.image` with whatever the cloud `'users'` row had (`if (xcUser.image) user.image = xcUser.image;`) — even blank/stale. Traced why the cloud `'users'` row can be stale: an avatar upload (`portfolioUploadAvatar` in `preview.html`) writes the new image onto `PLAYERS[i].image` and the in-memory `activeSession.image` immediately (which is why the toolbar, which reads `activeSession.image` directly with no cloud round-trip, always showed the fresh photo right away) — but the cloud `'users'` row only gets the new image via `broadcastPlayerChange()` finding a MATCHING record in the separate `mcPlayers` array by id and mirroring the change in before `mcCloudSync('players')` pushes it. If that id lookup misses (`mcPlayers` and `PLAYERS` can drift, per the July `id` split notes already in this Handoff), the image change never reaches the cloud `'users'` row at all — so the Pathways card's next Supabase fetch pulls the old/blank value and stomps the already-correct local copy with it, on every single load.
- FIX: `pathway.html` line ~6663 — `if (xcUser.image) user.image = xcUser.image;` → `if (xcUser.image && !user.image) user.image = xcUser.image;`. This brings `image` in line with every OTHER identity field already merged in this function ("only fill in what's missing locally") — a local avatar we already have (freshly uploaded this session, same browser) is trusted over a cloud row that may not have caught up yet. The cloud value is still used as a fallback for a genuinely fresh device/session with no local image at all. All other fields (xcoin, totalXcoin, digitalBadges, level, rank, brandName, name, isHost, role, earnedBadges, streak, shipTier) are untouched — they still sync unconditionally from the cloud exactly as before, since those ARE meant to reflect live server-driven state.
- Files: `pflx-platform/pathway.html` only (the sibling `preview.html` was ALSO shipped this same push, but only to bump `PFLX_PATCH`; no code changes to preview.html from this investigation). `PFLX_PATCH` 55→56, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified: syntax gate clean on both files (13/13 preview.html blocks, 4/4 pathway.html blocks). 18 jsdom/vm scenarios run against the ACTUAL extracted merge fragment (not a re-implementation) all PASS — a stale/blank cloud image never clobbers a fresh local avatar; local wins when both are present; cloud still fills in correctly on a fresh device with no local image (including the empty-string case); every other field (xcoin, totalXcoin, digitalBadges, level, rank, brandName, name, streak, shipTier, isHost, role, earnedBadges) still syncs unconditionally from the cloud exactly as before — confirming this patch is scoped to the avatar field only.
- HOST ACTIONS: none for this fix. BACKLOG (not fixed here, flagged for a future patch): the underlying `PLAYERS` vs `mcPlayers` id-mismatch that can silently drop an avatar (and potentially other fields) from ever reaching the cloud `'users'` row in `broadcastPlayerChange()` is still present — this patch makes the Pathways card resilient to that gap, but doesn't close it at the source. Worth revisiting if other MC→X-Coin field-drop symptoms show up.
