## PATCH PLATFORM v1.58 — PROGRAM COMPLETION ROLLUPS: CHECKPOINTS/PROJECTS INDICATORS, TASKS PROGRESS BAR, SEASONS SHOW PROGRAMS (Aug 13, Ennis)
- REQUEST: Ennis, on top of v1.57's richer Program cards — "It [Programs tab card] should show an indicator of Checkpoints and Projects completed. Tasks will not show individually but as a complete progress bar. Seasons view should show all Programs and Program progression bar."
- NEW SHARED HELPER — `_pflxProgramRollup(program)` (~line 38338): walks the same Checkpoint → Project → Task hierarchy already used by the MC scope picker (Checkpoints matched by `cp.programId`; each Checkpoint's Projects by `cp.projectIds` / `p.checkpointId` / `p.roundId`; each Project's Tasks by `p.taskIds` / `t.projectId`; Tasks parented directly to a Checkpoint — no Project — by `cp.taskIds` / `t.roundId` / `t.checkpointId`). Dedupes tasks so one claimed via its Project is never double-counted when also scanning the Checkpoint's direct task list. Returns `{cpTotal, cpDone, projTotal, projDone, taskTotal, taskDone, taskPct}` — a Checkpoint/Project counts as done when `status === 'completed'`; a Task counts as done when `status === 'approved'` (same definition the MC dashboard header stat already uses). One rollup function, used by both surfaces below, so the numbers always agree.
- PROGRAMS TAB (`mcRenderProgramsTab`, ~line 38482): each card now shows "Checkpoints: X / Y completed" and "Projects: X / Y completed" as plain indicators (both go green when fully complete), plus a single aggregate Tasks progress bar (done/total + %) — never an individual task list, since a host scanning this tab wants "how far along is this program" at a glance, not a task-by-task drill-down (that already exists on the Checkpoint/Project detail views). The bar is omitted entirely when the program has zero tasks yet (nothing to divide).
- SEASONS TAB (`mcRenderSeasons`, ~line 37926, new helper `_mcSeasonProgramsSummaryHtml` ~line 37904): each Season card now shows a "Programs (N)" section listing every Program under that Season (via `Program.seasonId`) with its name, status pill, and the SAME task-completion progress bar/percentage as the Programs tab — reusing `_pflxProgramRollup` so the two views can never disagree. A Season with no Programs shows nothing extra (no empty "Programs (0)" clutter on every card).
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 57→58, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) 19 jsdom/vm scenarios run against the ACTUAL extracted functions (not a re-implementation), all PASS — rollup correctly counts/dedupes checkpoints, projects, and tasks across both project-owned and checkpoint-direct task paths; handles a program with zero checkpoints without dividing by zero; Programs tab card renders correct Checkpoints/Projects completed fractions and a Tasks bar with the right done/total/percent; confirmed NO individual task names/titles appear anywhere on the card; the Tasks bar is omitted when there are zero tasks; the Seasons list's Programs section shows the right count, program name, and progression fraction, and renders nothing for a season with zero programs.
- HOST ACTIONS: none — purely a render/rollup change against existing data, no new fields, no migration.

## PATCH XCOIN v1.1 — DIGITAL BADGE GRANT MODAL: PLAYER PICKER OVERHAUL (Aug 13, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — the "Grant [Badge Name]" modal (X-Coin admin → Coins → Grant) only showed players' real names, not their brand names; the 2-column player list ran off the right edge of the modal and required scrolling sideways to see the second column; and every player showed a plain colored swatch with no photo or initials, even for players who don't have an uploaded avatar.
- ROOT CAUSE (overflow): the player list used a CSS Grid (`gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"`) with `overflowY: auto`. A grid track's implicit minimum width is its content's intrinsic (unwrapped) width — a long name like "Nila Vyshnavi Subhashchandra Nair" forced its column wider than its `1fr` share, pushing the whole grid (and its own scrollbar) past the 400px modal's right edge. This is the classic CSS Grid "blowout" failure mode (the fix is normally `minmax(0, 1fr)`, but a single-column list sidesteps it entirely and leaves room to show the brand name too).
- ROOT CAUSE (blank avatars): the fallback avatar rendered the raw `s.avatar` field, which is only populated for a handful of hand-seeded mock accounts (`data.ts`) — every player synced in from Mission Control has `avatar: p.avatar || ''`, i.e. blank, since Mission Control never asks a host to type in 2-letter initials. Blank `avatar` + no `image` rendered as an empty colored square.
- FIX (`app/admin/coins/page.tsx`, Grant Modal):
  - Player picker rebuilt as a single-column scrollable list (flex column, `overflowY: auto`, `overflowX: hidden`) instead of the 2-column grid — removes the blowout failure mode entirely.
  - Each row now shows the player's real name AND brand name (brand name shown as a muted second line, only when it differs from the real name) — both truncated with ellipsis instead of wrapping/overflowing, so a long name can never blow out the row width again.
  - Avatar: shows the uploaded `image` when present (unchanged); when absent, now shows INITIALS COMPUTED FROM THE PLAYER'S OWN NAME (brandName preferred, falling back to name, first letter of the first two words, uppercased, `"?"` for no name at all) instead of the unreliable raw `avatar` field — matches the "initials as normal" fallback already used elsewhere in the app (X-Coin leaderboard, per commit 5f27129) rather than introducing a new convention.
- Files: `pflx-xcoin-app/app/admin/coins/page.tsx` only.
- NOTE: this repo's local Mac clone was ~20 commits behind `origin/main` (the last local commit predated a run of recent pushes — sidebar, ticker, studios, leaderboard, and other fixes). Rebased cleanly onto `origin/main` before pushing — no conflicts, verified the Grant Modal edit survived the rebase intact before pushing.
- Verified: `esbuild` transform of the full file (JSX/TSX syntax, `--jsx=automatic`) completes cleanly — confirms no unbalanced tags/braces from the edit (a full `tsc` typecheck wasn't run since this sandbox doesn't have the project's `node_modules`/type declarations installed; the syntax-level check plus a clean Vercel production build together cover what that would have added here). 8 vm-based test scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted initials-computation fragment, all PASS — brandName preferred over name; falls back to name when no brandName; single-word names yield one letter; long multi-word names only take the first two words' initials; empty/whitespace-only names fall back to "?"; missing name+brandName falls back to "?"; lowercase names are uppercased. Vercel deployment `dpl_83nJtbuL1oV5f8rtJiW9fCZ8zXyc` confirmed `readyState: READY` on commit `5ad7c02`, aliased to production `pflx-xcoin-app.vercel.app`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.59 — DIGITAL BADGE DATA CORRUPTION FIXED (24 PLAYERS REPAIRED), BADGE ARTWORK IN EDIT PLAYER, DEFAULT PORTFOLIO/LOGO TASKS ON CHECKPOINTS (Aug 13, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis reported the Edit Player modal's "Digital Badges" list showed the literal text "[Object Object]" instead of a badge name, with no image, for several players (Vybe/Eden Johnson among them) — and that badges awarded to Vybe/Spark weren't reflected correctly.
- ROOT CAUSE (data corruption, active + ongoing): `_mcMergePlayers()` (the function that reconciles a player record when a local device and a cloud sync disagree) deduped each player's `badges` array with `bset[x] = 1` — for a STRING badge id this is fine, but for a rich badge OBJECT ({id,name,type,xc,awardedAt} — the shape used by Edit Player's "AWARD BADGE" form and by the X-Coin→MC badge-award bridge), using the object directly as a JS object-property key silently coerces it via `.toString()`, producing the literal key `"[object Object]"`. Every distinct badge object a player earned this way collapsed into that one bogus string on the next roster merge, permanently destroying the real badge name/id. This is NOT legacy/dead code — it runs on every player sync — and had already corrupted **24 players'** `badges` arrays in production (Vybe, Spark's roster-mate NEUROFLUX, C1RC3, CODECRAFTER, KABIR, and 19 others), which is why hosts saw blank/garbled badge names across Player Management.
- DATA SURGERY (Supabase, project `hyxiagexyptzvetqjmnj`): stripped every literal `"[object Object]"` string element out of `badges` arrays in (1) `app_data.pflx_mc_players.data.items[]` (24 players affected) and (2) any standalone `app_data.pflx_player_<id>` row (2 affected: Rumaisah Bilquies, Eden Johnson/VYBE). Ran as a single transaction; verified 0 remaining `"[object Object]"` entries afterward and confirmed the `pflx_mc_players` item count stayed at 140 (nothing else was touched). The specific badge identity behind each stripped entry is unrecoverable — hosts who want an exact badge back on an affected player's profile should re-grant it via Edit Player → AWARD BADGE (see Host Actions).
- CODE FIX 1 (`_mcMergePlayers`, ~line 24491): dedup now keys by an explicit identity (`badge.id || badge.name || JSON.stringify(badge)`), never by coercing the object itself into a key, and stores the ORIGINAL badge value (object or string) back into the merged array — never the coerced key string. When the same badge exists as both a bare id string on one side and a rich object on the other, the richer object wins. This stops the corruption from recurring.
- CODE FIX 2 (`pmBadgeNormalize` / `pmBadgeIdToName`, ~line 65464): added a defensive guard — if a stored badge is somehow still the literal string `"[object X]"` (a stale client re-pushing pre-fix data before it picks up CODE FIX 1), it now displays as "Unknown Badge" instead of re-showing the raw artifact.
- CODE FIX 3 (badge artwork, same functions): Edit Player's "DIGITAL BADGES" list never showed any image or icon for a badge, uploaded artwork or not — `pmBadgeNormalize()` now resolves each badge against the live catalog (`mcFindBadge()`) and `renderBadgeListHtml()` shows the catalog's uploaded image when set, else its emoji icon, in a small swatch next to each badge row.
- NEW — DEFAULT CHECKPOINT TASKS (Ennis: "Add a task to Checkpoint Alpha to Upload a Brand logo image... Add a Portfolio updating task to Checkpoint Beta. Players should be subtasked to add their bio, and other details and then publish. This should be a task to update for every Checkpoint. Make this happen by default."): `pflxScaffoldProgram()` (the existing "Scaffold Program" host action that creates the 10 named Alpha…Omega checkpoints) now also seeds, per checkpoint, a standing "Update Your Portfolio" task with a 3-item subtask checklist (Add your bio / Add your other profile details / Publish your portfolio) — on EVERY program checkpoint, not just Beta. Checkpoint Alpha additionally gets a one-time "Upload a Brand Logo Image" task. Seeding is idempotent (matched by title per-checkpoint via `roundId`/`checkpointId`), so re-running Scaffold Program on an already-built program just backfills whichever checkpoints predate this default — safe to click again.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 58→59, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified four ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) 12 jsdom/vm scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted `_mcMergePlayers` — distinct object badges union without stringification; same badge as object on both sides dedupes to one; a bare-string + rich-object pair for the same id dedupes with the object winning; plain string-id badges still union correctly (no regression); `digitalBadges` count reflects the corrected union size; no-badges-either-side doesn't crash; a brand-new player's badges pass through untouched — all PASS. (3) 13 scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted `pmBadgeNormalize`/`pmBadgeIdToName` — corrupted `"[object Object]"`/`"[object Array]"` literals show as "Unknown Badge"; normal `badge-*` ids still Title-Case correctly; own image beats catalog image; catalog image/icon used when the badge has none of its own; string-shaped badges resolve catalog artwork by id; missing `mcFindBadge` doesn't throw — all PASS. (4) 20 scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted `_pflxSeedDefaultCheckpointTasks`/`_pflxMakeDefaultTask` — Alpha seeds both tasks (2), Beta seeds only the Portfolio task (1); Portfolio task has the correct 3 subtask labels and links to its checkpoint via `roundId`; re-seeding an already-seeded checkpoint adds 0 (idempotent); two different checkpoints each get their own Portfolio task despite sharing a title; a pre-existing task matched via the legacy `checkpointId` field is respected; a retitled/differently-cased "Alpha" checkpoint still gets the logo task; null/id-less input doesn't throw — all PASS. Also directly queried Supabase after the data surgery to confirm 0 corrupted entries remain and the player count is unchanged.
- HOST ACTIONS: (1) click "Scaffold Program" once (Programs/Checkpoints panel) to backfill the new default Portfolio/Brand-Logo tasks onto the existing Alpha…Omega checkpoints — safe to click even though the program already exists, it only adds what's missing. (2) For any of the 24 players whose corrupted badge entry was stripped (Vybe/Eden Johnson, Spark's neighbors NEUROFLUX/C1RC3/CODECRAFTER/KABIR and 20 others — full list in this session's chat log), the original badge name is unrecoverable; re-grant via Edit Player → AWARD BADGE if that player should still have credit for it.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.21 — X-COIN FEED: STOPPED DOUBLE-POSTING BADGE GRANTS TO DISCORD/SLACK (Aug 13, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — a screenshot of #pflx-xcoin-feed on Discord showed the same badge grant (VYBE earning "AI App Developer") posted TWICE: a rich "🏅 Badge Awarded" embed card, immediately followed by a second plain-text "[PFLX-XCOIN-FEED] X-Bot: 🏅 [BADGE EARNED] @VYBE earned "AI App Developer" ... via SUBMISSION Administrator Grant" message with a `pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app/badge/sub-grant-...` link. "That is not necessary. The 'Badge Awarded' post is good enough."
- ROOT CAUSE: two independent systems both notice the SAME grant. X-Coin's admin Grant flow (`coins/page.tsx handleGrantCoin`, and the bulk grant on `admin/page.tsx`) does two things when a host grants a badge: (1) calls `notifyBadgeAwarded()` which posts the rich embed straight to Discord/Slack via webhook — this is message #1, and (2) writes an "approved" submission record (`reason: "Administrator Grant"`) purely for audit history. DarkCampus's `badge-feed` route (this repo) independently scans `transactions` + `submissions` every 10 minutes via Vercel Cron (and on live events) looking for badge earns it hasn't posted yet — it has no idea X-Coin already announced this one, sees that same "Administrator Grant" submission record, and posts its own plain-text version — message #2 — to the identical Discord channel (`isRewardFeedName()` matches the same `#pflx-xcoin-feed`-style channel both systems target).
- FIX (`badge-feed/route.ts`, `postBadgeRecord()`): disabled step 3 (the external Discord/Slack bridge — `findRewardFeedChannels()` + `sendToDiscord`/`sendToSlack`). DarkCampus still does everything else it did before — writes the event into its own Terminal channel feed (`dc_messages_mc-xcoin-feed`, so the in-app ticker and #Terminal still show it), and still writes the `dc_badge_feed` registry record so the public `/badge/<id>` share page (used for the LinkedIn share action) keeps working. Only the redundant external post is gone; X-Coin's own embed is now the single source of truth for badge grants on Discord/Slack.
- Files: `pflx-darkcampus/src/app/api/badge-feed/route.ts` only.
- Verified two ways: (1) `esbuild` transform of the file completes cleanly (no syntax errors from the edit; a full `tsc` typecheck wasn't run since this sandbox doesn't have the project's `node_modules` installed). (2) 13 test scenarios against the ACTUAL route file (transpiled to CJS via esbuild, run in Node with a mocked in-memory Supabase store and a mocked `global.fetch` that records every call) — granting a badge via the live "event" path succeeds and reports `bridgedTo: []`, and NO fetch call is made to `discord.com` or `slack.com`; the Terminal feed message and share-page registry record are still written exactly as before; posting the same event id twice still dedupes (second call reports `posted:false`, registry doesn't grow); a full ledger `sync` pass (the Vercel Cron path) over a mix of transaction- and submission-sourced badge earns also posts 0 external bridge calls while still recording both candidates — all PASS. Confirmed live on production: commit `a8d4892`, Vercel deployment `dpl_4W1VS9JRddHx22TNJkHswDsEUDRC` `readyState: READY`, aliased to `pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.22 — ACCOUNT LINKING FIXED: LIVE-CLAIM ON POLL INSTEAD OF WAITING ON THE 5X/DAY CRON (Aug 13, Ennis)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis — "this linking system isnt working," with two screenshots: Mission Control's "LINK YOUR ACCOUNT" modal for player IMPACT showing code `/link H5UT6` ("expires in 30 minutes... waiting for you to post it..."), and a Discord DM between LUMINA and IMPACT where IMPACT posts `/link H5UT6` twice in #general-chat and concludes "yeah i dont think its working," with LUMINA replying she'd already reported the same failure in the FeedForward form. `PFLX_COMMS_SPEC_v1.md` §3 independently confirmed this was systemic, not an edge case: "Current state: 4 of ~45 linked."
- ROOT CAUSE (timing mismatch, not a regex/logic bug): `LinkGate.tsx`'s modal polls `GET /api/link-account?playerId=...` every 5 seconds while a code is displayed — its own doc comment says "the overlay polls and dismisses itself the moment the claim lands," implying the poll was built to feel live. But the GET handler was purely passive (a read-only lookup against `dc_member_links`); the ONLY thing that ever wrote a claim was the `xbot-scan` Vercel Cron job, which runs ~5 times a day (roughly every 4.8 hours). Link codes expire in `CODE_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000` (30 minutes). A player who posts `/link <code>` in Discord has, on average, no chance of the cron catching it before the code expires — the UI was polling a well the cron almost never filled in time. (Ruled out first: hand-tested `LINK_CODE_RE`/`detectLinkCode()` directly in Node against the exact codes from both screenshots — the regex matches correctly; the bug is architectural, not a parsing bug.)
- FIX (`link-account/route.ts`): extracted the cron's claim logic into a shared `claimCode(code, platform, platformUserId)` helper (guarantees the live path and the cron path can never disagree on what counts as a valid claim), then added `tryLiveClaimForPlayer(playerId)` — on every `GET`, if the requesting player has an outstanding unexpired code, it live-scans the same Discord channels the cron watches (`general-chat`, `pflx-terminal`, `introductions`) for a recent non-bot message matching that exact code and claims it inline via `claimCode()`, all before answering the poll. This closes the gap between "UI polls every 5s expecting a live claim" (already true) and "nothing was actually live" (now fixed) by reusing the polling infrastructure `LinkGate.tsx` already had, rather than depending on the cron running more often (which is Vercel-plan-limited and would still leave a multi-minute gap). The 5x/day cron scan is left in place as a fallback/catch-all for anyone who links while no host has the modal open. Fails closed at every step — no Discord config, an unreachable Discord API, an expired code, a bot-authored message, or a wrong/unrelated code in the channel all resolve to a normal "not yet linked" response, never a thrown error.
- Files: `pflx-darkcampus/src/app/api/link-account/route.ts` only.
- Verified two ways: (1) `esbuild` transform of the file completes cleanly (no syntax errors from the edit; a full `tsc` typecheck wasn't run since this sandbox doesn't have the project's `node_modules` installed). (2) 16 test scenarios against the ACTUAL route file (transpiled to CJS via esbuild, run in Node with a mocked in-memory Supabase store, a stub `resolveDiscordToken`, and a mocked `global.fetch` recording every call) — issuing a code still works and returns a valid 5-char code; polling before anything is posted reports unlinked with no error; THE CORE FIX: a single poll cycle after `/link <code>` is posted in Discord claims it live, with no cron involved, exactly matching the IMPACT/LUMINA scenario; a second poll after claiming makes zero further Discord calls; a wrong/unrelated code in chat never claims the real one, and the real code still claims correctly afterward; bot-authored messages posting a code are ignored; an expired outstanding code is treated as nothing-to-claim with no Discord call and no crash; a host with no Discord configured gets a clean "unlinked," never a throw; a Discord API failure mid-live-check doesn't break the regular GET response — all 16 PASS. Confirmed live on production: commit `ecb1298`, Vercel deployment `dpl_ArR3UmvAmx1G7BiUUhUXy8DXBcAM`, `readyState: READY`, aliased to `pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Testers who hit this (IMPACT, LUMINA, and anyone else who reported a failed `/link` in the FeedForward form) should simply try linking again — a fresh code request now claims live within one 5-second poll cycle of posting it in Discord, instead of waiting on the cron.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.60 — HOME BASE TASK/CHECKPOINT DESYNC ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (Aug 13, Ennis-approved, from the FeedForward triage)
- SYMPTOM: by far the most-reported issue across the Aug 13 FeedForward triage (~30 of 86 backlogged submissions, spanning July 22 → Aug 12, nearly every active tester: Kabir, Feba, Alivia, Ayrene, Abeal, Hannah, Kaitlin, Eva, Essence, Aadhya, Kaavya) — Home Base (the player's dashboard: the "MY TASKS" card, the X-Bot Briefing's "you have N tasks remaining" line, the active-checkpoint hero's progress bar and "Next Up" strip) shows a task or checkpoint as NOT done — "0/3", "3 tasks remaining", "0% complete" — while the Tasks page and Checkpoint Detail page, for the exact same work, correctly show it approved and complete. Several reports (Kaavya's CodeCrafter cohort) show the same class of miscount on the HOST side too.
- ROOT CAUSE: `ppRenderHome()`'s task-completion check read the task's top-level `t.status === 'approved'` field directly. For a COHORT-assigned task (the normal case — a task shared across a cohort, tracked per-player via `task.submissions[]`), `mcApproveTask()` only ever flips that top-level field to `'approved'` once `_mcTaskHostComplete()` is true — i.e. once **every** assigned player has been individually approved (by design, per the July 15 fix: one player's approval must not close the task for the whole cohort). A host approving testers one at a time — the normal workflow — means that top-level field stays un-flipped for potentially days while individual players are approved one by one. `ppRenderMyTasks()` (the Tasks page) and `ppRenderCheckpointDetail()` (fixed July 23 for the analogous cohort-aggregate-vs-player bug) already read the correct PER-PLAYER state via `pflxTaskStateForPlayer(task, playerId)` — Home Base was the one surface still reading the raw shared field, so a player's own long-since-approved work permanently read as incomplete on their dashboard specifically, while every other page they clicked into showed it correctly. A second, smaller instance of the same top-level-field mistake sat in the checkpoint hero's "Next Up" task list. A related but separate bug: the Checkpoints nav card's progress bar read `checkpoint.progress`, a field that is never actually written anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep across the full file) — that card has always shown a flat 0% regardless of real progress.
- FIX (`ppRenderHome()`, ~line 27406 and ~27497): both task-completion filters (the MY TASKS / X-Bot Briefing counts, and the checkpoint hero's Next Up list) now route through a shared `__homeTaskDone(t)` helper that calls `pflxTaskStateForPlayer(t, playerId)` — the same function the Tasks and Checkpoint Detail pages already trust — instead of reading `t.status` directly. The Checkpoints nav card (~line 27638) now computes its progress bar via `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress()` (the same call `ppRenderCheckpointDetail` already makes for players) instead of the always-empty `checkpoint.progress` field. All three keep a defensive fallback to the old behavior if the helper functions are somehow unavailable, so this can't newly crash Home Base.
- SCOPE NOTE: this fixes the Home-vs-other-views DISAGREEMENT specifically — the dominant, best-evidenced pattern in the triage. It does not by itself address every flavor of "progress reset to 0% and came back" report (a handful of testers describe genuine flip-flopping, not just a stale display) — those may share a root cause with the still-open Aug 9 Handoff investigation ("APPROVALS DISAPPEAR WHEN I APPROVE 1", stale-tab merge race, never confirmed) and are worth re-checking against tester reports after this ships, since this fix may have already resolved some of them as a side effect of no longer trusting the top-level field.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 59→60, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) 7 scenarios (8 checks) run against the ACTUAL extracted `pflxTaskStateForPlayer` (unmodified) plus the patched Home Base counting logic verbatim as it now ships — a solo/legacy task with no `submissions[]` still counts correctly (regression guard); **the core bug scenario, run against the OLD logic first to prove it reproduces exactly what testers reported (my own approved cohort submission reads as 0% done) and then against the NEW logic to prove it's fixed (100% done)**; the still-pending cohort-mate correctly still sees the task as not done from their own view; a fully-approved cohort task (top-level status legitimately flipped) still reads done, no regression; a rejected submission is correctly not counted done; a mixed 3-task set counts 2/3 (67%) correctly; an empty task list doesn't divide by zero — all PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none — this is a pure read-side fix, no data migration. Worth telling the ~11 testers behind the 30 duplicate reports (see the Aug 13 FeedForward triage file) that Home Base should now agree with the rest of the platform, and asking them to confirm.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.61 — MISSION CONTROL CARD-SIZE SLIDERS (Seasons/Programs/Checkpoints/Projects/Tasks) (Aug 13, Ennis-requested)
- FEATURE: Ennis asked for a way to resize the card grid on each of the five main Mission Control tabs — Seasons, Programs, Checkpoints, Projects, Tasks — independently, while looking at the Checkpoints tab (Alpha at 33%, Beta at 10%) and wanting denser or larger cards depending on cohort size / screen size. Each tab now has a small "🖰 Card Size" slider docked just above its card list; dragging it live-resizes every card on that tab instantly, and the chosen size is remembered per-tab across visits/tab-switches.
- MECHANISM: one shared CSS custom property, `--pflx-card-min`, set on each tab's list container and referenced by every `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--pflx-card-min, <default>px), 1fr))` on that tab (including nested per-bucket/per-season sub-grids where a tab groups cards into sections) — so a single cheap `style.setProperty()` call resizes an entire tab's cards, however many grids it's actually built from, without touching card markup. New shared helper block (~line 30920, before `mcRenderCheckpoints`): `PFLX_CARD_SIZE_DEFAULTS` / `PFLX_CARD_SIZE_RANGE` / `PFLX_CARD_SIZE_LIST_ID` config, `pflxCardSizes()`/`pflxCardSize(key)` (read, with localStorage `pflx_mc_card_sizes` + safe fallback to defaults on corrupt/missing/invalid data), `pflxLiveResizeCards(key, px)` (drag-time — CSS var + label text only, no re-render, so the native `<input type=range>` drag gesture is never interrupted by its own DOM node being recreated mid-drag), `pflxSetCardSize(key, px)` (drag-release — persists to localStorage, also no re-render), `pflxApplyCardSize(key)` (applies the persisted size on render — called once near the top of each of the 5 `mcRender*` functions), `pflxCardSizeSliderHtml(key, label)` (builds the slider control, dropped into a `mc-<tab>-sizer` div that sits above each tab's list).
- LAYOUT CHANGES: 3 of the 5 tabs (Programs, Seasons, Tasks) previously used a flex-column "row list" layout rather than a grid — their card wrappers were converted to `display:grid` using `var(--pflx-card-min, ...)` (Checkpoints and Projects were already grids and only needed the var swapped into their existing `minmax(...)`). Verified by reading the card markup for all 5 types that each card is a self-contained box (own background/border/border-radius), so converting flex-column → grid is a pure layout change, not a card redesign. Per-tab default card-min widths were chosen to roughly match each type's existing footprint: Checkpoints 560px (hero-tier, range 380–900), Seasons 900px (range 420–1400), Tasks 900px (range 420–1400, full-width rows before), Programs 520px (range 320–900), Projects 380px (range 260–640).
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 60→61, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) 10 scenarios (29 checks) run against the ACTUAL extracted card-size helper functions verbatim as they now ship, with a minimal DOM/localStorage stub: all 5 tabs default correctly with no persisted override; `pflxApplyCardSize` sets the CSS var correctly on first render for all 5 list containers; drag-time (`pflxLiveResizeCards`) updates the CSS var + px label instantly WITHOUT touching localStorage; drag-release (`pflxSetCardSize`) persists and a fresh read picks it up; multiple live ticks followed by one release persist only the final value; a persisted override survives a later `pflxApplyCardSize` call (e.g. switching back to a resized tab); corrupt localStorage JSON falls back to defaults without throwing; zero/negative/non-numeric override values are rejected in favor of the default; the slider HTML reflects the persisted value, the correct per-tab range bounds, and wires `oninput`/`onchange` to the correct helper + key; resizing one tab never bleeds into another tab's stored size — all PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none — the slider is purely client-side (`localStorage`), no data migration, no Supabase changes.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.62 — BADGE CORRUPTION RECURRENCE FIXED (23 PLAYERS RE-CORRUPTED ONE DAY AFTER v1.59), X-COIN GRANT AMOUNT NOW CLAMPED (Aug 14, from the FeedForward XC_CREDIT/COURSE_REWARD investigation)
- CONTEXT: "move on to the next item" after v1.60/v1.61 pointed at the FeedForward triage's #2 cluster, XC_CREDIT/COURSE_REWARD (~15 submissions) — approved tasks/Battle Arena wins never crediting XC (Ayrene, Aadhya, Bijo), plus Hannah Rodrigues's Story Builder course consistently over-crediting by ~10x while never awarding the badge, reported 4 separate times (8/7, 8/8, 8/9, 8/10). Per the triage's own recommendation, checked her player row in Supabase directly before guessing at the reward code.
- KEY FINDING #1 — Hannah's XC delta is NOT repeating: her live Supabase record (`pflx_mc_players`, id `player-1784132285251-35nwi`, brand IMPACT) shows `xc: 7550` right now — the exact SAME number reported on 8/7, 8/8, 8/9, and 8/10. If the platform were re-crediting her every time she reported it, the number would climb each time; it didn't. This was ONE over-credit event that happened once (between her 8/6 report of "0 XC, no badge" and her 8/7 report of "5,500→7,550 XC, no badge"), which nothing ever corrected, and she kept re-reporting the still-broken state. This reframes the whole cluster: it's not an automated re-triggering bug, so the fix effort shifted to finding what actually produced that one event and why the badge never landed.
- KEY FINDING #2 (the actual bug, confirmed and fixed) — her `badges[]` array contained the literal string `"[object Object]"` as one of its 7 entries: the exact fossil the Aug 13 v1.59 patch documented and supposedly fixed (`_mcMergePlayers` coercing a rich badge object into a string key during roster merge). Querying ALL of `pflx_mc_players` turned up **23 players** with this same corrupted literal RIGHT NOW — one day after v1.59 claimed "confirmed 0 remaining corrupted entries" — including several never named in the original 24 (e.g. Kaavya Singh/VYATECH, Sarah Bose/PASSIONSTUDIOS, Callia Chon, erica jalili). ROOT CAUSE of the recurrence: v1.59's `_mcMergePlayers` fix stops NEW corruption from being CREATED (keys by explicit id/name identity instead of coercing the object), but it never stripped an ALREADY-corrupted literal string sitting in one side's `badges[]` — a bare string just unions through like any other id. Any device that cached a player's pre-Aug-13 corrupted `badges` array and hadn't synced since kept re-merging that literal straight back into the cloud roster on every subsequent sync, silently undoing the Aug 13 cleanup one stale client at a time. v1.59's own CODE FIX 2 (`pmBadgeIdToName`/`pmBadgeNormalize` showing "Unknown Badge" for the literal) anticipated exactly this "stale client re-pushing pre-fix data" scenario but only patched the DISPLAY side, not the merge itself — this is very likely why Hannah's Story Builder badge award (whatever produced the corrupted entry) never resolved into a real badge name: it kept losing the race to a stale re-merge.
- FIX (`_mcMergePlayers`, ~line 24548): the badge-union loop now drops any array element that is a string matching `/^\[object \w+\]$/i` (same detection pattern `pmBadgeIdToName` already uses) BEFORE keying it into the dedup set, so a stale client's corrupted literal can never be unioned back into a clean roster again. Also fixed a real bug the new unit test caught while writing it: the old `if (badges.length) merged.badges = badges;` guard meant a player whose badges array contained ONLY the corrupted literal — union result now correctly empty — kept the STALE pre-union corrupted array anyway, because `Object.assign({}, lose, win)` earlier in the function already copied the winning side's raw (corrupted) `badges` field, and the length-0 guard skipped overwriting it. Changed to assign whenever either side actually had a `badges` array (`badges.length || Array.isArray(a.badges) || Array.isArray(b.badges)`), so a real "strip everything corrupted" case correctly clears to `[]`.
- DATA SURGERY (Supabase, project `hyxiagexyptzvetqjmnj`, single transaction): stripped the literal `"[object Object]"` (and the same-family `"[object X]"` pattern) out of `badges[]` for all 23 currently-affected players in `pflx_mc_players.data.items[]`, and the 1 currently-affected standalone `pflx_player_<id>` row (Eden Johnson/VYBE — the same player fixed standalone in v1.59, now re-corrupted, confirming the recurrence mechanism). `digitalBadges` (a stored count, not computed live) was decremented by exactly the number of corrupted entries removed from that specific player's own array — never touched for any player whose array had no corruption. Verified after: 0 remaining corrupted entries in either location, `pflx_mc_players` item count unchanged at 140 (nothing else touched). Hannah's row specifically: `badges` now `["badge-digital-tool-master","badge-resilient-learner","badge-self-directed-player","badge-positive-participant","badge-pflx-user-certification","badge-personal-branding-level-1"]` (6, clean), `digitalBadges` corrected 7→6. Her `xc`/`totalXcoin` were left untouched — see Still Open below.
- ALSO FIXED (defensive hardening, `pflx-xcoin-app/app/admin/coins/page.tsx handleGrantCoin` + its Amount input): the admin "Grant Badge" modal's Amount field had `min="1" max="100"` as HTML attributes only — cosmetic, never enforced, since the modal's onChange did a bare `parseInt(...) || 1` with no clamp, and the Grant button calls `handleGrantCoin()` directly rather than through native form validation. `totalXcReward = coin.xc * amount` therefore had NO upper bound in practice — a stray keystroke, paste, or scroll-wheel tick on a focused number input could multiply a badge's XC value by an arbitrary amount with nothing stopping the grant from going through. Flagging this as a PLAUSIBLE mechanism for Hannah's ~10x overcredit (a badge worth ~20 XC at `amount=100`, the field's own advertised ceiling, already lands at 2000 XC — close to her observed +2050 delta) — NOT a confirmed cause, since there's no accessible admin action log to confirm what was actually clicked around 8/6–8/7. Now clamps to `[1,100]` in both the input's `onChange` and again inside `handleGrantCoin` itself (defense-in-depth, doesn't trust a single guard).
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` (`PFLX_PATCH` 61→62, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged 2026.08), `pflx-xcoin-app/app/admin/coins/page.tsx`.
- Verified: (1) syntax gate clean on preview.html (13/13 blocks). (2) `tsc --noEmit` on the edited X-Coin file surfaces zero TS1xxx syntax errors (only expected missing-module/missing-React-types noise from checking a single file outside its project — no parse errors in or near the edited regions). (3) 10 scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted `_mcMergePlayers` verbatim: a corrupted literal from a stale LOCAL copy is stripped and not unioned back in; the same from the INCOMING/cloud side; other `"[object X]"` constructor-name variants are also caught; a rich-object + bare-string pair for the same badge id still dedupes correctly with the object winning (v1.59 regression guard); two genuinely distinct rich badge objects still union to 2 entries without collapsing (the ORIGINAL v1.59 bug, regression guard); a badges array containing ONLY the corrupted literal correctly ends up empty (the length-guard bug this test caught and got fixed before shipping); no badges on either side doesn't crash; a brand-new player passes through untouched — all PASS. (4) 11 scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted Grant-modal clamp logic (both the onChange clamp and `handleGrantCoin`'s defense-in-depth clamp): normal values pass through; a value of 1000 (the suspected Hannah-scenario magnitude) clamps to 100; exactly-100 stays 100; zero/negative clamp up to 1; empty/garbage input falls back to 1; a pasted huge number is clamped not passed through raw; `handleGrantCoin` independently re-clamps even if something bypassed the input; NaN/undefined amount falls back to 1; end-to-end, a 20-XC badge with a runaway amount now tops out at 2000 XC instead of 20000 — all PASS. (5) Directly re-queried Supabase after the data surgery to confirm 0 corrupted entries remain anywhere and the player count is unchanged.
- STILL OPEN (continuing next): (1) Hannah's actual `xc`/`totalXcoin` (7550/8750) were NOT reverted — I don't have an admin action log to confirm whether the ~2050 XC overcredit was a genuine bug or a host's intentional (if oversized) manual compensation grant; needs Ennis's judgment, not a silent code-driven rollback of a player's balance. (2) Discovered a SPLIT-BRAIN between Hannah's `pflx_mc_players` roster copy (xc 7550, totalXcoin 8750, the 1200 gap consistent with her reported Chrono Extend Booster purchases) and her standalone `pflx_player_player-1784132285251-35nwi` row (xc 7550, totalXcoin **7550** — equal, meaning that copy never recorded the spend or the overcredit's totalXcoin bump) — the two sources of truth actively disagree and neither this patch nor v1.59 addressed why they drift; worth its own investigation, likely related to the existing "Schema splits" gotcha (MC vs X-Coin field conventions). (3) The OTHER XC_CREDIT flavor — approved tasks / Battle Arena wins never crediting XC at all (Ayrene, Aadhya, Bijo) — is NOT yet root-caused. Leading hypothesis for next session: `PflxDataBus.award()` (preview.html ~63631) silently no-ops with only a `console.warn` when `playerId` doesn't match any live `PLAYERS` record — worth checking whether Ayrene's/Aadhya's/Bijo's submission `playerId`/session id actually matches their canonical `PLAYERS.id` at award time, especially across the MC-roster-vs-standalone-row split found in (2). (4) COURSE_REWARD specifically: `pathway.html`'s Storyboarding node config (`xcReward: 200`, confirmed correct in source) is NOT what paid Hannah 2050 — the actual payout mechanism for her event is still unidentified (candidates: a manual X-Coin admin grant per the Amount-clamp finding above, or a pre-v1.48 pending submission that got approved through the OLD badge-catalog-value path described in v1.48's Handoff entry before the new node-aware Approvals Queue caught it) — needs Ennis to recall or look up what actually happened around 8/6–8/7 on his end, since no accessible audit trail confirms it from here.
- HOST ACTIONS: (1) for the 23 players whose corrupted badge entry was just stripped a second time, same as v1.59 — the original badge identity behind each is unrecoverable; re-grant via Edit Player → AWARD BADGE if a player should still have credit for it (full list: Essence Johnson/NEUROFLUX, Kaavya Singh/VYATECH, Sarah Bose/PASSIONSTUDIOS, Aadhya Khanna/C1RC3, Callia Chon, Rumaisah Bilquies/RUM, erica jalili, Sam Chen/CODECRAFTER, Kareem Bahei-Eldin/SPHINX LINK, Safa Parveen K R, Nirmal Sudheesh/1LLU510N15T, Ayrene Arun/IRENJ3PG, Alivia Vimal/LIVSTUDIOS, Niya Benoy, Eva Jojo/AVA, Bijo/BIJO, Kaitlin Francis, Abeal Kulangara Thomas/LUMINA, Kabir Grover, Hannah Rodrigues/IMPACT, Mariya Jomon/MARIQUE, Feba/LU3UR, Eden Johnson/VYBE). (2) Ennis's call on Hannah's XC balance — leave at 7550/8750 as an intentional-if-oversized grant, or manually adjust; I did not touch it. (3) If Ennis remembers manually granting Hannah XC/badges around 8/6–8/7 via the X-Coin admin panel, that would confirm finding (4) above and close COURSE_REWARD as "host action, not a code bug" — worth a 30-second gut check before the next session spends more time chasing it as code.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.63 — DIFFICULTY_LOCK ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: TIER PICK NEVER REACHED THE PLATFORM'S OWN SSO-URL BUILDER (Aug 14, from the FeedForward priority list)
- CONTEXT: continuing down the recommended FeedForward priority order after TASK_SYNC (v1.60), the card-size sliders (v1.61), and XC_CREDIT/COURSE_REWARD (v1.62) — item #3, DIFFICULTY_LOCK: "Core Pathways always opens Novice regardless of Starter/Pro selection," reported 7 times by Hannah Rodrigues alone plus Mariya Jomon, spanning the full 3 weeks, described in the triage as "100% consistent" and "reads like a single, findable bug."
- SYMPTOM: a player picks Starter or Pro on the Detail Panel's difficulty picker inside Core Pathways (`pathway.html`) — the pick visibly takes (pill highlights, persists within that session) — but the next time they enter Core Pathways (new tab, page refresh, revisiting the app after using another tab), it's back to Novice, as if the choice was never saved.
- ROOT CAUSE — a cross-origin write that never reached its read: `pathway.html` (served from `pflx-pathway-portal.vercel.app`) and the Platform/Console shell (`preview.html`, served from `prototypeflx.com`/`pflx-platform.vercel.app`) are DIFFERENT origins, so `localStorage` is NOT shared between them — a browser fundamental, not a PFLX bug per se. `pathway.html`'s tier picker correctly writes the pick to ITS OWN origin's `localStorage['pflx_player_tier']` (fine for reads that happen *inside* that same pathway.html session) and ALSO correctly announces the change to its parent via `postMessage({type:'pflx_tier_change', playerId, from, to, ...})` — this postMessage bridge is exactly the mechanism that should close the cross-origin gap. But the Platform's listener for `pflx_tier_change` (preview.html, added when tier history/audit logging was built) only ever wrote the pick onto the CLOUD PLAYER RECORD (`tp.tier`, persisted via `mcSaveData('players')`) — it never updated `activeSession.tier` or the Platform's OWN origin's `localStorage['pflx_player_tier']`. Those are the ONLY two things `buildAppURL()` (the function that builds the SSO iframe `src` for Core Pathways, embedding tier as a URL param that `pathway.html`'s own tier-resolver checks FIRST, ahead of its local storage) and `_ppPlayerTier()` (the Portal-side tier-variant resolver used for checkpoint reward overrides) ever read. Compounding it: `activeSession` itself never carried a `tier` field to begin with — the login flow's session-construction object explicitly copies a long list of player fields ("Copy ALL host-editable fields... not just identity") but `tier` was missing from that list, and the separate `buildPlayerSession()` used by host mimic-mode had the same gap. Net effect: every SSO URL rebuild for Core Pathways — a fresh login, a tab revisit, any full iframe reload — was built from a tier value that had structurally never been written to since account creation, so it silently defaulted to `novice` every single time, regardless of what the player had picked minutes earlier inside the iframe itself.
- FIX (4 sites, all `pflx-platform/preview.html`):
  1. **Login session construction** (~line 20507): added `tier: player ? (player.tier || 'novice') : 'novice'` alongside the other copied player fields, so a returning player's saved tier is present on `activeSession` from the moment they log in.
  2. **`buildPlayerSession()`** (~line 61449, host mimic-mode): same one-line addition — `tier: p.tier || 'novice'` — so mimicking a player also carries their real tier instead of silently resetting it.
  3. **The `pflx_tier_change` listener** (~line 25484): after the existing `tp.tier = msg.to` (cloud record, unchanged), now ALSO sets `activeSession.tier = msg.to` when the change is for the currently logged-in player, and unconditionally writes `localStorage.setItem('pflx_player_tier', msg.to)` — closing the loop for both readers, live, the moment a pick happens, with no reload required.
  4. **`buildAppURL()`** (~line 15311) and **`_ppPlayerTier()`** (~line 27850): both now check `activeSession.tier` BEFORE falling back to `localStorage` (previously `buildAppURL` checked localStorage only; `_ppPlayerTier` checked URL param then localStorage, skipping activeSession entirely). `activeSession.tier` is the freshest, most-authoritative source now that (1)–(3) keep it current; localStorage remains a defensive fallback, and the DarkCampus `/leaderboard` slash command's viewer-tier lookup — which already correctly preferred `activeSession.tier` — now actually finds a value there instead of always falling through.
- Files: `pflx-platform/preview.html` only. `PFLX_PATCH` 62→63, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged (2026.08).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean (13/13 blocks). (2) 20 scenarios against the ACTUAL extracted logic verbatim from all 4 edited sites: login correctly copies a saved Pro tier onto the session, and safely defaults to novice for a player with no saved tier or no player record at all; mimic-mode session construction copies the mimicked player's tier (or defaults safely); **the core bug, proven directly** — a `pflx_tier_change` message for the CURRENT player now updates both `activeSession.tier` and localStorage (previously only the cloud record), while a tier change broadcast for a DIFFERENT player correctly updates their own record without touching the current session's tier; `buildAppURL`'s resolver prefers a fixed `activeSession.tier` over a stale localStorage value, falls back to localStorage when activeSession has none, and defaults to novice as a last resort; **the full end-to-end repro** — a fresh session starts at novice, the SSO-URL resolver correctly shows novice before any pick (expected), the player picks Pro inside Pathways (the message fires), and the very next SSO-URL resolution now correctly returns 'pro' instead of silently resetting — this is the literal “opens Novice regardless of choice” bug, reproduced and proven fixed; `_ppPlayerTier`'s three-tier priority order (URL param → activeSession → localStorage → novice) holds at every level — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this fixes the tier NOT STICKING ACROSS SSO URL REBUILDS specifically, which is the mechanism that matches "100% consistent, always Novice" exactly. It does not touch `pathway.html` itself (its own picker/local persistence were already correct) or the module-content tier-awareness for the ~2 nodes with an actual `coursePackage` attached (`pflx_mod_init`'s `context.tier` was already wired correctly and is untouched) — those were read, verified correct, and ruled out as part of this investigation, not fixed because they weren't broken.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — pure read/write-path fix, no data migration. Worth telling Hannah and Mariya to try picking their difficulty again and confirm it sticks after leaving and re-entering Core Pathways.

## PATCH XCOIN v1.2 — LINKEDIN CONNECT ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: THE OAUTH LINK WAS NAVIGATING THE EMBEDDED IFRAME, WHICH LINKEDIN REFUSES TO RENDER (Aug 14, from the FeedForward priority list)
- CONTEXT: item #4 on the FeedForward priority list — LINKEDIN connect broken for 3+ weeks, reported 6 times by 2 testers (Abeal x4, Hannah x2), one noting "many people in Discord report the same issue." Never been touched before this session.
- SYMPTOM: clicking "in CONNECT LINKEDIN" in the Wallet's Digital Badge Collection header (X-Coin, `LinkedInConnect.tsx`) landed testers on an error page instead of LinkedIn's consent screen.
- ROOT CAUSE — verified against real production responses, not guessed: X-Coin runs embedded inside `<iframe id="xcoin-frame">` on the Platform shell (`pflx-platform/preview.html` ~line 11330) whenever a player reaches it the normal way, via Mission Control's Launch Apps tiles. The CONNECT LINKEDIN `<a href="/api/linkedin/auth?playerId=...">` had no `target` attribute, so clicking it navigated THAT IFRAME (not the top-level browser tab) — `/api/linkedin/auth` 307-redirects to `linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization`, which redirects again to `linkedin.com/uas/login`. Both LinkedIn responses were captured live via curl on Aug 14 and both carry `x-frame-options: sameorigin` plus a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive (`'self' *.linkedin.com teams.microsoft.com client.learningapp.microsoft.com` on the authorize page; the narrower `'self' *.www.linkedin.com:*` on the login page) — neither allows framing by `prototypeflx.com` / `pflx-platform.vercel.app`. Browsers refuse to render a page inside a frame when its own headers forbid it, so the xcoin-frame iframe went blank/errored instead of showing LinkedIn's login — exactly the reported symptom, and 100% reproducible for every tester since Launch Apps → embedded iframe is the only way anyone reaches X-Coin.
- FIX (`pflx-xcoin-app/app/components/LinkedInConnect.tsx`, the CONNECT LINKEDIN anchor only): added `target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, matching the pattern the badge page's `ShareButtons.tsx` (SHARE ON LINKEDIN / ADD TO PROFILE) already used correctly. A new tab has no frame ancestor at all, so LinkedIn's `frame-ancestors` restriction can't block it — sidesteps the whole problem without needing any change on LinkedIn's side. The "⚡ POST LATEST BADGE" button was untouched — it posts via `fetch()`, which isn't subject to `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors` at all.
- Files: `pflx-xcoin-app/app/components/LinkedInConnect.tsx` only.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` (jsx/target/module flags matching a Next.js 14 project) clean, no `TS1xxx` syntax errors. 12 scenarios in a live-code test: parsed LinkedIn's real captured `frame-ancestors` directives with a minimal matcher and confirmed neither the authorize nor login page allows framing by the Platform's real origins (while confirming the matcher correctly allows LinkedIn's own subdomains and the explicitly-listed Microsoft Teams domains, so it isn't just returning false for everything); confirmed the shipped anchor tag now carries `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` while its href/playerId behavior is unchanged; confirmed `ShareButtons.tsx`'s already-correct links were untouched (regression guard); and a direct old-vs-new simulation showing the old markup would fail to render inside the real Platform iframe while the new markup renders correctly — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this fixes the OAuth "CONNECT LINKEDIN" flow specifically (Phase 2). The zero-API "SHARE ON LINKEDIN" / "ADD TO PROFILE" buttons on the public `/badge/<playerId>` page (Phase 1+3) already had `target="_blank"` and were verified working correctly (confirmed via a live curl to `pflx-xcoin-app.vercel.app/badge/<real playerId>` — renders the actual badge wall, not an error) — not touched because they weren't broken.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — no LinkedIn Developer Portal config change needed, this was purely a same-frame-navigation bug on our side. Worth telling Abeal and Hannah to try CONNECT LINKEDIN again; it now opens a new tab for LinkedIn login/consent, then can be closed to return to the Platform.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.23 — DC_CHAT: RELAY ECHOES NOW ATTRIBUTE TO THE REAL SENDER, HIDDEN DISCORD CONTENT NOW SAYS SO, CHANNEL-SWITCH NO LONGER FREEZES ON STALE MESSAGES (Aug 14, from the FeedForward priority list)
- CONTEXT: item #6 on the FeedForward priority list, DC_CHAT — 4 reports across 3 distinct symptoms, all under the same "DarkCampus↔Discord sync" umbrella: Abeal (8/4) "only sender names show, message text missing"; Kaitlin (8/8, described as a clean repro) "PFLX→Discord shows sender as 'X-Bot' instead of the real name; Discord→PFLX only shows X-Bot messages, real content never arrives"; Abeal (8/8) "switching groups doesn't update messages; eventually all messages/terminals vanish."
- ROOT CAUSE #1 (Abeal 8/4 + half of Kaitlin's report) — CONFIRMED LIVE, not guessed: curled the real production API (`pflx-darkcampus.vercel.app/api/messages?...platform=discord`) for 4 different real Discord channels (general-chat, pflx-terminal, introductions, +1 more) — every single non-bot message across all of them (40/40, 40/40, 16/16, …) came back with `content: ""` while `authorName` came through fine every time. This is the textbook signature of Discord's **Message Content privileged intent** not being granted to X-Bot's Discord application — without it, Discord's REST API withholds `content`/`embeds`/`attachments` for any message the bot didn't author and isn't mentioned in. This is a Discord Developer Portal setting (Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents), not something fixable in this repo's code.
- ROOT CAUSE #2 (Kaitlin's "shows sender as X-Bot") — a real, code-level bug, now fixed: every DarkCampus→Discord/Slack relay posts via X-Bot's own bot token (`sendToDiscord`/`discordSend`, `sendToSlack`/`slackSend`) — a bot-token POST can't set a custom display name (only a Discord webhook can), so Discord always renders "X-Bot" as the author regardless of who actually sent it. The code already embeds the real sender in the message TEXT (`relayPrefix()` → `"[DC] Kaitlin: hello everyone"` for registry channels; `crossPostToMissionControl()` → `"[GENERAL-CHAT] Kaitlin: hello everyone"` for legacy ones) — Discord-side readers see it fine — but reading that same message back into DarkCampus's own feed showed literally "X-Bot" as the sender, discarding the name that was right there in the text.
- ROOT CAUSE #3 (Abeal's "switching groups doesn't update") — `terminal/page.tsx`'s `loadMessages()` returned immediately when `activeChannel` didn't resolve (`if (!activeChannel) return;`) WITHOUT clearing the `messages` state — so if the selected channel ever dropped out of `visibleChannels` (a filter re-evaluating, a list refresh racing the selection), the feed silently froze on the PREVIOUS channel's messages instead of updating or clearing. The "eventually everything vanishes" half of this report is not fully explained by static reading alone — see SCOPE NOTE.
- FIX (`pflx-darkcampus/src/app/api/messages/route.ts`): added `unwrapRelayEcho()` — when a message is bot-authored AND its content matches the `"[BRACKET] Name: text"` shape both relay paths already produce, `toDCMessage()` now attributes it to the real sender (`authorName` = the embedded name, `content` = the text with the wrapper stripped, `isXBot` flips to `false`) instead of showing raw "X-Bot". `isBot` stays `true` (Discord genuinely did post it) so `scanInboundMessages()` still correctly skips re-scanning it as a fresh inbound message (would have double-counted peer rewards/violations otherwise). Gated strictly on `isBot` — a genuine human message is never reinterpreted even if its text coincidentally looks like the pattern. Separately, when a message is NOT bot-authored and its content comes back empty, `contentHidden: true` is now set and `content` becomes a clear, actionable notice ("Message content hidden by Discord — ask the host to enable the Message Content privileged intent…") instead of silently rendering blank. Added a guard to `scanInboundMessages()`'s candidate filter (`&& !m.contentHidden`) so that notice text is never fed to X-Bot's profanity/reward scanner as if a member actually said it.
- FIX (`pflx-darkcampus/src/app/lib/types.ts`): added `contentHidden?: boolean` to `DCMessage`.
- FIX (`pflx-darkcampus/src/app/components/MessageFeed.tsx`): renders the `contentHidden` notice in italic/muted styling instead of running it through `RichText` as if it were a normal message.
- FIX (`pflx-darkcampus/src/app/terminal/page.tsx`): `loadMessages()` now clears `messages` (and `loadingMessages`) when `activeChannel` is unresolved, instead of leaving the previous channel's messages frozen on screen.
- Files: `pflx-darkcampus/src/app/api/messages/route.ts`, `src/app/lib/types.ts`, `src/app/components/MessageFeed.tsx`, `src/app/terminal/page.tsx`.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` clean on all 4 files, no `TS1xxx` syntax errors. 16 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `unwrapRelayEcho()`, `toDCMessage()`, the `scanInboundMessages` candidate filter, and `loadMessages()`'s early-return verbatim: registry-channel and legacy cross-post relay formats both unwrap correctly; a non-relay X-Bot message (e.g. the link-verification note) is left alone; a genuine human message is never reinterpreted even when it coincidentally matches the pattern (the `isBot` gate holds); **Kaitlin's exact repro** — X-Bot's echo of her own "[DC] Kaitlin: hello everyone" now attributes to Kaitlin, `isXBot` flips false, `isBot` stays true, content is the clean message text; **Abeal's exact repro** — a real member's empty-content message now shows the actionable notice instead of blank, sender name unaffected; a normal message with real content passes through completely unchanged (regression guard); an empty-content BOT message (not a relay echo) is never falsely flagged `contentHidden`; the placeholder notice is confirmed excluded from X-Bot's inbound scan; and the terminal freeze fix — an unresolved `activeChannel` now clears stale messages instead of freezing, while a valid channel still loads normally — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this fixes the DISPLAY-side half of DC_CHAT — attribution and honest error states — without needing any Discord-side config. The actual restoration of real message TEXT reading from Discord requires HOST ACTION (below); this patch cannot do that part. Slack's bot-authored messages are currently filtered out entirely (`!m.bot_id` in `fetchSlackMessages`) rather than unwrapped like Discord's — Slack wasn't named in any of the 4 reports, so this was left alone to keep the change scoped and fully tested rather than extending an untested code path. The "eventually all messages/terminals vanish" half of Abeal's 8/8 report is only partially addressed by the freeze fix above; a `LinkGate.tsx` full-screen blocking overlay (added Aug 9, shown to any unlinked member) is a plausible alternate explanation for "everything disappeared" but doesn't explain the "switching groups" lead-in and looked like working-as-designed rather than a bug, so it was not touched — worth a live check with Abeal specifically (is his account linked?) if this recurs.
- HOST ACTIONS: **enable Discord's Message Content privileged intent** — developer.discord.com/applications → X-Bot's application → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents → toggle on "Message Content Intent" → save. This is the actual fix for "message text missing" / "only X-Bot messages show real content" and cannot be done from code. Worth telling Kaitlin and Abeal that the sender-attribution half is live now (relay echoes show real names), and that the content-missing half needs this one Discord setting before it's fully resolved.

## PATCH PATHWAY v1.1 — CHASE CAM / COCKPIT: CAMERA SPIN ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED, WEAPONS NOW FIRE ON CLICK (Aug 14, from the FeedForward priority list)
- CONTEXT: item #7 on the FeedForward priority list, BATTLE_ARENA Chase Cam — re-scoped after checking the FeedForward sheet directly: all 4 concrete repro reports (Essence 8/8 ×2, Essence 8/11, Kabir 8/8) are about Core Pathways' space **chase/cockpit flight view** (`pflx-pathway-portal/pathway.html`), not the separate `pflx-arena-check` (Battle Arena building) repo — Essence's 8/6 report about rotating the camera while building is a different, unrelated feature in that other app and was not touched here.
- SYMPTOM 1 — camera spin (Essence, 8/8 + 8/11): "the chase cam and the cockpit both have the camera spinning around over and over again in a 360 repeatedly" / "disconnect the camera from the cursor that's following."
- SYMPTOM 2 — weapons don't fire (Essence, 8/8 + 8/11): "I can't figure out how to shoot, in most games it's simply hold your mouse down or tap" / fix spec: "get the mouse position on the screen, convert it to world coordinates, find the direction vector from the gun to that point, and apply velocity to the bullet along that direction."
- ROOT CAUSE 1, confirmed by reading the shipped code: mouse position drove ship heading directly. Every `mousemove` recomputed `window._pflxMouseSteer` from how far the cursor sat from screen-center (dead zone only the middle 16% of the screen width), and `pflxKeyLoop()` added `turn * 0.042` radians to `pflxShipHeading` on EVERY animation frame for as long as the cursor stayed outside that narrow strip — which is almost always, since nothing tells a player to park their mouse dead-center to stop turning. That's an unbounded, ever-accumulating spin: a completely ordinary resting cursor position (e.g. 70% across the screen) integrates well past a full 360° within a few seconds and never stops on its own. Matches the report exactly.
- ROOT CAUSE 2: weapons DID fire, but only via the SPACE bar (`pflxKeys.fire`, auto-targeting the nearest asteroid/pirate in range) — there was no click-to-fire path at all, so a tester expecting "hold mouse / tap" (the control scheme "most games" use, per Essence) would reasonably conclude the weapon was broken rather than discover the SPACE shortcut.
- FIX (`pathway.html`): removed mouse-driven steering entirely — the cursor no longer feeds `pflxShipHeading` at all. Left/Right (arrows or A/D) are the sole turn control again (`pflxKeyLoop` now computes `turn` from `pflxKeys.left`/`.right` only); this also retires the Left/Right "strafe" behavior added in the June 2026 rework, since that traded turning away specifically to avoid conflicting with mouse-steer — with mouse-steer gone there's no conflict left to avoid, and a player needs turning back. Added `pflxScreenToWorld(clientX, clientY)` — converts a screen point through the existing pan/zoom transform AND (new) the flight-model's world-rotation (`pflxViewRotDeg`, which spins the map around the ship so heading stays up-screen in chase/cockpit) to get the correct world-space point; the cosmetic 3D `rotateX` tilt is intentionally not inverted, matching the same flat-2D approximation the pre-existing click-to-lock handler already used. Added `pflxBlaster.fireAt(wx, wy)` and a `canvas` `mousedown` listener (left-click, chase/cockpit only, ignores clicks on UI chrome) that fires a bolt from the ship toward the clicked world point, crediting a hit to any live asteroid/pirate within a 140px aim-assist radius of that point — the existing SPACE-bar auto-target fire is untouched and still works as an alternate control.
- BONUS FIX (same root cause, same file): the pre-existing birdseye/flight-mode canvas `click` handler (target-lock, `flyToObject`) computed screen→world using pan/zoom only, the same way the removed mouse-steer code did — meaning it silently mis-targeted in chase/cockpit any time the ship had turned away from its spawn heading (the world-rotation was never accounted for). Now routed through the same `pflxScreenToWorld()`; unchanged in birdseye, where rotation is always 0.
- Files: `pflx-pathway-portal/pathway.html` only (also updated the two in-app control hints — the onboarding tooltip and the `#arrowKeyHint` strip — to describe the new click/SPACE-fire and arrow-only-steer controls instead of the old mouse-steer text).
- Verified: all 16 inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check` (no syntax errors introduced). 15 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `pflxScreenToWorld`, the `pflxKeyLoop` turn computation, and `pflxBlaster.fireAt` verbatim: reconstructed the OLD mouse-steer formula and confirmed a perfectly ordinary cursor position (70% across the screen) drives the heading past 360° within a few seconds with nothing to stop it (the bug, reproduced); confirmed the NEW turn computation is exactly 0 regardless of cursor position when no turn key is held, and stays 0 across simulated frames; confirmed Left/Right individually turn ±1, cancel to 0 when both held, and stop immediately the frame a key is released; confirmed `pflxScreenToWorld` is unchanged from the old math when there's no world rotation, and correctly un-rotates a 90°-rotated view (with an explicit contrast against what the old, rotation-blind math would have returned); confirmed `fireAt` credits the nearest live target within the aim-assist radius, fires cleanly at empty space with no false target when nothing is nearby, never targets a depleted/collected object, and picks the nearest of multiple in-range candidates — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: Kabir's 8/8 report ("after selecting cockpit camera, the interface only occupies part of the screen and doesn't scale to fill the window") was investigated but NOT fixed — his attached screenshot shows the platform's top nav bar over a "PERSONAL BRANDING — LOCKED / A PlayDNA account is required" panel with large unfilled black space above/below, which is a pathway skill-node detail view (`pe-branding`, a real locked node in the pathway data) gated behind an unrelated sign-in wall, not the 3D cockpit HUD (no dashboard, joysticks, or reticle visible in the screenshot at all). This doesn't match the space-flight code path investigated for the other two symptoms, and I couldn't establish a confident root cause from a single screenshot that may not actually be showing the cockpit view he described. Left open — worth asking Kabir for a fresh screenshot taken while the cockpit dashboard/HOTAS sticks are actually on screen, since the current evidence points to a different (possibly unrelated) locked-node/sign-in layout bug.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — this was a pure client-side control/input fix, no config or data changes.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.64 — P2P CALLS: INBOUND-INVITE CHANNEL NOW SELF-HEALS, CAMERA-OFF ACTUALLY RELEASES THE HARDWARE, SCREEN-SHARE FAILURES NO LONGER SILENT (Aug 14, from the FeedForward priority list)
- CONTEXT: item #8 (last) on the FeedForward priority list, P2P_CALL — 2 reports from Abeal, both against the Mission Control chat's WebRTC video/screen call feature (`preview.html`, the `_pcCall*`/`pflxChatCall*` functions): 8/11 a detailed 4-part repro, 8/12 a follow-up confirming it was still broken.
- SYMPTOM 1 (8/11, part 1): "the calling notification did not appear always, kept bugging out, and the only way to join was by pressing the call button in chat."
- SYMPTOM 2 (8/11, part 2): "the camera function was bugged, it showed it was off but i could see that my camera was on."
- SYMPTOM 3 (8/11, part 3): "the share screen function was not working."
- SYMPTOM 4 (8/11, part 4): "I could not hear nor see the person i was calling, could not see their shared screen aswell" — see HOST ACTIONS, this one is infrastructure, not code.
- ROOT CAUSE 1: the passive per-thread channel that listens for inbound `invite` broadcasts (`_pcCallAttachInbound`) called `.subscribe()` with no status callback at all — unlike the presence channel (`_prBoot`) elsewhere in this same file, which already has a `CHANNEL_ERROR`/`TIMED_OUT`/`CLOSED` → rebuild handler. Any realtime hiccup (network blip, a backgrounded tab, an idle timeout) silently killed the channel, and `_pcCallAttachInbound()`'s own "already attached, skip" guard meant a dead channel was never revisited — that thread stopped ringing for the rest of the session, with zero indication anything had gone wrong. Exactly matches "did not appear always, kept bugging out" (intermittent, not systematic) and "the only way to join was the call button in chat" (which opens a brand-new channel of its own, bypassing the dead one).
- ROOT CAUSE 2: `pflxChatCallToggleCam` only flipped `MediaStreamTrack.enabled`, which mutes the track's OUTPUT but does not release the camera device — in most browsers the hardware keeps actively capturing (and its indicator light stays lit) the whole time a track is merely disabled rather than stopped. The UI said "Cam Off" while the physical camera plainly wasn't, exactly as reported.
- ROOT CAUSE 3: `pflxChatCallToggleScreen`'s `getDisplayMedia()` failure path only did `console.warn(...)` — a denied permission or a dismissed browser screen-picker produced zero user-visible feedback. Clicking the button and having nothing happen, with no explanation, reads exactly like "not working."
- ROOT CAUSE 4 (documented in the code already, not new): the WebRTC config only lists public STUN servers (`stun.l.google.com`) — no TURN server. The code's own comment already says as much: "calls behind symmetric NAT will fail until a TURN URL is added." Testers on typical school/home/mobile networks are very likely to sit behind NAT that STUN alone can't traverse, which would produce exactly "could not hear nor see the person." This is an infrastructure gap, not a logic bug — see HOST ACTIONS.
- FIX 1 (`_pcCallAttachInbound` / new `_pcCallAttachInboundOne`): split the per-thread attach into its own function and added a `subscribe(status => …)` callback matching the same recovery pattern `_prBoot` already uses — on `CHANNEL_ERROR`/`TIMED_OUT`/`CLOSED`, the dead channel is removed from `_pcInboundChannels`, cleaned up via `client.removeChannel`, and a fresh one is re-attached after a 4s backoff. A benign status (e.g. `SUBSCRIBED`) does nothing.
- FIX 2 (`pflxChatCallToggleCam`): turning the camera off now fully `.stop()`s every local video track (releasing the device — the indicator light goes out) and sends a `null` track to every peer connection (so remote viewers see it stop too, not just a frozen last frame from an "enabled=false" track). Turning it back on re-acquires a fresh track via `getUserMedia`, the same pattern the screen-share toggle already used for restoring the camera.
- FIX 2b (`_pcCallBuildPeer` / `_pcCallReplaceEveryVideoSender`): fixing FIX 2 surfaced a real latent bug — `_pcCallReplaceEveryVideoSender` located "the video sender" on each peer connection by searching `pc.getSenders()` for one whose `.track.kind === 'video'`. The instant a sender's track is set to `null` (turning the camera fully off), that search can never find it again — so turning the camera back ON would silently fail to restore video to any peer. `_pcCallBuildPeer` now captures and caches the video sender reference explicitly (`peers[id].videoSender`) at the moment the track is first added, and `_pcCallReplaceEveryVideoSender` uses that cached reference (falling back to the old track-based lookup only if the cache is somehow missing). Verified this survives repeated off/on cycles, not just a single toggle.
- FIX 3 (`pflxChatCallToggleScreen`): both failure paths (starting a share, and restoring the camera afterward) now call `pflxToast(...)` with the underlying error message instead of only logging to the console. The success paths are unchanged.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 63 → 64 (`PFLX_BUILD` already `2026.08`, no change needed).
- Verified: all 14 inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check` (no syntax errors introduced). 34 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `_pcCallAttachInboundOne`, `pflxChatCallToggleCam`, `pflxChatCallToggleScreen`, and `_pcCallReplaceEveryVideoSender` verbatim against mocked Supabase-channel/WebRTC/DOM primitives: a normal invite still rings; a dropped channel (`CHANNEL_ERROR`/`TIMED_OUT`/`CLOSED`) is removed and a retry is scheduled, and firing that retry proves the SAME thread rings again afterward (the actual bug fix, not just "code runs"); a benign `SUBSCRIBED` status does not trigger cleanup (regression guard); toggling the camera off calls `track.stop()` and clears the local stream's video track (contrasted directly against a reconstruction of the old `enabled=false`-only code, which never stops the track); toggling back on re-acquires a live track and restores it on the peer sender; a failed re-enable toasts instead of silently leaving `camEnabled` in a wrong state; an explicit contrast test proves the OLD track-based sender lookup returns `undefined` the moment a track is nulled (the FIX 2b bug), while the NEW cached-sender version survives two full off/on cycles; screen-share start/restore failures both toast with the real error message, and the success paths are unchanged (regression guard) — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: SYMPTOM 4 (can't hear/see the other person at all) is very likely the undocumented-until-now-flagged STUN-only NAT limitation, not a logic bug — see HOST ACTIONS. Also not touched: a late-joining peer while the caller's camera is ALREADY off won't get a video sender created at all (since `_pcCallBuildPeer` only adds a sender for tracks present in `localStream` at connect time) — turning the camera back on later won't reach that particular peer's connection. This is a pre-existing structural limitation of the addTrack-based mesh setup, not something FIX 2/2b introduced, and wasn't part of either report; a real fix would need `pc.addTransceiver('video', {direction: 'sendrecv'})` reserved up front regardless of whether a local track exists yet, which is a bigger change I didn't want to risk untested in this pass.
- HOST ACTIONS: **add a TURN server to `_pcCallRtcConfig()`** if "can't hear/see the other person" keeps happening after this patch (fixes 1-3 do NOT touch this) — STUN-only ICE negotiation fails for peers behind symmetric/restrictive NAT (common on school WiFi and mobile networks), which is the most likely explanation for total audio/video connection failure. Options: a managed TURN service (Twilio Network Traversal Service, Xirsys, Cloudflare Calls) or self-hosting `coturn`; either way it needs a `urls`/`username`/`credential` entry added to the `iceServers` array alongside the existing STUN entries. This requires picking a provider and provisioning credentials — a decision for Ennis, not something codeable without an account. Worth telling Abeal that the notification/camera/screen-share issues are fixed and to try a call again, but that the "can't hear or see them" part specifically needs this follow-up before it's fully resolved.
