## PATCH PLATFORM v1.65 — XC_CREDIT ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: APPROVED TASKS / BATTLE ARENA WINS WERE SILENTLY FAILING TO CREDIT XC (Aug 14, from the fresh FeedForward sweep)
- SYMPTOM: Bijo Bintu (8/5) — "I was told that I got credited 100 Xc for participation, and 500 Xc for winning the challenge, but after I went to Mission Control, my balance stayed at 0 Xc. I even did a hard reset, but no change." Ayrene Arun (8/2, 8/9) — "I have submitted tasks but still have not received any x-coins." Aadhya Khanna (8/9) — "I have 0 XC despite my tasks being fully approved... I'm not the only one with this issue as brand IRENJP3G [Ayrene] also expressed that their account also shows 0 X-coin." Flagged as NOT yet root-caused in v1.62 with a leading hypothesis; this patch confirms and fixes it.
- ROOT CAUSE: `PflxDataBus.award()` and `applyUpdate()` (`preview.html`) resolved players ONLY against the in-memory `PLAYERS` array — hydrated exclusively from individual `pflx_player_<id>` cloud rows. A player added directly through Player Management lands immediately in the bulk MC roster (`mcPlayers` / cloud key `pflx_mc_players`) but only gets an individual row via a one-shot `setTimeout` self-heal 4 seconds after page load (`_mcBackfillMissingPlayerRows`). If a host approves that player's task, or an arena win reports their result, before that timer fires (or before `mcPlayers`' own cloud fetch has resolved), `PLAYERS.find` misses, `award()` hits `console.warn(...); return null;`, and the caller (`mcApprovePlayerSubmission`, the arena win handler, `_mcRollupAwards`) never checks the return value — the task/match still shows "approved"/"won" in the UI, but the XC write silently never happened, and it stays broken in that host's browser tab until the next full page reload re-triggers the 4s timer (matching "did a hard reset, no change" — a reload starts a NEW race, it doesn't retroactively fix already-approved items).
- FIX: added `_pflxResolvePlayerForAward(playerId)` — tries `PLAYERS.find` first (fast path, unchanged behavior), and on a miss falls back to `mcPlayers`, pushing the found record into `PLAYERS` inline and synchronously (no timer dependency) before the award/update proceeds. Both `award()` and `applyUpdate()` now route through this resolver. Also made the still-possible failure case (player genuinely doesn't exist anywhere) loud instead of silent: fires a host-visible `pflxToast` warning and a `pflx_award_failed` broadcast, instead of only a `console.warn` no one sees until a tester complains days later.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 64 → 65.
- Verified: all 13 inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. 11 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `_pflxResolvePlayerForAward`, `applyUpdate`, and `award` verbatim: Bijo's exact repro (player only in `mcPlayers`) — OLD code contrast returns `null`/no credit, FIXED code resolves and credits 100 XC, then a second award (arena win, 500 XC) stacks correctly to 600 on the now-resolved player; a genuinely-unknown player still correctly fails, now with a host toast + broadcast (was silent); a regression guard proving the mcPlayers fallback is never consulted once a player already exists in `PLAYERS` (no stale-data overwrite risk); `applyUpdate()` benefits from the same fix, not just `award()`; a race scenario proving a player who arrives in `mcPlayers` mid-session succeeds on the very next award call with no reload needed — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this closes the reported symptom for BOTH task-approval and Battle Arena win paths (they share the same `award()` funnel). Also addresses the long-standing `pflx_mc_players` vs `pflx_player_<id>` split-brain for this specific consumer (award/update) — other code paths that read `PLAYERS` directly without going through the bus are not covered by this patch.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required for this fix. Separately — Hannah Rodrigues's XC balance (7550/8750, from the v1.62 COURSE_REWARD investigation) is still sitting untouched pending your confirmation of whether the ~2050 XC jump around 8/6–8/7 was a manual grant; see the COURSE_REWARD note below for the open question.

## PATCH XCOIN v1.3 — PATHWAY GUIDE / X-BOT CHAT ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED: THE GEMINI MODEL BEHIND IT WAS RETIRED BY GOOGLE (Aug 14, from the fresh FeedForward sweep)
- SYMPTOM: Hannah Rodrigues, 5 separate reports over 3 weeks — "Sorry, I'm having trouble connecting right now" from the PFLX Pathway Guide chat widget. Related quality complaints (Feba, Ayrene, Abeal) about irrelevant/canned answers turned out to be a different, client-side fallback masking this same root failure.
- ROOT CAUSE: `pflx-ai-chat.js` (served from `pflx-pathway-portal`, loaded by `pathway.html`) calls `pflx-xcoin-app.vercel.app/api/gemini`, whose `route.ts` had `GEMINI_MODEL` hardcoded to `"gemini-2.0-flash"`. Google retired that model; every single request returned a live `404` — confirmed directly against the production endpoint: `{"error":"api_error","details":"...This model models/gemini-2.0-flash is no longer available...","status":404}`. The widget's `catch` block converts ANY non-OK response into "Sorry, I'm having trouble connecting right now," so this had been failing 100% of the time with no visible cause in either browser console error message a tester would report.
- FIX: updated `GEMINI_MODEL` to `"gemini-3.6-flash"`, the current recommended stable Flash model (confirmed via Google's own model docs and independent coverage of the Aug 2026 retirement of 2.0/2.5-era models). No other logic changed — `fetchWithRetry`'s 429/503 backoff and the `rate_limited`/`api_key_invalid`/`api_error` response mapping were already correct and are untouched.
- Files: `pflx-xcoin-app/app/api/gemini/route.ts` only (a Next.js API route — not part of the `preview.html`/`pathway.html` single-file apps, so no `PFLX_PATCH` bump applies here).
- Verified: single hardcoded string change, no logic touched — confirmed live in production immediately after deploy by re-calling the endpoint directly (see deploy confirmation below).
- SCOPE NOTE: this is DISTINCT from `preview.html`'s own `XBOT_AI` chat engine (the in-Console X-Bot, used by players/hosts inside the platform itself), which proxies through `pflx-pathway-portal.vercel.app/api/pflx-ai` — that endpoint currently returns `{"error":"no-key"}` (no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY`/`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` configured on that Vercel project at all), which is why in-Console X-Bot falls back to the keyword-matcher (`XBOT_STATIC.default()`) and gives the "talks about a completely different feature" / "doesn't answer all questions" style replies Feba/Ayrene/Abeal described. That's a separate, still-open issue.
- HOST ACTIONS: **add at least one AI provider key** (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) to the `pflx-pathway-portal` Vercel project's environment variables to fix the in-Console X-Bot's answer quality (separate from the Pathway Guide widget fixed above, which now has a working key+model on the `pflx-xcoin-app` project). Also worth a periodic check of Google's Gemini model deprecation schedule going forward — this exact failure mode (a hardcoded model name silently retired upstream) can recur.

## PATCH PATHWAY v1.2 — PROJECT X "DISAPPEARING" ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (WHOLESALE-ARRAY SAVE OVERWRITE), DEAD START BUTTONS FIXED FOR COURSEPACKAGE-ONLY NODES (Aug 14, from the fresh FeedForward sweep)
- SYMPTOM 1 (disappearing course): Hannah Rodrigues, 4 escalating reports — "connection error" resuming Project X → "I had the same problem yesterday... I was at 25% progress" → Project X "not there at all" → "I can't see the PROJECT X Course anymore." First scoped in the v1.37-era Handoff entry ("scoping these next") and never revisited.
- SYMPTOM 2 (dead Start buttons): Hannah Rodrigues (7/23) and Mariya Jomon (8/7) — Start does nothing on Professional Entrepreneur's "Intro to Entrepreneurship," CS/AI Specialist's "Intro to CS/AI," Digital Artist's "Graphic Design Concepts," and Industrial Designer's "Intro to Interior Design" — while Content Creator/Game Designer/3D Modeler/Sound Designer's intro nodes worked fine.
- ROOT CAUSE 1: `savePathwayEdits()` upserted the ENTIRE `pathway.nodes` array from whichever browser tab called it as the new value of the `pathway_<slug>` Supabase row — a classic wholesale-array, last-write-wins overwrite (the exact class of bug flagged in this skill's own Gotchas section). A host tab that loaded before Project X was added (by another host session, or before this tab's last refresh) simply never had it in memory; ANY save from that tab afterward — even just dragging an unrelated node — silently wrote a cloud record with Project X missing, and it vanished for every player on their next load.
- ROOT CAUSE 2: the Start button's click-wiring only checked `n.url || n.contentUrl` — never `n.coursePackage`, even though `showLaunchOverlay`'s own `resolvedCourseUrl()` has always been able to resolve a `coursePackage` slug into a real, loadable content URL. Any node configured through the Node Editor's "Course Package" field alone (rather than an external URL) got no `onclick` at all — a confirmed orphaned example: `courses/graphic-design-concepts/course.json` exists on disk, fully built, but was never wired to `da-intro` via `coursePackage`.
- FIX 1: `savePathwayEdits()` now re-fetches the CURRENT cloud row before upserting, and carries forward any node present there but absent from the local save — UNLESS it was genuinely deleted this session (new `_pflxDeletedNodeIds` Set, populated only by `deleteNode()`). A real deletion still goes through; an unrelated tab's stale view no longer wipes nodes it never knew about.
- FIX 2: the Start button now wires up on `n.url || n.contentUrl || n.coursePackage`. Also added a fallback for genuinely unconfigured nodes (previously a totally silent no-op): clicking Start now shows a toast — hosts get "set a URL or Course Package in the Node Editor," players get "this course isn't set up yet."
- Files: `pflx-pathway-portal/pathway.html` only. No `PFLX_PATCH` bump (that constant lives in `preview.html`/Console only, per this skill's own numbering rule for the PATHWAY track).
- Verified: all 4 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. 12 scenarios in a live-code test extracting the merge-safety block and the click-wiring condition verbatim: Hannah's exact repro (stale tab saves an unrelated edit, Project X exists in the cloud) — OLD code contrast shows Project X wiped, FIXED code carries it forward intact with no duplicates; a genuine deletion is still respected and not restored; a node the local tab DOES have wins over the stale cloud copy (no silent downgrade of a host's own edit); a coursePackage-only node (da-intro style) now wires up correctly; url-based and contentUrl-based nodes still wire up as before (regression guards); a genuinely unconfigured node still correctly gets no launch handler — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this patch does NOT fix Project X's "connection error" on resume (the iframe has no load-failure detection — a blocked/failed embed just renders the browser's own error page inside the sandboxed frame with no visible signal to the app) or progress loss on resume (course progress is localStorage-only by default; cloud backup exists but is off unless the "Cloud Saves" toggle is enabled in Mission Control Settings — see HOST ACTIONS). Nor does it address the in-course logout button, which sits behind the platform's own `#pcLogout` — that control is fully covered by the full-screen course overlay and has no independent wiring; worth a follow-up pass. Also left open: whether the "Checkpoint Beta not unlocking despite Alpha 3/3" report (Kabir Grover) is a real gating fault or a stale checkpoint `status` flag needs a direct check of Kabir's player record against the current (not July-era) checkpoint config, which wasn't done in this pass.
- HOST ACTIONS: **enable Cloud Saves** (Mission Control → Settings → the global "Cloud Saves" toggle, writes `pflx_cloud_saves_global`) if course-progress loss on resume/device-switch keeps being reported — it exists and is fully wired, just off by default. This alone may resolve Hannah's "back to 25%" symptom without further code changes.

## ⚠️ URGENT ADDENDUM TO XCOIN v1.3 — THE GEMINI API KEY ITSELF HAS BEEN REVOKED BY GOOGLE AS LEAKED (HOST ACTION, SECURITY)

Immediately after the v1.3 deploy went READY, I re-verified the fix live against production and found a NEW failure — proof the model-name fix itself worked (no more 404 "model not found"), but exposing a different, more urgent problem underneath:

```
HTTP 403 {"error":"api_key_invalid","details":"...\"message\": \"Your API key was reported as leaked. Please use another API key.\",\n  \"status\": \"PERMISSION_DENIED\"..."}
```

Google's own automated key-scanning has revoked the `GEMINI_API_KEY` currently set on the `pflx-xcoin-app` Vercel project because it was detected exposed somewhere public (`pflx-xcoin-app` is a public GitHub repo — the key was very likely committed in plaintext at some point in its history, in this file or elsewhere, or logged/echoed somewhere a scraper found it).

**HOST ACTIONS — please do both, and treat this as a security item, not just a bug:**
1. Generate a brand-new Gemini API key in Google AI Studio / Google Cloud Console, and set it as `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the `pflx-xcoin-app` Vercel project's environment variables (Project Settings → Environment Variables), then redeploy so it picks up the new value.
2. **Explicitly revoke the old leaked key** in Google AI Studio/Cloud Console if it isn't already fully dead — Google's message suggests it's already blocked from use, but confirming/rotating it fully closes the exposure.
3. Worth a quick `git log -p -- app/api/gemini/route.ts` (and a repo-wide secret scan, e.g. `gh secret-scanning` or `trufflehog`) across `pflx-xcoin-app` to find exactly where/when the key was committed, so it doesn't happen again — I did not do this myself since it involves reading full git history I don't have local access to search efficiently, and any further key material shouldn't be handled by an agent regardless.

Once the new key is live, the Pathway Guide / X-Bot chat widget fixed in v1.3 should work end-to-end — the model-name fix is confirmed correct and deployed; only the key is now blocking it.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.66 — P2P CALLS: CAMERA-OFF NOW SHOWS THE PLAYER'S AVATAR, AVATARS GLOW WHILE SPEAKING, QUICK EMOJI REACTIONS, CONNECTION STABILITY HARDENED (Aug 15, Ennis-requested)

- REQUEST: following the v1.64 P2P call fixes (notification reliability, camera-off actually releasing the hardware, screen-share error surfacing), Ennis asked for camera-off tiles to show the player's avatar instead of a blank/frozen frame, plus more generally "add more useful and innovative features" and "make sure the calls are stable." Scoped this pass to four concrete, testable additions to the existing `_pcCall`/`pflxChatCall*` WebRTC mesh (`preview.html` ~line 66900+); did NOT touch the separate Virtual Theater broadcast system (see the scoping note at the end of this entry — that's a much bigger, separate ask).
- FEATURE 1 — camera-off shows the player's avatar: previously a camera-off tile just went black/froze (v1.64 correctly stops the local track, but nothing filled the resulting empty video element). `_pcCallBuildPeer()` now carries an `avatar` field (sourced from the `join`/`offer` signaling payloads, which now include `avatar: me.image`) and a `camEnabled` flag defaulting `true`. Because a WebRTC `replaceTrack(null)` doesn't reliably fire a track-ended event on the *receiving* end across browsers, camera state is now signaled explicitly via a new `cam-state` broadcast — sent whenever a participant toggles their camera, and proactively re-sent the moment a new peer connection is built (so a late joiner immediately learns if someone's camera was already off). `_pcCallRenderTiles()` shows a centered avatar image (or a colored initial-letter fallback if no avatar) over the tile whenever `camEnabled` is false, for both the local tile and every remote tile — the underlying `<video>` element is preserved (not torn down), so a camera toggle mid-call updates instantly.
- FEATURE 2 — avatars glow while speaking: a Web Audio `AnalyserNode` is attached to every tile's stream (`_pcCallEnsureMeter`), and a shared `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`_pcCallSpeakingLoop`) computes an RMS audio level each frame, smoothed via `_pcSpeakingSmooth()` — fast attack (jumps up immediately on a loud frame) and slow decay (~0.82×/frame) so the glow doesn't flicker in the brief silent gaps between words. Above a 0.06 threshold (`_pcSpeakingIsActive`), the tile gets a `pc-speaking` CSS class — a green pulsing border, works whether the tile is showing live video or the camera-off avatar. Audio meters are wrapped in try/catch and never affect call functionality if unsupported (e.g. an unusual browser, a stream with no audio track yet).
- FEATURE 3 — quick emoji reactions: a new "😀 React" button in the call control bar opens a 6-emoji picker (👍 ❤️ 😂 🎉 👏 🔥); tapping one shows the emoji floating up and fading over the sender's own tile locally, and broadcasts a `reaction` event so it also floats over that tile for everyone else in the call (`_pcCallShowReaction`).
- FEATURE 4 — connection stability: `onconnectionstatechange` previously only reacted to `'failed'`/`'closed'` (immediately dropping the peer's tile). A `'disconnected'` state — very often a transient blip (WiFi handoff, brief packet loss) — was previously silently ignored with no recovery attempt, so a call could sit half-broken with no explanation. Now: a `'disconnected'` peer gets a host-visible toast ("…trying to recover") and, if still disconnected 3 seconds later, an `RTCPeerConnection.restartIce()` attempt (guarded — a no-op, not a crash, on browsers that don't support it). `'failed'`/`'closed'` behavior (remove the tile) is unchanged.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 65 → 66 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 13 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) 31 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `_pcSpeakingSmooth`/`_pcSpeakingIsActive` verbatim plus verbatim source-match checks on the tile `camEnabled`/avatar resolution, the new peer-object defaults, the `cam-state`/`reaction` broadcast handlers' self-echo guards, and the `disconnected`→`restartIce` branch: fast-attack/slow-decay smoothing behaves correctly at the boundary and under clamped/NaN input; an end-to-end burst-then-silence sequence stays "speaking" briefly after the burst ends (no flicker) and correctly settles back to not-speaking; a brand-new peer defaults camera-ON until a `cam-state` broadcast says otherwise; an avatar-less participant falls back to their name's initial; both new broadcast handlers correctly ignore their own echoed broadcasts (matching the existing pattern used by every other handler in `_pcCallWireChannel`); the `'failed'`/`'closed'` regression guard holds — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this is entirely within the existing 1:1/small-group P2P call mesh — it does NOT touch or extend the separate **Virtual Theater** broadcast system (`vtLaunchTheater()` and friends, ~line 39969+), which is a one-way YouTube/Twitch iframe embed, not WebRTC. Ennis separately asked (same session) for a much larger "Live Streaming Session" feature set — group randomizer + breakout rooms with cohort/Startup Studio/project presets, multi-host Theater control, live lighting effects, DJ/sound control, and ProPresenter-style display switching. A read-only survey of the existing codebase before committing to any of that turned up a genuinely mixed picture worth knowing before scoping further work:
  - **Group randomizer**: already built and live — `mcGenerateGroups(participants, size, strategy)` (~line 44269) supports random, skill-matched (pathway+XC snake-distribute), cohort-same, and cohort-mixed strategies; `crRandomGroups()`/`crRecallAll()` in the Host Floating Controller (Console Remote, ~line 45057) drive it. Startup Studio and project-based presets would be new strategies following the same established pattern (players already carry `studioName`; project grouping would need a similar existing field or a small new one).
  - **Breakout rooms**: the grouping/assignment/notification layer is real and live (`crRenderBreakoutRooms()`, broadcasts `pflx_session_breakout`), but the receiving side only toasts players their assignment — it does NOT yet isolate players into actually-separate call/UI contexts (no real per-room video). Making that real would mean wiring breakout groups into the existing `_pcCall` mesh (or a new per-room channel) — a genuine build, not a config change.
  - **Multi-host / crew roles**: more built than expected — `VT_ROLES` (Director/Presenter/Sound Tech/DJ/Lighting Tech/Media Tech), `vtAssignRole()`/`vtUnassignRole()`/`vtApplyCrewRole()` already gate Theater's top-bar controls to `isHost || role === 'director'` and show/hide tabs per role. This is most of the "allow other hosts to control Theater" ask already scaffolded — likely needs surfacing/testing/hardening rather than a from-scratch build.
  - **Lighting effects**: already real and working — `vtLightUpdate()`/`vtLightPreset()`/`vtApplyLiveSkin()` (~line 40369) drive a live CSS-gradient overlay with named presets (warm/cool/concert/party/dramatic/blackout).
  - **DJ/sound control**: cosmetic only — the DJ tab/mixer UI exists (`vt-dj-layout`, deck/crossfader buttons) but every `vtDeck*`/`vtCrossfaderChange` handler referenced in the markup has **no function definition anywhere in the file** — dead buttons, no audio engine. A real build, not a wire-up.
  - **ProPresenter-style display switching**: nothing found — would be a from-scratch build.
  - Given the size and mix of "quick wins" vs. "multi-day builds" here, this was flagged back to Ennis rather than guessed at blind in the same pass as the P2P call work above — see the session report for the proposed phased breakdown and the question on priority order.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required for the 4 features shipped in this patch — pure client-side additions, no data/config migration.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.67 — HOST MISSION CONTROL QUICK XC AWARD TOOLS: SILENT DATA-LOSS FIXED (Aug 15, found while scoping "quick XC/badge tools for live stream")

- CONTEXT: while scoping Ennis's request for "quick XC Digital Badge tools for live stream functions with audience" (alongside a broader Wayground/Nearpod/Pear Deck/Mentimeter/Socrative/Padlet/ClassDojo-style feature request — see the session report for the full survey), a read-only investigation found that a quick-award tool matching exactly what he's asking for ALREADY EXISTS (`hmcAwardXC`/`hmcDeductXC`/`hmcBulkAwardXC`/`hmcPromotePlayer` in the "Host Mission Control" admin dashboard's Players tab) — but it had a real, silent bug worth fixing before building anything new on top of it.
- SYMPTOM (would never have been reported as a "bug" per se — just XC that mysteriously never showed up): these four one-tap host actions mutated `player.xc` directly on the in-memory `PLAYERS` array with **no save call anywhere in the function** — the edit only reached localStorage/Supabase if the host separately remembered to click the unrelated "💾 Save All Settings" button afterward. Close the tab, get pulled into something else, or the browser crashes first, and the award silently never persisted — no error, no warning, nothing to report.
- ROOT CAUSE: these four functions predate `PflxDataBus.award()`/`.update()` (the canonical, hardened award path every other reward source in the platform — task approval, checkpoint completion, Battle Arena wins, X-Coin, automations — already routes through) and were never migrated onto it. Direct `PLAYERS.find(p => p.id === id)` also had none of the v1.65 fallback-to-`mcPlayers` resolution, so a player who exists only in the MC bulk roster (the exact split-brain v1.65 fixed for task/arena awards) would silently no-op here too — but even more quietly, since the old code didn't even have a `console.warn`, just a bare `if (!player) return;`.
- FIX: all four now route through `PflxDataBus.award()` (award/deduct/bulk-award, using a signed XC delta) or `PflxDataBus.update()` (promote, which sets an absolute XC value rather than a delta). This gets three things for free: (1) the v1.65 `PLAYERS`→`mcPlayers` resolver fallback, (2) automatic debounced (~1.2s) cloud persistence via the same `broadcastPlayerChange()`→`persistPlayers()` path every other award uses — no more relying on a manual "Save All Settings" click, (3) a host-visible toast if an award genuinely fails to resolve, instead of total silence. `hmcBulkAwardXC` also now tracks and reports the ACTUAL number of successful awards (previously always reported the full attempted count, even if some silently failed).
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 66 → 67 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 13 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) 19 scenarios in a live-code test extracting all four functions verbatim and running them against a mock `PflxDataBus` (award/update) plus static source-pattern checks confirming the old direct-mutation pattern is gone: a normal award routes through `award()` exactly once with the correct delta and broadcasts success; an unresolvable player bails cleanly with no crash and no false "awarded" broadcast; a mid-call `award()` failure (simulating the exact split-brain case) does NOT broadcast a false success (the old code had no such guard at all); deduct sends a negative delta and lets the shared `award()` logic floor at 0; promote sets the absolute rank-unlock XC value via `update()` rather than a delta; bulk-award only targets `role:'player'` records (regression guard) and reports the REAL success count on a simulated partial failure, not the attempted count — all PASS.
- SCOPE NOTE: this fixes the SAVE-PERSISTENCE and RESOLUTION gap in the existing quick-award tool; it does not add new UI. Ennis's fuller "quick XC/badge tools for live stream with audience" ask, and the much larger Wayground/Nearpod/Pear Deck/Mentimeter/Socrative/Padlet/ClassDojo-style request, is covered in the session report — short version: Mission Control already has a genuinely working Nearpod/Wayground-style live session engine (`mcStartLiveSession()`, poll/quiz/multiplechoice/openresponse/grouping slide types, host pause/lock/freeze/reveal controls, cross-device sync) that likely covers most of that ask already; the "whiteboard" slide type is a non-functional placeholder (renders explanatory copy, no actual drawing/multi-poster logic — worth flagging as potentially misleading if shown to hosts as a real feature); DarkCampus's own `/poll` chat command is broken at the code level (`send/route.ts` imports `../../lib/engagement` and `../../lib/rewardRequests`, neither file exists in the repo — a genuine dead import, not just an undocumented feature); and there is no existing mechanism for pushing a poll/quiz/badge-ticker to a single SHARED audience display during a livestream (today's Live Session engine is pulled per-player, not projected).
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — pure bug fix, no data migration. Worth spot-checking recent Host Mission Control quick-award usage (if any) against known player XC totals, since any award made through this tool before this patch and not followed by a manual "Save All Settings" click may not have actually persisted.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.68 — LIVE SESSION "CLASSDOJO TOOLS": REAL DRAWING SLIDE (DOODLE WALL), STANDALONE RANDOM PICKER, STANDALONE GROUP PICKER, NOISE METER (Aug 15, Ennis-requested — "There needs to be a drawing type of slide, random player picker for those in the session, group picker, and other tools you would find in Classdojo tools")

- CONTEXT: direct follow-up to Ennis's engagement-tools request (v1.67's SCOPE NOTE flagged the "whiteboard" slide as a fake placeholder and noted `mcSessionRunGrouping()` only groups when the current slide happens to be a grouping/partnership slide, not on demand). This patch builds the four things he explicitly asked for.
- (1) REAL DRAWING SLIDE — the `whiteboard` slide type (relabeled "Drawing" in the type dropdown/meta; slide-type key kept as `whiteboard` for backward compatibility with any session already using it) no longer renders static "collaborative whiteboard" copy with zero drawing logic. `mcRenderSlideBody()`'s whiteboard branch now renders a real "doodle wall": a grid of every participant's submitted drawing (their `slide.responses[playerId].drawing`, a PNG data URL) with their name underneath, or a waiting message if nobody has drawn yet. On the player side, `pflxRenderLiveSessionOverlay()` renders a real `<canvas>` with a 6-color palette, Clear, and Submit Doodle — freehand drawing wired via mouse + touch events (`pflxDoodleInit`), submitted as a single PNG snapshot through the SAME `pflxSubmitSessionResponse()` path `openresponse` text already uses (`pflxDoodleSubmit`).
  - ARCHITECTURAL NOTE (why a snapshot, not live-synced strokes): the player overlay body is fully re-rendered every 2s by `window.pflxLiveSessionPoll`. A continuously-synced freehand canvas would get its in-progress strokes wiped by that same poll on the DRAWER'S OWN screen, independent of any other player — so a discrete "submit when done" design (mirroring `openresponse`) is the only architecturally-safe option without deeper poll-loop surgery.
  - SIDE FIX (same architectural issue, smaller scope): even a discrete-snapshot canvas would still get torn down and rebuilt (losing in-progress strokes) by the SAME player's own 2s poll tick while they're still mid-drawing, since `pflxRenderLiveSessionOverlay()` previously did one `body.innerHTML = badges + display + interactive` on every call. Split the overlay body into three sub-regions (`#pflx-live-session-badges`, `#pflx-live-session-display`, `#pflx-live-session-interactive`); the interactive region (buttons, textarea, canvas) is now only rebuilt when a `slide.id + canRespond + alreadyResponded` key actually changes, not on every poll tick. This also incidentally fixes the pre-existing (unreported) issue where an `openresponse` textarea got wiped mid-typing every 2 seconds.
- (2) STANDALONE RANDOM PICKER — new `mcSessionRandomPicker(index)`, a host-controls button ("🎯 Random Pick") usable on ANY slide, not tied to slide type. Picks uniformly from `sess.liveParticipants` (session-joined players only, never the full roster), avoids repeating the immediately-previous pick when more than one participant is available, stores the result on the session (`sess.lastRandomPickId`) so it persists across slide navigation, and broadcasts `pflx_session_random_pick`.
- (3) STANDALONE GROUP PICKER — new `mcSessionGroupPicker(index)`, a host-controls button ("🧩 Group Picker") that prompts for group size + strategy (random/skill-matched/cohort-same/cohort-mixed) and reuses the existing, already-correct `mcGenerateGroups()` algorithm — but stores the result on `sess.lastGroupPick` (session-level) instead of a specific slide's `slide.generatedGroups`, so it works regardless of what slide is currently showing. The pre-existing slide-bound `mcSessionRunGrouping()` ("Run Grouping") is UNCHANGED and still the right tool when a host wants a grouping/partnership slide's result shown/synced to players' individual overlays (`sess.lastGroupPick` is host-panel-only display, not pushed into any player's "YOUR GROUP" card).
- (4) NOISE METER — new `mcToggleNoiseMeter()`/`mcStartNoiseMeter()`/`mcStopNoiseMeter()`, a host-controls button ("🔊 Noise Meter") that requests mic access via `getUserMedia`, runs a `Web Audio AnalyserNode` over the live input (same pattern as the P2P call speaking-indicator from v1.66), and shows a floating green/yellow/red level bar. Mic is released automatically when the meter is closed or the session ends (`mcEndLiveSession()` now calls `mcStopNoiseMeter()`).
- New static container `#mc-session-picker-result` added next to `#mc-session-host-controls` in the live-session banner markup, rendered by `mcRenderSessionPickerResult(index)`.
- OTHER CLASSDOJO-STYLE TOOLS — DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT THIS PASS (flagging rather than silently dropping): a class-wide "Big Screen" projector/display mode (today's Live Session is per-player pulled, not a single shared display — same gap noted in v1.67's SCOPE NOTE); attendance tracking as its own report (participant list already exists via `sess.liveParticipants` but nothing summarizes it after the session ends); a positive-behavior sound-effect ticker. Timer/Challenge slide types needed NO new work — confirmed already real and fully working (`mcStartSlideTimer()`, shipped pre-v1.66).
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 67 → 68 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 14 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) 32 scenarios in a live-code test (jsdom-backed for the DOM-dependent functions) extracting every touched function verbatim: Random Picker excludes the immediately-previous pick when ≥2 participants are available and alerts cleanly (no fake pick, no save) with zero participants; Group Picker stores results on the session (not a slide), produces correct group counts/membership via the real `mcGenerateGroups()`, and bails cleanly if the size prompt is cancelled; the picker-result panel renders both a named pick and group membership into real DOM; the doodle-wall branch of `mcRenderSlideBody()` renders an actual `<img>` from a submitted drawing's data URL (and excludes malformed responses without a `.drawing` field) instead of the old static claim; the doodle canvas helpers wire color/clear/submit correctly against a mocked canvas context; and — the key architectural claim — a jsdom test proves the SAME canvas DOM node (tagged with a marker attribute simulating in-progress strokes) survives an unchanged second poll tick untouched, while a genuinely changed eligibility state (responses locked) correctly rebuilds the interactive region. All 32 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — this is additive UI, no data migration. Existing sessions with a `whiteboard` slide will now show the real doodle wall instead of the placeholder text automatically.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.69 — LOGIN-SCREEN REFRESH LOOP (NEUROFLUX): REALTIME ROSTER MERGE NOW FALLS BACK TO A BRAND MATCH LIKE EVERY SIBLING MERGE PATH (Aug 15, Ennis-reported live — "Neuroflux's screen is refreshing over and over")

- CONTEXT: Ennis reported watching a live tester's (NeuroFlux / Essence Johnson) login screen refreshing on a loop in real time. Queried the live Supabase `app_data` table directly rather than guessing from code alone.
- CONFIRMED (data): NeuroFlux has TWO individual `pflx_player_<id>` cloud rows, not one — `pflx_player_player-import-1774891628716-25` (her original pre-entered seed id; xc 2,100, 4 badges, 58 activity entries, updatedAt Aug 13) and `pflx_player_player-1778102469849-m7xam` (a second id, minted by a later self-claim; xc **100,000**, 0 badges, 10 activity entries, updatedAt Aug 11). Both rows are STALE as of this investigation (last written 2+ and 3+ days ago respectively) — so whatever's visually looping right now is not an active Supabase write ping-pong; the duplicate rows are a real, separate, confirmed defect, not necessarily the full live-moment explanation (see OPEN QUESTION below).
- ROOT CAUSE (code, confirmed): `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud()` (the boot-time roster pull) already matches an incoming cloud player row by id **or** brand — same as `_mcMergePlayers`'s callers elsewhere. `pflxStartRosterSubscriber()`'s realtime handler (the one that fires live, mid-session, whenever ANY `app_data` row changes) was the ONE merge path in the file that matched by **exact id only**. With two cloud rows for the same brand, a realtime tick for whichever row wasn't already resolved into `PLAYERS` got **pushed as a second, duplicate entry** instead of merged into the existing one — from that point `PLAYERS` held two NeuroFlux records, `BRANDS['NEUROFLUX']` could flip between the two rows' PINs, and every affected re-render (roster views, login brand list) would refire.
- FIX: `pflxStartRosterSubscriber()`'s handler now uses the SAME id-or-brand match (`x.id === p.id || (x.brand && p.brand && x.brand.toUpperCase() === p.brand.toUpperCase())`) as `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud()`, applied to all three lookups in the handler that previously matched by id only: the `prevRecord` snapshot (used for reward-toast deltas), the `PLAYERS` merge itself, and the localStorage cache sync — so the realtime path can no longer create a duplicate the boot-fetch path wouldn't have.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 68 → 69 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 14 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) 9 scenarios in a live-code test, extracted verbatim from the shipped handler via brace-balancing: confirms the old exact-id-only pattern is fully gone and all three lookups now carry the brand fallback; reproduces the exact NeuroFlux data (both real record shapes, real ids, real XC values) against the OLD matcher and shows it creates a duplicate `PLAYERS` entry (reproduces the bug), then against the NEW matcher and shows it correctly collapses to one record with the more-recent (updatedAt) record winning, order-independently; and confirms the brand-fallback never accidentally merges two genuinely different brands. All 9 PASS.
- OPEN QUESTION — NOT resolved by this patch, needs Ennis's call: the two rows disagree by **97,900 XC** (2,100 vs 100,000) and 4 vs 0 badges. The 100,000-XC record has far less activity history (10 entries vs 58) and looks like leftover test/mistake data rather than legitimate progress, but I'm not deciding that unilaterally — same policy as the still-open Hannah Rodrigues ~2,050 XC question above. The code fix stops NEW duplication; it does NOT delete or merge the two existing stale cloud rows, and does not touch either XC value. If the login-screen refresh is still happening after this patch deploys, that means the live symptom has a separate cause I haven't found from code alone — I need a screenshot, screen recording, or the browser console output (DevTools → Console tab, any red errors, especially anything repeating) from that tab to chase it further; I don't have a way to see a live tester's screen directly.
- HOST ACTIONS: (1) decide which NeuroFlux XC total (2,100 or 100,000) is correct, and whether to delete the loser row from `app_data` — I can execute the cleanup once you confirm. (2) if the refresh is still happening after this deploys, grab a screenshot/console log from that tab so I can keep chasing it.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.70 — LOGIN SCREEN'S EVERY-BOOT ROSTER CACHE NO LONGER RE-WRITES EMBEDDED PHOTOS TO localStorage (Aug 16, found while still chasing the NeuroFlux "flashes white and reloads" report — Ennis: "fix it now" with no screenshot/console log available)

- CONTEXT: v1.69 fixed a real, confirmed duplicate-roster-record bug (see above), but Ennis confirmed the login-screen refresh was **still happening** after that shipped, and characterized the symptom precisely: "whole page flashes white and reloads." I asked three separate times for a DevTools screenshot/console log/incognito-test result to pin down whether this is in-app JS or something external (device-management extension, OS low-memory tab kill, network redirect) — none has been provided, and every in-app JS reload trigger I can find by reading the code (`location.reload()`, `location.href`/`.replace()`/`.assign()`, a meta-refresh tag, a service worker) is absent from the login/boot path entirely (all 5+4 matches elsewhere in the file sit behind explicit user clicks — sign-out, cloud restore, exit-preview — never auto-fire). Rather than keep asking for evidence that isn't coming, went back into the boot path itself looking for a REAL, fixable cost that could plausibly explain a self-sustaining crash-reload loop with no explicit "reload" call anywhere in the code — because a genuine tab crash (OS/Chrome kills the renderer for memory) IS a full navigation-level reload from the page's own perspective, and if the SAME expensive boot step re-runs immediately after that reload, that alone produces "flashes white and reloads, over and over" with no JS-triggered redirect ever executing.
- CONFIRMED (data, live Supabase query): `app_data` currently holds 156 `pflx_player_%` rows totaling ~2.5MB of JSON. 12 of those 156 embed a base64 `image` field; combined they account for ~2.36MB of that total. The single largest: `pflx_player_player-import-1774891628716-28` at just over 1,000,000 bytes (~1MB) for its `image` field alone — i.e. one player's photo is nearly half the entire roster's data weight.
- ROOT CAUSE (code): `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud()` — called from `initLogin()`, i.e. on the LOGIN screen, before anyone has signed in — pulls the full `data` blob (photo included) for every roster row on every single page load (`.select('key, data, updated_at').like('key','pflx_player_%').limit(2000)`), then, after merging into the in-memory `PLAYERS` array, `JSON.stringify()`'d the ENTIRE resulting roster — photos and all — and wrote it to `localStorage` as the `hydratePlayers`-on-next-boot cache. The login screen itself never renders any of these photos (it only needs id/brand/name/pin for the brand datalist and PIN check), so none of that image weight was ever needed in the cache — it was pure, avoidable, recurring cost: a multi-MB string built and synchronously written to localStorage on the main thread, every single time the login screen loads, with no upper bound as more testers add profile photos over time. On a memory-constrained device (a school Chromebook is the likely tester hardware here) this is a plausible, self-sustaining contributor to exactly the reported loop: boot does the expensive fetch+stringify+write → tab gets killed for memory → Chrome auto-reloads the tab → boot immediately repeats the same expensive step → crashes again.
- FIX: `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud()`'s localStorage-cache-sync step now strips any `image` field over 2,000 characters (`_pflxStripHeavyForCache`) before writing — both for records touched in this pass AND for every already-cached entry (`saved.map(_pflxStripHeavyForCache)`), so a device that already has a bloated cache from before this patch shrinks it on its very next boot, not just going forward. The in-memory `PLAYERS` merge is untouched — full photos still load into memory and render normally everywhere else in the app (profile views, cards, calls); only what gets serialized into the pre-login localStorage cache changed.
- HONEST FRAMING: this is a real, verified inefficiency directly on the reported screen, and closing it is a legitimate defensive fix regardless of outcome — but it is NOT confirmed to be the actual cause of the reload loop, since I still have no direct evidence (screenshot/console/network capture) of what's happening on that device. If the loop continues after this deploys, that still points toward an external cause (device-management extension, network/captive-portal redirect) rather than anything left in this boot path — I've now covered both the JS-trigger angle (v1.69's exhaustive grep, still clean) and the plausible memory-pressure angle (this patch). At that point a screenshot or the incognito/different-device test result becomes the only way to move further; there's no more code-only lead I can chase blind.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 69 → 70 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 14 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) 9 scenarios in a live-code test extracting `pflxIdentityFetchRosterFromCloud` verbatim: static checks confirm the strip helper is present, applied to already-cached entries (not just newly-touched ones), and that the in-memory `PLAYERS` merge still uses the full unstripped record; behavioral tests reproduce the real NeuroFlux-scale image size (1,001,678 chars) and confirm a fetched record with a huge image caches without `image` (all other fields intact, resulting JSON well under 2KB), a pre-existing bloated cache entry gets trimmed on the next boot even with no matching fetch that pass, small/placeholder image strings (≤2000 chars) are left alone, and records with no image field at all are unaffected. All 9 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — pure client-side cache optimization, no data migration. If NeuroFlux's device is still looping after this deploys, the single most useful thing you can send is a phone photo of the DevTools Network tab (or even just the Console tab) taken WHILE it's happening — that's the one piece of evidence that would tell me for certain whether this is still a PFLX code issue or something on that specific device/network.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.71 — UNIVERSAL PORTFOLIO VIEWER, APPLY-TO-JOIN FOR PROGRAMS/PROJECTS (+ PLACEHOLDER PAID CHECKOUT), PLAYER-FACING SEASON/PROGRAM TABS, COMPLETION-APPROVAL SWEEP FOR PROGRAMS/CHECKPOINTS/PROJECTS (Aug 17, Ennis-requested — largest single-turn feature set to date)

- ASK (Ennis, verbatim across several messages): "Portfolios should be viewable to anyone in PFLX with no need to publish... I should be able to click on a brandname anywhere in PFLX and it should directly open the players portfolio." / "lets add an apply feature to Programs and Projects... when a cohort is attached... they can see it but can't officially open or join until they apply. Then the Guest Host, Instructor Host, or any other Host can see the players applying and accept based on either payment or viewing their portfolio." / "apple pay, google pay, samsung pay like feature for paid programs and projects" / "on the Player dashboard, they should also see a Season and Program tab... seen by all players... they just cant enter unless their cohort is attached and apply or pay is bypassed" / mid-build follow-up: "there is no End date, I also should be able to select active checkpoints. Checkpoint cadence should be optional... what happens when the program ends? There should be a program approval process for each player who participated. If a player has completed all tasks within the Program by the deadline then they should pop up for approval. I should also be able to bypass that as well. This should be the same for Checkpoints, and Projects." Card-size sliders on the player dashboard and the Mimic-feature rebuild were also raised this turn but are explicitly DEFERRED — see bottom of this entry.

**1. Universal Portfolio Viewer** — `pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio(idOrBrand)` is now the one entry point for "view anyone's portfolio without publishing": resolves a player by id or brand (`pflxResolvePlayer`), fetches their live portfolio data (new reliable Supabase key `pflx_portfolio_<id>`, falling back to the legacy `portfolio_<id>` key, then localStorage), sanitizes it (strips `privateBio`, respects `hideRealName`) via `pflxSanitizePortfolioForViewing`, and renders a read-only modal. `pflxBrandLink(player, text)` is the reusable "clickable brand name → opens their portfolio" helper. `portfolioSaveData()` now also writes directly to Supabase (`pflx_portfolio_<id>`) instead of relying solely on the X-Coin iframe bridge, so the viewer has a reliable source even for players who never opened X-Coin. Wired into the new Apply-to-Join Approvals cards (a "View Portfolio" link per applicant/completion, satisfying "accept based on either payment or viewing their portfolio") — wiring it into the other ~14 brand-name surfaces found by research (Player Management, Live Session roster, DarkCampus/PFLX Chat, Leaderboard, Scouting) is a documented fast-follow, not done this patch.

**2. Apply-to-Join for Programs & Projects** — new `applyEnabled` + `price` fields on both Program and Project forms. New top-level `mcApplications` collection (fully wired into the generic MC cloud-sync system — declaration, boot-load, `mcSaveData`, `MC_CLOUD_TYPES`, `_mcCollectionFor`, `_mcApplyCollection`, same pattern as every sibling collection). Player-facing `mcApplyToProgramOrProject(type, itemId)` creates a `pending` application (blocked while a pending/approved one already exists, but a **rejected** application never blocks a fresh reapply). Host flow matches Ennis's explicit ordering — "host reviews first, then payment": `mcApproveApplication(id)` finalizes enrollment immediately for a free item, or sets `paymentStatus:'awaiting_payment'` for a priced one (enrollment does NOT happen yet); `mcMarkApplicationPaid(id)` is the placeholder checkout — a host-only "mark paid" button that finalizes enrollment. Per Ennis's explicit choice ("not yet — build a placeholder for now"), there is no real payment processor: no Stripe, no Apple Pay/Google Pay/Samsung Pay. The data model (`price`, `paymentStatus`) is shaped so a real Stripe Checkout with the browser Payment Request API (Apple Pay + Google Pay — I told Ennis Samsung Pay isn't realistically supportable for web checkout the way those two are, and he didn't object) can slot in later without touching `mcApplications`' shape. Approved application → `_mcFinalizeApplicationEnrollment` pushes the player id into `Program.enrolledPlayers[]` (new field, mirrors Project's existing `assignedPlayers[]`) or `Project.assignedPlayers[]` directly — same field the pre-existing cohort-based access check already reads, so an approved application grants entry exactly like cohort membership does.
  - Entry gate: `pflxPlayerCanEnterItem(item, type)` — host tiers always enter; a **cohort match always grants direct entry regardless of `applyEnabled`** (this is my own reconciliation of two of Ennis's messages that read slightly differently in isolation — worth double-checking against what he actually wants once he sees it live, flagged to him already); otherwise an approved (and paid, if priced) application is the only path in. `pflxPlayerApplicationState(item, type)` reads the applicant's **most recent** matching record (last-pushed, not first-found) so a rejected-then-reapplied player's card shows `pending`, not stale `rejected`.
  - Approvals integration: applications and awaiting-payment items ride the existing unified `mcApprovals` card system (`mcApproveItem`/`mcRejectItem`/`_mcApprovalAllowed`/`_mcApprovalActionAllowed` all gained an `'application'` case; new `CAP['approve.application']` = same 5 tiers as task approval). Awaiting-payment applications surface a `Mark Paid — Enroll` button right on the card.

**3. Player-facing Season/Program tabs + universal Program/Project visibility** — the Seasons and Programs sidebar buttons lost `mc-host-only` (players now see both). New `ppRenderPrograms`/`ppRenderProgramDetail` (Program's own player-facing views — lists every Program, card shows OPEN / 🔒 COHORT REQUIRED / ⏳ PENDING / 💳 PAY $X, "Open" drills into that Program's checkpoints via the existing `checkpoint.programId` back-pointer). `ppRenderCheckpointDetail`'s project list is now universal-visibility (was cohort-filtered) with the same lock/apply states per project; `ppRenderProjectDetail` gained a top-of-function entry guard so a direct deep-link to a project a player hasn't entered bounces to a locked/apply screen instead of the full detail. The existing single-season `ppRenderSeason` view (unchanged) is now reachable from the sidebar for players, not just hosts.

**4. Program form fixes (mid-build follow-up)** — added the missing **End Date** field (drives the completion sweep below); **Checkpoint Cadence is now optional** (blank = no cadence-driven auto-generation, rely on manually-attached checkpoints instead — `mcSeasonGenerateCheckpoints`'s own "Generate Checkpoints" button still defaults to 2wk if clicked with cadence blank); new **"Attach Existing Checkpoints"** multi-select writes the reverse pointer (`checkpoint.programId`) directly from the Program form (in addition to the pre-existing per-checkpoint Program dropdown) — single source of truth either way a checkpoint gets attached, and the picker only ever offers checkpoints that are unattached or already attached to this Program, so it can never steal one from another Program.

**5. Completion-approval sweep for Programs, Checkpoints, AND Projects** — direct answer to "what happens when the program ends?" `mcCheckCompletionApprovals()` (same idempotent-sweep architecture as the existing v1.44 lateness-tax sweep and v1.46 project-reminder sweep: host-gated, runs off the 3-minute MC health interval AND once every time a host opens the Approvals tab, dedup marker lives on the record itself so re-running never re-queues). For each Checkpoint/Project/Program whose deadline (`endDate`/`dueDate`) has passed, every player who has completed 100% of their assigned/required work in it (Checkpoint: `pflxPlayerCheckpointProgress`; Project: `pflxProjectCompletion` per-assignee units; Program: aggregated across every checkpoint linked via `cp.programId`) gets pushed into the unified Approvals queue as a `type:'completion'` card (with a "View Portfolio" link, same as Apply-to-Join) for the host to sign off on. New host-toggle **"Skip completion approval — auto-approve players who finish on time"** on all three forms (Program/Checkpoint/Project) bypasses the queue entirely — the player is pre-marked `approved` instead of `pending`, satisfying "I should also be able to bypass that as well." Reject just means "not yet" — no auto-requeue on more work being submitted later in this pass (documented limitation below).
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 70 → 71 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified two ways: (1) syntax gate clean — all 13 non-empty inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. (2) Two live-code behavioral test files extracting the actual functions verbatim from `preview.html`: 21 scenarios covering the full apply→approve→pay→enroll state machine, the duplicate-application guard (blocks while pending, allows reapply after rejection), and the entry gate (cohort bypass, locked-without-cohort-or-app, approved-but-unpaid still locked, approved+paid unlocks) — all 21 PASS; 9 scenarios covering the completion sweep (fully-approved player queued, partial player not queued, `skipCompletionApproval` auto-approves instead of queuing, 3x-rerun idempotency produces exactly one record, future deadline queues nothing, project per-assignee completion, Program only queues once EVERY one of its checkpoints is fully approved) — all 9 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS / KNOWN LIMITATIONS:
  - The cohort-bypasses-apply rule (§2) is my own synthesis reconciling two of your messages — please sanity-check it against what you actually meant once you see it live; it's the one genuinely ambiguous call in this whole patch.
  - No real payment processor — `Mark Paid` is a manual host action. Flag when you want real Stripe/Apple Pay/Google Pay wired in; the data model is ready for it.
  - A rejected completion-approval record does not currently reopen automatically if the player later finishes more work — a host would need to manually revisit it (no UI for that yet).
  - Card-size sliders on the player dashboard (Ennis: "give the player dashboard the resize sliders much like the host dashboard") — NOT done this patch. Deferred as its own fast-follow since the player views are prose/list-style rather than the uniform card grids the existing slider engine targets.
  - Portfolio-viewer wiring beyond the new Approvals cards (Player Management, Live Session roster, DarkCampus/PFLX Chat, Leaderboard, Scouting — ~14 more surfaces found by research) — NOT done this patch.
  - **Mimic feature fix (Ennis: "fix my Mimic feature from Master Host controls only... full dashboard mimicry... Host make a change then it will officially affect the players dashboard") — NOT started.** Flagged as security-sensitive (a host live-editing another player's real data) and deliberately scoped as its own separate patch rather than folded into this already-large one.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.72 — PROJECT EDIT CRASH FIX (bad `team` data) + PROJECTS NO LONGER REQUIRE A TASK TO SAVE (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis reported an error trying to edit "Checkpoint Beta: Project Management & Administration." Two screenshots followed — the first showed a red `PFLX Error Log` banner (illegible in the screenshot text); the second, taken while reproducing, showed the actual dialog: `www.prototypeflx.com says — A Project needs at least one Task. Please select a Task below, or create one first from the Tasks tab.`
- ROOT CAUSE (two separate issues found while investigating):
  1. **Real crash, confirmed via Supabase**: `mcShowProjectForm()`'s field-population line `(p.team || []).join(', ')` assumes `team` is always an array. A live query against `app_data.projects` found 5 of 7 projects — all 5 "Checkpoint Beta: …" projects — with `team` stored as a plain **string** (the department name, e.g. `"Project Management & Administration"`), not an array. `"string" || []` evaluates to the string, and `.join` doesn't exist on strings → `TypeError: p.team.join is not a function`, thrown the instant the Edit form tried to populate — before the host ever saw the form. This is almost certainly what the (illegible) first error banner was showing.
  2. **The actual dialog in the second screenshot** is a pre-existing, deliberate "structural rule" in `mcSaveProjectForm()` that blocked saving any Project with zero Tasks checked. Ennis's follow-up message confirmed this needed to change: *"I want to be able to create projects without adding a task. This allows better preparation."* The equivalent rule for Checkpoints was already removed back on July 9 for the same reason (`mcSaveCheckpointForm` — "Empty checkpoints are allowed… template holders… customized later") — Projects had simply been missed.
- FIX:
  1. `mcShowProjectForm()` (~line 38224): team-field population now checks `Array.isArray(p.team)` first, falls back to the raw string if it's a string, else `''`. `mcSaveProjectForm()` always writes `team` back out as a proper array from the comma-split input, so every project self-heals the first time it's re-saved through the fixed form.
  2. **Data surgery**: migrated all 5 malformed `team` string fields in `app_data.projects` (Supabase project `hyxiagexyptzvetqjmnj`) to single-element arrays in one transaction (`jsonb_set(elem,'{team}',jsonb_build_array(elem->'team'))` for every element where `jsonb_typeof(team)='string'`), verified with a SELECT after — all 5 now read as arrays (`["Project Management & Administration"]` etc.), matching what a normal save has always produced. No other fields touched.
  3. Removed the "Project needs at least one Task" block from `mcSaveProjectForm()` entirely. Checked the two places that assumed `totalTasks`/`taskIds.length` downstream — the Mission Progress panel already only renders `if (totalTasks > 0 || xcTotalPool > 0)`, and this patch's own v1.71 completion-approval sweep (`_pflxPlayerCompletedProject`) already requires `comp.total > 0` before it will ever queue a player — so a 0-task Project just renders as an empty shell with no progress panel and never spuriously "completes." No other guard was needed.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 71 → 72 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean — all 14 inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check` (before and after both edits). 5-case unit test against the extracted team-resolution logic (array → joined string, string → passthrough, null/undefined/empty-array → `''`) — all 5 PASS. Confirmed the old blocking alert string no longer exists in the file. Confirmed via Supabase SELECT that all 5 previously-broken projects now carry `team` as an array.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — the crash is fixed and the 5 already-broken projects were repaired directly in the cloud data, so they should open cleanly now without needing a re-save.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.73 — MIMIC FIX: MASTER-HOST-ONLY GATE, FULL FIELD FIDELITY, NAV-GATING SYNC (Aug 17, Ennis)
- ASK: *"fix my Mimic feature from Master Host controls only. I should be able to mimic anyones full dashboard, exactly how theirs look in all aspects. This should allow the host to provide extra support on any profile. This mimic feature will allow the host to control a players profile in its entirety. If the Host make a change then it will officially affect the players dashboard."*
- Researched the existing Mimic mechanism (`preview.html`, the self-contained IIFE around `pflxMimicEnter/Exit/Render`) against three threads in the ask and found one real bug per thread:
  1. **"From Master Host controls only"** — the entry gate (`isAdmin()`) allowed ANY host role — admin, host, teacher, or instructor — not just Master. Replaced with `isMasterHost()`, which defers to the real TIERED HOST ACCESS engine (`window.pflxHostTier(session) === 'master'`) instead of a private, looser string check — so it tracks the same tier resolution used everywhere else in the Console (`legacy role:'admin'` → master tier, `role:'host'` → admin tier, etc.), with a same-as-before fallback only if the tier engine hasn't loaded.
  2. **"Exactly how theirs looks in all aspects"** — two separate causes:
     - `buildPlayerSession(p)` only copied a handful of fields (id/brand/name/email/pin/role/cohort/xc/totalXcoin/digitalBadges/badgeCounts/image/level/studioId/pathway/tier). Compared field-for-field against the real `loginUser()` session construction (same source array, `mcPlayers`, so every field loginUser reads is present on the mimic target too) and found it was silently dropping `cohorts[]` (falling back to a single 'PlayerPool'), `slogan`, `interests[]`, a real `badges[]` array (only a count survived), `rankOverride`, and the entire rank-resolve pass (`rank`/`rankIcon`/`rankName`/`rankLevel`) that `getPlayerLevel()` and the rank-gated nav-lock system read from `activeSession.rank`. Expanded `buildPlayerSession` to mirror `loginUser` exactly, including the same rank-resolve logic (rankOverride → `mcPflxRanks` lookup, else `getRankForXC(xc)`), and added `onboardingComplete`/`onboarded` (read by the identity-broadcast payload sub-apps use to decide whether to show their own onboarding wizard).
     - **Root cause of the nav-lock mismatch specifically**: `window.pflxApplyAppGating()` (the rank-gated app-unlock pass that adds/removes `.pflx-locked` on nav buttons per `getPlayerLevel()`) was only ever re-run through an EARLIER wrapper of `window.pflxSetRole` — but a LATER, full reassignment of `window.pflxSetRole` (further down the file) silently replaced that wrapper instead of extending it, so the app-gating pass stopped re-running on ANY role switch, Mimic included. A mimicking host saw the HOST's own unlock state, not the mimicked player's. Fixed by calling `pflxApplyAppGating()` directly at the end of the real (later) `pflxSetRole`, so there's one source of truth instead of a wrap chain that can be silently clobbered again.
  3. **"If the Host make a change then it will officially affect the player's dashboard"** — traced two representative native write paths: task submission (`ppRenderTaskDetail`'s submit handler writes `playerId: activeSession.id` directly into the shared `mcTasks` array, synced via `mcSaveData('tasks')`) and portfolio edits (`portfolioSaveData/LoadData`, keyed off `activeSession.brand || activeSession.name`). Both already resolve correctly during Mimic because `buildPlayerSession` sets `id`/`brand`/`name` to the REAL player's values — so this was already working and needed no code change, just field-fidelity (item 2) to actually verify it end-to-end.
  - Also expanded the two `pflx_user` localStorage writes (Mimic enter + exit) to carry the same widened field set, so sub-apps reading the identity bridge (X-Coin, Core Pathways) see the mimicked player's full profile too, not just the Console's own UI.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 72 → 73 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean — all 14 inline `<script>` blocks pass `node --check`. Live-code behavioral test extracting `isMasterHost()` and `buildPlayerSession()` verbatim from the file: 8 scenarios — master tier passes, admin/cohost/instructor/guest/no-tier all correctly rejected, fallback-when-tier-engine-absent still restricts to legacy `role:'admin'`, full-record field fidelity (cohorts/slogan/interests/badges/rank all present and correct), sparse-legacy-record graceful defaults, rankOverride taking precedence over xc-derived rank — all 8 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS / KNOWN LIMITATIONS:
  - Mimic's player picker (the X-Bot panel search list) still only lists accounts with `role === 'player'/'Student'/'student'` — mimicking a HOST account isn't reachable from the UI yet, even though `buildPlayerSession` would now carry `hostTier`/`managedScope` correctly if it were. Flag if you want that opened up.
  - This was investigation-heavy — I did not find (and did not go looking for) any additional data-flow gaps beyond the three threads above. If something still looks/behaves differently while mimicking after this patch, tell me exactly what and I'll trace that specific path next rather than guess.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.74 (+ X-Coin) — PORTFOLIO CLICK NO LONGER DEAD-ENDS THROUGH THE OLD PUBLISH-GATED PAGE (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis clicked a player (@NEUROFLUX) to view their portfolio and landed on two dead-end screens in sequence: X-Coin's own "Portfolio moved — Redirecting…" stub, then the Console's "Portfolio not found — No published portfolio exists yet for @NEUROFLUX. The owner needs to open their portfolio in the PFLX Platform and click PUBLISH." His ask: *"It should open directly with no middle ground."*
- ROOT CAUSE: X-Coin still has its old `/profile/[id]` route wired up from its Leaderboard (player + admin), Player Management, and side-nav "view portfolio" clicks (`app/admin/players/page.tsx`, `app/admin/leaderboard/page.tsx`, `app/player/leaderboard/page.tsx`, `app/components/SideNav.tsx` — all still `router.push('/profile/${id}')`). That route was already stubbed out months ago in favor of the Console's portfolio, and correctly does — but it redirects (via a `pflx_navigate` postMessage the Console's shell listens for) to the Console's **legacy, Publish-gated** `/<brand>` page — the exact page the v1.71 Universal Portfolio Viewer was built to make optional ("Portfolios should be viewable to anyone in PFLX with no need to publish. Publish is for viewing outside of PFLX."). Any player who's never clicked Publish (the common case, since v1.71 made it unnecessary for in-PFLX viewing) dead-ends in "not found." The v1.71 fix wired brand-name clicks INSIDE the Console to the new no-publish modal (`pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio`), but never touched this older cross-app hop from X-Coin, which was still pointed at the pre-v1.71 destination.
- FIX:
  1. `pflx-xcoin-app/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx` — when reached inside the Console iframe (the normal case for every call site above), now posts a new `pflx_open_portfolio` message with the raw `playerId` instead of resolving a brand and requesting a `pflx_navigate` to the old gated URL. Renders nothing (`return null`) while iframed — the parent takes over instantly, no interstitial screen. Dropped the now-unnecessary `mockUsers`/`localStorage` brand-lookup entirely (the Console resolves the id itself, it already has the full roster). Kept a plain, non-dead-ending fallback for the rare case of hitting this route standalone (outside the Console iframe): a pointer back to the Platform instead of a broken "OPEN PORTFOLIO" link to the old gated page.
  2. `pflx-platform-check/preview.html`'s cross-app `postMessage` listener (the same handler documented as already anticipating "e.g. X-Coin's profile route redirecting to the Console's unified portfolio") gained a new case: `pflx_open_portfolio` → `window.pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio(playerId)` — the exact same no-publish-required modal a brand-name click inside the Console itself opens.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` (bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 73 → 74, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged `2026.08`) and `pflx-xcoin-app/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx`.
- Verified: syntax gate clean on `preview.html` (all 14 `<script>` blocks). `tsc --noEmit` clean on the rewritten X-Coin page (no type errors). Live-code behavioral test extracting the new message-handler block verbatim: 5 scenarios — playerId forwarded correctly, numeric id stringified, other message types ignored, a message missing `playerId` ignored, no throw when `pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio` isn't yet defined — all 5 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Fixes every "view portfolio" click that routes through X-Coin's `/profile/[id]` (Leaderboard, Player Management, side nav) in one place — no per-surface changes needed on the X-Coin side beyond this file.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.75 (+ X-Coin) — PORTFOLIO VIEWER NOW SHOWS THE FULL PAGE, AND CLOSING IT NO LONGER LEAVES A BLANK SCREEN (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis tried the fixed portfolio flow from v1.74 on @NEUROFLUX and got two follow-on problems: (1) it opened, but only as a small card — avatar, name, XC, badge count, "No projects added" — nothing like the rich "MY PORTFOLIO" page he sees for his own brand (banner, bio, 5-tile stat grid, Projects & Links, Completed Tasks, Badge Portfolio); (2) after clicking the X to close it, the screen went blank instead of returning to the Leaderboard he'd clicked from. His ask: *"I want it to show the full portfolio much like I show here from TheTomorrowTeacher."*
- ROOT CAUSE (two separate bugs, one per repo):
  1. **Console — wrong renderer.** `pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio` (the v1.71 Universal Portfolio Viewer) was always calling `pflxRenderPortfolioModalHtml`, a deliberately small "quick-look" card — avatar/name/2 chips/short project list — never the full page layout the owner's own `portfolio-view` section renders via `portfolioRender()`. That richer pipeline (`portfolioRender`, `portfolioRenderTasks`, `portfolioRenderBadges`, `portfolioGetTaskStats`) is hardwired to `activeSession` (reads `PLAYERS.find(id===activeSession.id)`, localStorage keyed by `activeSession.brand`) — it was never built to show anyone but the currently logged-in user, so it couldn't just be pointed at another player's id.
  2. **X-Coin — blank page left behind.** The v1.74 fix had this route ask the Console to open its modal, then render `null` on the assumption "the iframe stays wherever it was." It doesn't — every "view portfolio" click (Leaderboard ×2, Player Management, side nav) is a real `router.push('/profile/${id}')`, so the X-Coin iframe's own location genuinely becomes this now-blank route. The Console's modal covered that up while open; closing it exposed the blank page underneath — exactly what Ennis saw.
- FIX:
  1. `preview.html`: replaced `pflxRenderPortfolioModalHtml` with `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml(player, data)`, which renders the SAME sections the owner's own portfolio page shows — banner, header (avatar/name/tagline/rank+cohort+XC+pathway+studio chips), Brand Bio, a 5-tile stat grid (Digital Badges, Lifetime XC, Evo Rank, Projects, Tasks Done), Projects & Links (reusing the existing `portfolioRenderProjectMedia` for embeds), Completed Tasks, and Badge Portfolio — but entirely read-only (no EDIT/PREVIEW/PUBLISH controls, since this is always someone else's portfolio) and sourced from the `player`/`data` params instead of `activeSession`, leaving the owner-only edit pipeline completely untouched. Badges pull from the player record's own `badgeCounts`/`badges` fields (already per-player). Completed Tasks needed a new per-player path since the existing one reads an `activeSession`-scoped localStorage key: added `pflxPlayerTaskStats(player)` and `pflxPlayerCompletedTasksHtml(player)`, both sourced from the global `mcTasks` roster filtered through the existing `pflxTaskStateForPlayer(task, playerId)` resolver (already correctly handles per-player submission matching) — both degrade to 0/"no completed tasks yet" rather than throwing if `mcTasks` isn't populated. The modal itself grew from a 520px card to a 960px scrollable panel (own portfolio's `max-width:960px`) with a viewport-fixed close button so it stays reachable regardless of scroll position.
  2. `pflx-xcoin-app/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx`: after posting `pflx_open_portfolio` to the parent, now also calls `router.back()` (guarded on `window.history.length > 1`) to pop this route off the iframe's own history — since every click that lands here arrived via `router.push()`, one step back returns the iframe to the actual page the click came from, so the Console's modal sits on top of the correct background and closing it reveals that page, not a blank one.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` (bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 74 → 75, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged `2026.08`) and `pflx-xcoin-app/app/profile/[id]/page.tsx`.
- Verified: syntax gate clean on `preview.html` (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). `tsc --noEmit` clean on the X-Coin page (stubbed `next/navigation` types, real `@types/react`). Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml`, `pflxPlayerTaskStats`, `pflxPlayerCompletedTasksHtml`, and `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim from the file — 27 scenarios: empty-player renders every "nothing yet" state without throwing; full player renders real name (hideRealName:false)/bio/banner/project card with embed+url+tags/pathway+studio chips/cohort chip/correct rank tile/badge category cards/earned badge artwork; task stats and Completed Tasks correctly filter to ONLY the target player's approved tasks (verified a second player's task is excluded); `mcTasks` undefined/missing degrades to 0 and an empty-state message rather than throwing; `pflxPlayerTaskStats(null)` never throws — all 27 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Every "view portfolio" surface across the Console and X-Coin now opens the same full read-only page, and closing it returns you to wherever you clicked from.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.76 — BADGE ARTWORK MISSING WHEN badgeCounts AND badges[] DRIFT APART (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: right after v1.75 shipped, Ennis compared two portfolios: @NEUROFLUX showed its "Earned Badges" artwork grid correctly (4 badges with real art/names), but @VYBE showed the "Official Certifications: 1" category tally card with NO earned-badge artwork section below it at all — as if the badge didn't exist, even though the category count said it did.
- ROOT CAUSE: confirmed via a direct Supabase query against `pflx_mc_players` — VYBE's record has `badgeCounts.signature: 1` (and `digitalBadges: 2`, a third disagreeing number) but `badges: []` — a genuinely EMPTY array, not a missing field. `hmcEditPlayer` (Player Management's Edit modal, ~line 66955) already has self-heal logic for exactly this kind of drift — "legacy badgeCounts → synthesized entries" — but its guard was `if (!Array.isArray(p.badges))`, which only fires when `badges` is missing entirely. An empty array passes `Array.isArray` (`Array.isArray([]) === true`), so that self-heal silently never ran for a record in VYBE's exact state — present-but-empty. `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` (the new v1.75 read path for viewing any player's badge portfolio) inherited the same blind spot: it only ever showed badges actually resolvable from `player.badges`, so a category count with zero backing refs rendered zero artwork cards, no error, nothing wrong-looking — just silently incomplete. This was invisible before v1.75 because the old mini-card modal never showed individual badge artwork, only a single combined count.
- FIX (same shortfall-topping algorithm applied in both places it was needed):
  1. `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` (~line 56922, the portfolio viewer's badge renderer): after resolving `player.badges` against the catalog, now walks each category and — using the existing canonical `_pflxBadgeCategoryKey` helper to bucket real resolved badges by category — tops up the earned-badge list with generic placeholder entries (icon tile, "‹Category› Badge #N", no XC) for whatever shortfall remains between `badgeCounts` and the real resolved list. A fully-consistent record (like NEUROFLUX) synthesizes nothing — verified explicitly.
  2. `hmcEditPlayer`'s self-heal (~line 66955): same fix, one level up — the guard no longer only checks "is `badges` an array"; it now tops up any category's shortfall the same way, so opening Edit Player on an affected account (and saving) permanently repairs the record instead of only patching the read-side display.
  - Deliberately did NOT touch the live VYBE Supabase record directly — unlike the v1.72 `team`-field data surgery, there's no way to know from `badgeCounts` alone which SPECIFIC catalog badge VYBE actually earned in the Official Certifications category, so writing a real (but potentially wrong) badge id would misattribute credit. The synthesized placeholder is honest about what's known (a signature-tier badge is owed) without fabricating which one; a host can open Edit Player → award the correct specific badge to replace the placeholder with real artwork/name/XC.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 75 → 76 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim — 11 scenarios: VYBE's exact real data (badgeCounts.signature:1, badges:[]) now renders both the category card AND a synthesized "Official Certification Badge #1" artwork tile; NEUROFLUX's exact real data (4 real catalog badges, fully consistent) renders all 4 real badges with zero phantom synthesis; a partial-drift case (1 real badge, category claims 2) tops up exactly the shortfall without duplicating the real one; a fully-empty player is unchanged ("No badges earned yet."); `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml(null)` never throws — all 11 PASS. A second isolated test against the exact `hmcEditPlayer` synthesis block (copied verbatim, diffed against the shipped file to confirm no transcription drift) — 3 scenarios: VYBE-shaped present-but-empty array now tops up, an already-consistent record does not duplicate, the original missing-array case still works — all 3 PASS. 14/14 total.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required to see badge artwork appear again on affected profiles. Optional cleanup: open Player Management → Edit Player on VYBE (and any other player who might be in the same state) and re-award the actual specific Official Certification badge they earned, which will replace the generic placeholder with the real name/artwork/XC once saved.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.77 — NEW CROSS-APP BADGES (X-COIN) NEVER LANDED IN THE PORTFOLIO'S BADGE ARTWORK (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: right after v1.76 shipped, Ennis reported a third badge issue on the same player: *"Its also not loading all badges as well. I just gave Neuroflux 2 new badges and it didnt show."* Screenshots showed NEUROFLUX's XC/rank had jumped (2,100 → 201,950, Player → Director) but the portfolio still showed only the original 4 badges.
