- ROOT CAUSE: confirmed via a direct Supabase query against both `pflx_mc_players` and NEUROFLUX's own per-id row (`pflx_player_<id>`) — `digitalBadges` had moved 5 → 6 (only +1, not +2) while `badgeCounts` (sum 4) and `badges` (length 4, the same 4 real catalog ids from before) were completely unchanged. Reading NEUROFLUX's own activity log nailed it: the most recent entry was `data_bus_update` with `keys: [xc, totalXcoin, digitalBadges, level]` and `source: "xcoin"`. That's `PflxDataBus.applyUpdate()` being invoked by the Console's `pflx_player_update` postMessage handler (~line 61497), which just forwards whatever `changes` object a sub-app sends verbatim into `WRITABLE_FIELDS`. X-Coin's own internal schema tracks `digitalBadges` as a plain number — it has no concept of the Console's `badges[]`/`badgeCounts` shapes — so whatever award X-Coin runs on its own side bumps that number and syncs it across, but never sends `badges`/`badgeCounts` in the same payload. This is the cross-app "Schema splits" gotcha from the Handoff's own gotcha list, now caught in the act: a THIRD kind of badge drift, distinct from the two v1.76 already covers (which only ever reconciles `badges[]` against `badgeCounts` — it never once looks at `digitalBadges`, so a record where `badges`/`badgeCounts` agree with EACH OTHER but disagree with `digitalBadges`, exactly NEUROFLUX's case, sailed straight through v1.76 undetected).
- FIX (write-time root cause + display-time safety net for records that already drifted before this shipped, matching the v1.76 pattern):
  1. `PflxDataBus.applyUpdate` (~line 65231, the single funnel every cross-app partial update — including X-Coin's — passes through): when an incoming `changes` object raises `digitalBadges` without also supplying `badges`, it now tops up the player's real `badges[]`/`badgeCounts` with generic placeholders (bucketed to `primary` — a bare number carries no category signal) to close the gap, before the update is broadcast/persisted. This stops the drift at its actual source going forward, for X-Coin or any other sub-app that sends a `digitalBadges`-only update.
  2. `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` (~line 56922): added a second top-up pass, after the existing v1.76 per-category one, that compares `player.digitalBadges` against the final earned-badge count and synthesizes any remaining shortfall — so any record that already drifted before this patch (NEUROFLUX's stored data won't self-heal until it next passes through `applyUpdate` or `hmcEditPlayer`) still displays correctly today.
  3. `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml`'s stat-tile badge count (~line 56790): was `totalBadges || player.digitalBadges`, which only fell back to the legacy number when `totalBadges` was exactly 0 — silently wrong when `totalBadges` is non-zero but still behind (4 vs. 6, NEUROFLUX's exact case). Changed to `Math.max(totalBadges, player.digitalBadges || 0)` so the tile always matches what the badge grid below it actually renders.
  4. Bonus fix found while tracing this, same class of bug: `broadcastPlayerChange`'s mirror of an edited player into `mcPlayers` (~line 64958, feeds the `pflx_mc_players` cloud roster) copied `digitalBadges` and `badgeCounts` but never `badges` itself — so a Player Management badge edit correctly fixed the PLAYERS-side per-id record but silently never reached the bulk `mcPlayers` roster's own badge artwork. Added `badges` to the mirrored field list. Not the root cause of NEUROFLUX's specific report (the portfolio viewer reads from `PLAYERS` first, which was already correct), but a real, adjacent gap worth closing now that it's been found.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 76 → 77 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks, `node --check`-equivalent pass on every inline block). Live-code behavioral test extracting `PflxDataBus`'s `applyUpdate` verbatim — 15 scenarios: NEUROFLUX's exact real-world update (`{xc,totalXcoin,digitalBadges:6,level}`, no badges/badgeCounts) tops `badges[]` up from 4 to 6 with generic Primary placeholders while leaving the 4 real ids untouched and badgeCounts summing correctly to 6; a normal `award()`-style update that DOES supply `badges`/`badgeCounts` explicitly triggers no extra synthesis (not double-applied); a `digitalBadges` value that doesn't exceed the real array is a no-op; a player with no `badges` array at all still synthesizes cleanly from scratch; an unknown player never throws and returns null; an identical-value no-op update fires no broadcast and mutates nothing — all 15 PASS. A second test against `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim — 8 scenarios: NEUROFLUX's stuck real data (badgeCounts/badges agree at 4, digitalBadges says 6) now renders all 6 with the 2 new ones as generic "Primary Badge #5"/"#6" placeholders; a fully consistent record adds nothing extra; a record with no `digitalBadges` field at all behaves exactly as before (no crash, no bogus top-up); VYBE's v1.76 per-category scenario still works unaffected by the new pass; `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml(null)` never throws — all 8 PASS. 23/23 total. Manually verified the `Math.max` stat-tile formula against NEUROFLUX's (4,6), a normal (4,4), an all-zero (0,0), and an undefined-`digitalBadges` case.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — NEUROFLUX's portfolio will now show all 6 badges (4 real + 2 generic placeholders) immediately on next view. Optional cleanup, same as the v1.76 VYBE note: open Player Management → Edit Player on NEUROFLUX and award the 2 actual specific badges (whatever was awarded from X-Coin) to replace the generic placeholders with real names/artwork/XC — Edit Player's Save already recomputes `badgeCounts`/`digitalBadges` from the real array, so doing this will also correct the underlying numbers, not just the display.
- BACKLOG / OPEN QUESTION: Ennis said he gave 2 badges but `digitalBadges` only moved by 1 (5→6) — this Console-side fix makes the portfolio display correct regardless of the exact number X-Coin sends, but doesn't explain why X-Coin's own count came up short. That logic lives in the `pflx-xcoin-app` repo's badge-award code, not `preview.html` — worth a follow-up look there if it recurs after this patch.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.78 (+ X-Coin) — CROSS-APP BADGE GRANTS NOW CARRY THE REAL BADGE, NOT A GENERIC PLACEHOLDER (Aug 17, Ennis-corrected)
- SYMPTOM: after v1.77 shipped (generic "Primary Badge #N" / "Official Certification Badge #N" placeholders for badges that drifted before the fix), Ennis compared the placeholders against X-Coin's actual badge catalog and called it out directly: *"This seems to be showing dummy badges. Vybe received the AI App Developer badge. Neuroflux and C1RC3 should have received the Global Digital Intern and Beta Tester badges. You seem to not be receiving all of the right information."* v1.77's synthesis was a display-side safety net for records that had ALREADY drifted — it was never meant to be the permanent answer, and Ennis was right that it wasn't showing what was actually granted.
- ROOT CAUSE: traced into the `pflx-xcoin-app` repo itself (previous sessions' analysis had only gone as far as "X-Coin sends a bare `digitalBadges` count"). The Grant button's handler, `handleGrantCoin` in `app/admin/coins/page.tsx`, bumps `targetPlayer.digitalBadges += amount`, credits XC via `earnXCWithTax`, and calls `updatePlayerStats()` — a bridge that only ever carries the `PlayerStats` shape (`xcoin`/`totalXcoin`/`digitalBadges`/`level`/`rank`). X-Coin's own data model has no concept of "badge identity" at all — its own catalog (`coinCategories`) is keyed by `name` with no stable id — so there was never a payload for `handleGrantCoin` to send that COULD carry which specific badge was granted. `notifyBadgeAwarded()` (Discord/Slack) runs in the same handler and does receive the real badge name, which is why Discord posts were fine while the Console's own portfolio wasn't — confirming this was a Console-ingestion gap, not a Discord one.
- FIX (two repos, three parts):
  1. **`pflx-xcoin-app` — `handleGrantCoin`**: added a second, distinct `postMessage` alongside the existing stats bridge — `pflx_player_award`, carrying `{playerId, badge:{name, image, category, xcValue:0}, source:'xcoin', reason}`. `xcValue` is deliberately `0`: the XC for this grant is already credited via `earnXCWithTax`/`updatePlayerStats` in the same handler, so carrying it again here would double-credit it once the Console applies the badge's own `xcValue` on top (see `award()` below).
  2. **`preview.html` — new postMessage handler**: added `pflx_player_award` to the Console's cross-app message listener (next to the pre-existing `pflx_player_update` handler, ~line 61497). It resolves the incoming badge via a new helper, `_pflxResolveAwardBadge(badgeRef)` (~line 23619) — checks the live `mcBadges` catalog first via `mcFindBadge`, and falls back to the badge's own carried `name`/`category`/`image`/`xcValue` (deriving a stable id from the name via `mcBadgeIdFromName`) when there's no catalog entry — then routes the resolved badge through `PflxDataBus.award()` (~line 65448), the SAME canonical award funnel task/checkpoint/project completions already use. `award()` pushes the badge's real id into `badges[]` (deduped), bumps the correct `badgeCounts` bucket from the badge's own category, and fires the usual broadcast/activity-log/XC-popup side effects — so a badge granted this way is now indistinguishable from one awarded any other way in the Console, real artwork included.
  3. **Data repair — the 3 specific records Ennis named**: with the exact badges confirmed (unlike v1.76's VYBE case, where no specific badge could be known), directly repaired via Supabase: VYBE (`player-1786104211856-6ryhl`) gained "AI App Developer"; NEUROFLUX (`player-import-1774891628716-25`) and C1RC3 (`player-1784385012246-jylqd`) each gained "Global Digital Intern (Level 1)" and "Beta Tester", replacing their v1.77 generic placeholders. While repairing C1RC3, also found and removed one unrelated pre-existing junk entry — the literal string `"[object Object]"` sitting in its `badges[]` array (a leftover of the older "badge merge corruption" bug referenced in the v1.59 deploy history) — unambiguous cleanup, not a guess. Deliberately left C1RC3's separate, larger, pre-existing `badgeCounts.primary` mismatch (7 claimed vs. 4 real primary-tier badges) untouched — it predates this incident and isn't part of what Ennis flagged; flagging it below instead.
  4. **Follow-up catch, found during post-repair verification**: neither "AI App Developer" nor "Beta Tester" exist in the Console's synced `mcBadges` catalog (only "Global Digital Intern (Level 1)" does) — confirmed by reading `mcFindBadge` verbatim: it always requires a catalog match by `id`/`name` and returns `null` otherwise, with NO special-casing for a full badge object passed as `player.badges[]` entry. That meant the just-repaired VYBE/NEUROFLUX/C1RC3 records — and any future `award()` grant of these same two badges — would have silently rendered NOTHING in `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` (`.map(mcFindBadge).filter(Boolean)` drops unmatched entries with no error), reproducing the exact "not showing" complaint a second time. Fixed at the source instead of patching the renderer: synced both badges into the `pflx_mc_badges` Supabase catalog (44 → 46 items), pulling their real `name`/`xc`/`image`/`description` straight from X-Coin's own `coinCategories` catalog (same source of truth `_pflxResolveAwardBadge` already trusts) so both now resolve normally, for these 3 records and for any player awarded either badge from now on.
- DATA: Supabase `app_data`, project `hyxiagexyptzvetqjmnj`. Backed up `pflx_mc_badges` to `backup_badge_catalog_sync_20260817_pflx_mc_badges` before writing (verification SELECT confirmed 44 items backed up). Appended `badge-ai-app-developer` (xc 10000) and `badge-beta-tester` (xc 1000), both tier `signature` / category `Signature Badges (Skill Mastery)`, sourced from `coinCategories` — verification SELECT confirmed 46 items post-write, both new ids resolvable with real image data (>100 chars, not truncated). Player repair (`pflx_mc_players`, per-player `badges[]`/`badgeCounts`/`digitalBadges`, `awardedBy: 'xcoin-grant-repair-v1.78'` tagged on each new entry): VYBE `badges` 0→1 (`badge-ai-app-developer`), `badgeCounts.signature` 0→1, `digitalBadges` unchanged at 1 (already correct); NEUROFLUX `badges` 5→6 (added `badge-global-digital-intern-level-1`, `badge-beta-tester`), `badgeCounts.signature` 2→4; C1RC3 `badges` 7→8 (added the same two badges, minus the removed `"[object Object]"` junk entry), `badgeCounts.signature` 2→4. `digitalBadges`/`badgeCounts` sums verified against final `badges[].length` for all three after the write.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` (bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 77 → 78, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged `2026.08`) and `pflx-xcoin-app/app/admin/coins/page.tsx`.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). `tsc --noEmit` clean on the touched X-Coin file (one pre-existing, unrelated `task-management/page.tsx` error confirmed present via `git stash` even without this change). Live-code behavioral test extracting `mcBadgeIdFromName`/`mcFindBadge`/`_pflxBadgeCategoryKey`/`_pflxResolveAwardBadge`/`award` verbatim, run against a harness replicating the exact Console message-handler logic — 15 scenarios covering NEUROFLUX's real Beta Tester grant (real name lands in `badges[]`, correct id derived, correct category bucket bumped, XC untouched since `xcValue:0`, idempotent on a repeat grant, broadcast fires, postMessage ack reflects the new badge), VYBE's real AI App Developer grant from a player with no prior `badges` array, a catalog-matched grant (Global Digital Intern) resolving to its canonical id, and malformed/unknown-player messages never throwing — all 15 PASS. A second live-code test extracting `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim and running it against VYBE/NEUROFLUX/C1RC3's exact real (post-repair, post-catalog-sync) data — 8 scenarios: all 3 real badge names ("AI App Developer", "Global Digital Intern", "Beta Tester") appear in the rendered HTML for the right players, and no generic placeholder text appears for any of them — all 8 PASS. 23/23 total.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. VYBE, NEUROFLUX, and C1RC3 will show their real granted badges (name + artwork) immediately on next portfolio view — no re-save or Edit Player action needed, since the fix was applied directly to their cloud records. Going forward, every Grant-button badge award from X-Coin will carry its real identity into the Console automatically.
- BACKLOG: C1RC3's pre-existing `badgeCounts.primary` mismatch (7 claimed vs. 4 real primary-tier badges in `badges[]`) is still unresolved — deliberately out of scope for this patch since Ennis didn't flag it and there's no way to know which specific primary badges are missing without asking. Worth a follow-up if it surfaces as its own complaint. Also still open from v1.77: why X-Coin's `digitalBadges` counter moved by fewer than the number of badges actually granted in that earlier incident — not re-investigated this session.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.79 — CLICK-THROUGH BADGE DETAIL POPUP + VISIBLE BADGE TYPE (Aug 17, Ennis-requested)
- REQUEST: right after v1.78 shipped (VYBE/NEUROFLUX/C1RC3 now showing real badge artwork), Ennis asked for two small follow-on features on the same Badge Portfolio grid: *"Now I want to be able to click on the badges and a popup comes up with the image and description of the badge"*, then *"Also show badge type: Primary, Exclusive, etc."*
- IMPLEMENTATION: both earned-badge grids in the app share the same tile HTML shape, so both got the change identically:
  1. `portfolioRenderBadges()` (~line 56587, the owner's own "MY PORTFOLIO" page) and `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml()` (~line 56996, the read-only viewer for any other player) — each earned-badge tile now carries its own identity on `data-*` attributes (`data-badge-name`, `data-badge-desc`, `data-badge-xc`, `data-badge-type`, `data-badge-category`) and an `onclick="pflxShowBadgeDetail(this)"`, plus a small uppercase tier tag (Primary/Premium/Executive/Signature) under the badge name on the tile itself. Deliberately did NOT introduce a separate JS registry keyed by index/id to hold this data — a tile's own attributes can never go stale if the grid re-renders, unlike a shared array a click handler might read after the underlying data moved on.
  2. New shared helper `pflxBadgeTierLabel(key)` (~line 23614, next to the existing `_pflxBadgeCategoryKey`) — maps the canonical tier key (`primary`/`premium`/`executive`/`signature`) to its short display label (`Primary`/`Premium`/`Executive`/`Signature`), exposed on `window` so both renderers and the new popup share one source of truth for the label text.
  3. New shared modal, `window.pflxShowBadgeDetail(el)` + `pflxCloseBadgeDetailModal()` (~line 56957, right before `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml`) — follows the same dynamically-built-overlay pattern already used by `pflxOpenPlayerPortfolio`/`pflxClosePortfolioModal` (a module-level element reference so calling it twice in a row swaps the popup instead of stacking two). Reads the name/description/XC/type/category straight off the clicked tile's `data-*` attributes, and — this is the part worth flagging — does NOT duplicate the badge's image into a data attribute (would double the DOM's payload for every base64 image already rendered on the tile); instead it reads the image back off that same tile's own `<img>` (or falls back to its icon `<div>`'s emoji) at click time and re-renders it larger (140px vs. the tile's 60px) in the popup. A badge with no description (synthesized placeholders, or a catalog entry that's missing one) shows "No description available." rather than an empty gap; a badge with `xc:0` shows no XC chip at all rather than "+0 XC".
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 78 → 79 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `mcFindBadge`/`_pflxBadgeCategoryKey`/`pflxBadgeTierLabel`/`escapeHtml`/`pflxCloseBadgeDetailModal`/`pflxShowBadgeDetail`/`pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim, run against a real jsdom document (not a mocked DOM) so the actual click → attribute-read → DOM-append flow executes exactly as it will in the browser — 17 scenarios: a real catalogued badge (AI App Developer) renders its tile with the correct `Signature` type tag, clicking it opens a popup with the correct name/description/the FULL-SIZE 140px image (not the 60px tile thumbnail)/type+category chip/XC chip, and closing it removes the popup from the DOM; a badge with no description falls back to the placeholder text; a `primary`-tier badge is tagged `Primary`; a legacy synthesized placeholder badge (no catalog entry, no image, no description, no XC) never throws on click and shows the graceful empty states; clicking a second tile while a popup is already open swaps to the new badge instead of stacking two popups; calling the handler with `null`/`undefined` never throws — all 17 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Every badge tile across both the owner's own portfolio and the read-only viewer for any other player is now clickable.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.80 — BADGE DETAIL POPUP: FIX REAL DESCRIPTIONS SHOWING AS MISSING, DEDUPE REDUNDANT TYPE TAG (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: right after v1.79 shipped, Ennis reported the new popup had two problems: *"It is redundant showing badge type twice"* (e.g. "SIGNATURE · SIGNATURE BADGES (SKILL MASTERY)") and *"its saying no description when there are descriptions"* — with a screenshot of X-Coin's own badge catalog admin page showing "Personal Branding (Level 1)" has a real description ("Completed Project: Brand Identity...") that the Console's popup showed as "No description available."
- ROOT CAUSE (two separate bugs, one genuinely pre-existing and only now surfaced):
  1. **Missing descriptions — pre-existing bug in `mcGetAllBadges()` (~line 23552), not something v1.79 introduced.** Confirmed via a direct Supabase query against `pflx_mc_badges` that EVERY catalog entry, including "Personal Branding (Level 1)", already has a real, non-empty `description` field — the data was never missing. The bug is in how the Console reads it: `mcGetAllBadges()` rebuilds a brand-new object for every entry in `mcBadges` (to normalize `id`/`tier`/`category`/`image` across old and new shapes) but its field list never included `description` — so `mcFindBadge()`, which is built entirely on top of `mcGetAllBadges()`, always returned an object with the description silently stripped, no matter how complete the underlying Supabase record was. v1.79's popup was the first UI surface in the entire app that ever tried to read `.description` off a resolved badge, which is why this had never been noticed before — every other consumer of `mcFindBadge` (grant flows, portfolio tiles, etc.) only ever reads `name`/`image`/`xc`/`category`.
  2. **Redundant type tag — a v1.79 design gap, not a data bug.** The popup's type chip concatenated the short tier label (`type`, e.g. "Signature") with the badge's raw source category string (`category`, e.g. "Signature Badges (Skill Mastery)") unconditionally. For 3 of the 4 tiers this reads fine (e.g. "Primary · Professional Endorsements" — genuinely different information), but `signature`-tier badges' raw category text happens to already contain the word "Signature" (it's literally how X-Coin names that category), so the two concatenated into an obviously repeated phrase.
- FIX:
  1. `mcGetAllBadges()`'s `dynamic` (and, for consistency, `hardcoded`) object-rebuild now includes `description: b.description || ''` in the returned shape, so it round-trips instead of silently dropping on the floor. This fixes descriptions everywhere `mcFindBadge`/`mcGetAllBadges` are used, not just the new popup.
  2. `pflxShowBadgeDetail` (~line 56973): before building the type chip, checks whether `category`'s lowercase text already contains `type`'s lowercase text; if so, `category` is cleared and only the short type label shows. Non-redundant category text (the common case) still displays exactly as before.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 79 → 80 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test — this time deliberately NOT mocking `mcGetAllBadges`/`mcFindBadge` (the v1.79 test suite had mocked them, which is exactly why it didn't catch this) — extracting the real `mcBadgeIdFromName`/`mcGetAllBadges`/`mcFindBadge`/`_pflxBadgeCategoryKey`/`pflxBadgeTierLabel`/`escapeHtml`/`pflxShowBadgeDetail`/`pflxPlayerBadgesHtml` verbatim and running them together against a catalog shaped exactly like the real Supabase data (including "Personal Branding (Level 1)"'s real description, copied verbatim from the live catalog) — 7 scenarios: the real description reaches the tile's `data-badge-desc` attribute and then the popup (reproducing and then confirming the fix for Ennis's exact report); a signature-tier badge's type chip shows "Signature" exactly once, no redundant category suffix; a primary-tier badge (genuinely different type vs. category text) still shows both, unaffected by the dedup logic; a badge with a genuinely empty description in the catalog still shows the "No description available." fallback correctly (proving the fix doesn't mask real gaps); AI App Developer and Beta Tester (the v1.78 uncatalogued-badge repair) both resolve their real descriptions post-fix — all 7 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none. Every badge popup across the app now shows its real description (where the catalog has one) and a clean, non-repeated type/category line.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.81 (+ X-Coin) — BADGE ENDORSEMENT COUNTS: MULTI-GRANTS NO LONGER CORRUPT THE RECORD (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- REQUEST + SYMPTOM (same message): with two screenshots of NEUROFLUX's Badge Portfolio, Ennis said: *"I also just added Video Editor badge to Neuroflux and changed the grant number to 5. The Video Editor badge should show 5 endorsements. So in other words there should be a number indicator by the badge. When clicked on it should show 5 endorsements."* The screenshots showed the real request (a visible "×N" count on a multi-granted badge, expanded on click) alongside a live data-corruption bug: granting Video Editor with X-Coin's Grant modal "Amount" field set to 5 had NOT produced "Video Editor ×5" — it produced one bare `badge-video-editor` entry plus 5 fake `legacy-primary-N` "Primary Badge #7"–"#11" placeholder tiles, and `badgeCounts.primary` had inflated from 2 to 7.
- ROOT CAUSE: X-Coin's Grant modal has always had an "Amount" field, but neither X-Coin's `handleGrantCoin` nor the Console's `award()` had ever had a concept of "grant this ONE badge N times" — X-Coin's only use of `amount` for badges was `targetPlayer.digitalBadges += amount`, a bare inflated count sent to the Console via `updatePlayerStats()` with no badge identity attached. This raced against the same handler's identity-aware `pflx_player_award` message (the v1.78 fix). Whichever the Console's `PflxDataBus.applyUpdate` processed second saw a `digitalBadges` claiming more badges than `badges[]` actually held, and its v1.77 placeholder-synthesis safety net (which exists specifically to guard against exactly this kind of drift) topped up the "shortfall" with generic placeholders bucketed to `primary` — the same mechanism that made v1.77's own display-time top-up necessary is what fabricated these 5 fakes.
- FIX (three repos' worth of surface, one concept threaded through all of them — a badge ref can now carry `endorsements: N`, an integer count of how many times that specific badge id has been granted, distinct from `badgeCounts` which still tracks distinct TYPES):
  1. **`PflxDataBus.award()`'s badge branch** (~line 65594): reads a new optional `awardObj.badge.count` (defaults to 1). Granting a NEW badge id pushes a bare string (unchanged, `count:1` — every existing single-grant badge's storage shape is untouched) or `{id, endorsements: count}` when `count > 1`, and bumps `badgeCounts[category]` by 1 (one new distinct type) exactly once. Re-granting an ALREADY-EARNED badge id now adds to its running `endorsements` total instead of the old silent no-op dedupe — and deliberately does NOT bump `badgeCounts` again, since it's not a new distinct type. Critically, `changes.badges` is always set alongside `changes.digitalBadges` in this branch, so `applyUpdate`'s v1.77 placeholder-synthesis guard (which only fires when `badges` is `undefined`) never activates — the exact mechanism that fabricated NEUROFLUX's 5 fakes structurally cannot fire from this path anymore.
  2. **`_pflxResolveAwardBadge(badgeRef)`** (~line 23638) — the resolver every incoming `pflx_player_award` message funnels through before `award()` ever sees it. Found and fixed a second, silent bug while wiring this up: this resolver rebuilds a fresh badge object and, like `mcGetAllBadges` before its v1.80 fix, wasn't carrying an incoming `count` field through at all — so even after fixing X-Coin to send `count: amount`, the field would have been dropped right here, before `award()`'s new logic ever ran. Added `count: (typeof raw.count === 'number' && raw.count > 0) ? raw.count : 1` to its returned shape.
  3. **`portfolioRenderBadges()` and `pflxPlayerBadgesHtml()`** (~line 56606 and ~56606+458, visual twins): both `earned = earnedRefs.map(...)` resolution steps now carry a ref's own `endorsements` onto the `mcFindBadge()`-resolved catalog object. Both tile-rendering loops add a small "×N" pill (top-right corner of the artwork, only rendered when `endorsements > 1` — a normal single-grant badge shows nothing extra) and a new `data-badge-endorsements` attribute alongside the existing v1.79 data-* set.
  4. **`pflxShowBadgeDetail`** (~line 56994): reads `data-badge-endorsements` off the clicked tile and, when `> 1`, shows a distinct "N Endorsements" chip in the popup (Ennis: "when clicked on it should show 5 endorsements") — separate from the XC chip, shown only for multi-grant badges.
  5. **`pflx-xcoin-app` — `handleGrantCoin`** (`app/admin/coins/page.tsx`): added `count: amount` to the existing `pflx_player_award` postMessage's `badge` object, so the Grant modal's "Amount" field now carries its real intent end-to-end instead of only ever driving the old bare `digitalBadges` bump. Removed `digitalBadges: targetPlayer.digitalBadges` from the same handler's `updatePlayerStats()` call — the field that raced against `pflx_player_award` and triggered the placeholder synthesis; the Console now derives `digitalBadges` itself from the real `badges[]` array once the identity-aware award lands, so there's nothing left to race. Deliberately left `targetPlayer.digitalBadges += amount` itself untouched — confirmed via `grep` across the X-Coin app that `digitalBadges` is X-Coin's own widely-used lifetime-badges-granted counter (dashboard, ticker, leaderboard, assistant), a legitimate "schema split" per the Handoff's own gotcha list, not something this fix should change.
- DATA REPAIR: NEUROFLUX's corrupted state, in both Supabase representations (`pflx_mc_players` bulk roster item and the mirrored `pflx_player_player-import-1774891628716-25` per-id row), was identical pre-repair: `digitalBadges: 12`, `badgeCounts: {primary:7, premium:0, executive:1, signature:4}`, `badges[]` holding 5 real catalog ids (`badge-self-directed-player`, `badge-positive-participant`, `badge-pflx-user-certification`, `badge-personal-branding-level-1`, `badge-global-digital-intern-level-1`), 1 full-object real badge (`badge-beta-tester`), 5 fake `legacy-primary-N-1786947743537` placeholders, and a bare `badge-video-editor` string with no endorsement tag. Queried the live `pflx_mc_badges` catalog to confirm each real badge's actual tier before touching anything — notably `badge-video-editor` is catalog tier `executive` ("Executive Badges (Jobs)"), not `primary` as the corruption's placeholder-bucketing had implied. Repair (identical SQL applied to both representations, verified with a post-write SELECT): removed all 5 `legacy-primary-*` entries; converted the bare `badge-video-editor` string to `{id:'badge-video-editor', endorsements:5}`; set `badgeCounts` to `{primary:2, premium:0, executive:1, signature:4}` (2 real primary badges — Self Directed Player, Positive Participant — plus the correctly-classified 1 executive and 4 signature, summing to the 7 real distinct types); set `digitalBadges` to `7`. Post-repair verification SELECT against both keys confirms identical, correct final state.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` (bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 80 → 81, `PFLX_BUILD` unchanged `2026.08`; this patch also carries v1.80's description/redundant-type-tag fix, which was coded and Handoff-documented in the prior session but never shipped — see the v1.80 entry above) and `pflx-xcoin-app/app/admin/coins/page.tsx`.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks) after both the v1.80 carry-forward and all v1.81 edits. Live-code behavioral test extracting `mcBadgeIdFromName`/`mcGetAllBadges`/`mcFindBadge`/`_pflxBadgeCategoryKey`/`pflxBadgeTierLabel`/`escapeHtml`/`pflxPlayerBadgesHtml`/`pflxShowBadgeDetail`/`pflxCloseBadgeDetailModal`/`WRITABLE_FIELDS`/`getPlayer`/`_pflxResolvePlayerForAward`/`applyUpdate`/`broadcastTo`/`broadcastAll`/`award` verbatim (mocking only the true external boundary — `logActivity`, `broadcastPlayerChange`, `pflxToast`, `pflxEmitXcoinEvent`, the badge catalog — never the functions under test or their real dependencies), run against a real jsdom document with a NEUROFLUX-shaped fixture — 17 scenarios: granting a brand-new badge with `count:5` adds exactly ONE `badges[]` entry (not 5 fakes) tagged `endorsements:5`, bumps `badgeCounts.primary` by exactly 1, and sets `digitalBadges` to the correct distinct-type count (not the endorsement-inflated one); re-granting the same badge with `count:2` accumulates to `endorsements:7` without a duplicate entry or a second `badgeCounts` bump; a normal single-grant badge (no `count` field, the overwhelming common case) still stores as a bare string exactly as before; the full render→click pipeline against a `{endorsements:5}` fixture shows the "×5" tile pill, the `data-badge-endorsements="5"` attribute, and a "5 Endorsements" popup chip, while a single-endorsement badge in the same render shows none of those — all 17 PASS. Brace/paren balance check on the edited X-Coin file (no local TypeScript toolchain available in this session to run `tsc --noEmit`; the edit is small, additive, and was checked by hand against `updatePlayerStats`'s existing `Partial<PlayerStats>` signature). Live Supabase repair verified via post-write SELECT on both `pflx_mc_players` and `pflx_player_player-import-1774891628716-25` showing identical, correct final state.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — NEUROFLUX's portfolio will show "Video Editor ×5" immediately, clickable to a popup confirming "5 Endorsements". Going forward, any Grant with an Amount > 1 (new or repeat) will produce a correct endorsement count instead of placeholder corruption. Worth spot-checking other players who may have received multi-amount grants before this patch (the corruption mechanism wasn't unique to NEUROFLUX/Video Editor) — none were reported, so none beyond NEUROFLUX were repaired this session.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.82 — persistPlayers() WAS RE-UPLOADING THE ENTIRE ROSTER ON EVERY SINGLE EDIT, STOMPING OTHER PLAYERS' REAL DATA (Aug 17, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis, with two screenshots of Trinity's portfolio card (all five stat tiles at zero, "No projects/tasks/badges"): *"Trinity should have digital coins and a more updated profile."* Direct Supabase query showed Trinity's per-id row (`pflx_player_player-import-1774891628716-55`) correctly held `xc:3900, digitalBadges:12` (with a real `data_bus_update` activity trail from X-Coin proving it), but the `pflx_mc_players` bulk-roster mirror — which the portfolio card renders from — showed all zeros. A systemic query joining every per-id row against its bulk-roster mirror surfaced the same divergence for 18 players total, in BOTH directions (some players' bulk entry under-reports XC/badges vs. their real per-id row, some over-reports) — including NEUROFLUX, whose bulk `digitalBadges` had reverted to the pre-repair value of 12, even though this exact session had already fixed it to 7 in v1.81.
- ROOT CAUSE: found by tracing every write path that touches `pflx_player_<id>` rows. `persistPlayers()` (~line 65025) is called from roughly a dozen sites across the app — critically including `logActivity()` (fires on nearly every action: awards, task approvals, XC grants, badge grants — anything that logs to a player's activity trail) and `broadcastPlayerChange()` (the single-player-edit path used by Player Management's Save, avatar upload, XC-event delivery). Every one of those calls only ever *changes one player*, but `persistPlayers()` had no concept of "just this player" — it re-filtered the ENTIRE in-memory `PLAYERS` array and enqueued *every* player in it for cloud persist, every single time. A direct Supabase timestamp query confirmed this in the act: 135 of 156 `pflx_player_<id>` rows carried the identical millisecond timestamp `2026-08-17 06:22:24.847`, i.e. one host's single edit cascaded into a mass rewrite of the entire roster from whatever was sitting in that host's in-memory `PLAYERS` array at the time. Any host/tab whose in-memory snapshot was even slightly stale — hadn't refetched since a *different* tab, sub-app, or X-Coin grant updated some *other* player — would silently overwrite that other player's real, current cloud data the next time literally anything happened in its own tab. This is the same "wholesale-array sync, last-write-wins" gotcha already on record for the bulk `pflx_mc_players`/`mcSaveData` path, just discovered independently on the per-id-row path, and firing far more often (on every activity-log entry, not just explicit roster saves).
- FIX: `persistPlayers()` now takes an optional `onlyIds` array. When provided, only those player(s) get enqueued into `_pflxCloudPersistQueue` for the cloud upsert — everyone else's untouched cloud row is left alone. The full in-memory roster is still always written to `localStorage` (that part was never the problem; it's local-only and cheap). Updated every single-player call site to pass its own id: `broadcastPlayerChange(player)` → `persistPlayers([player.id])`; `logActivity(playerId, ...)` → `persistPlayers([playerId])`; the XC-event queue's `enqueueToRecord`/`clearRecord` → `persistPlayers([p.id])`; avatar upload → `persistPlayers([p.id])`; both delete paths (`hmcEditPlayer`'s Delete button and `pflxDeletePlayerFully`) → `persistPlayers([])` (the deleted player is already gone from `PLAYERS`, and a separate step deletes their per-id row directly — there's no "changed" player left to enqueue, and definitely no reason to re-touch everyone else's); bulk CSV import → `persistPlayers([])` (each new player is already individually cloud-persisted via the existing `pflxIdentityPersistNewPlayer()` call in the same loop, so the roster-wide call only needs to refresh `localStorage`). Any future caller that doesn't pass `onlyIds` still gets the old whole-roster behavior (no silent behavior change for code not yet touched), but every real call site in the app as of this patch is now scoped.
- DATA REPAIR: Trinity's `pflx_mc_players` bulk item repaired to match her real, activity-log-verified per-id row: `xc:3900, xcoin:3900, totalXcoin:3900, digitalBadges:12` (specific badge identities unknown — left `badges:[]`/`badgeCounts` zeroed, matching the established no-guessing repair pattern; the render-time placeholder-safety-net handles display gracefully). Verified via post-write SELECT; bulk-roster array length unchanged (140 items) confirming no entries were dropped or duplicated. The other 17 mismatched players found by the systemic query were NOT repaired this session — the mismatches run in both directions and, unlike Trinity/NEUROFLUX, most don't yet have an activity-log-verified "true" value on hand; batch-guessing which side (bulk vs. per-id) is correct for each risks making things worse. Flagged to Ennis for a scoping decision before any further data surgery. A duplicate, fully-empty all-caps "TRINITY" player record (`player-1782293539007-n3j3g`, cohort "Core 3") was also noticed during this investigation and left untouched — looks like a stale leftover, not confirmed safe to delete, no deletion requested.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 81 → 82 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting the real `persistPlayers()` verbatim, run against a 3-player fixture: a scoped call with `onlyIds:['A']` enqueues only A for cloud persist and leaves B/C untouched (the exact bug, reproduced and confirmed fixed); an empty `onlyIds:[]` (the delete/bulk-import case) enqueues nobody; a legacy call with no argument still enqueues everyone (back-compat for any caller not yet updated); the full in-memory roster is still always written to `localStorage` regardless of scoping — all 6 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required for the code fix — it's live immediately. Awaiting Ennis's direction on the other 17 flagged players (list captured in this session, available on request) before doing any further Supabase data surgery on them; recommend spot-checking a few of the highest-value ones (players with real XC swings, not just badge-count drift) against their own activity logs the same way Trinity's was confirmed.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.83 — AI WRITING ASSIST + AUTOCORRECT ACROSS MISSION CONTROL (Aug 18, Ennis)
- REQUEST: Ennis, with a screenshot of the Task Form's Description field (his own Grammarly extension was underlining a grammar slip — "is" where it should read "are" — and the Firefox/Chrome icon in the corner is that extension, not anything built into the app): "Add AI and autocorrect to help with descriptions and input in Mission Control." Clarified scope: AI should offer an Improve/Expand button, a conservative Fix Grammar option, and a Generate-from-Title option, plus native spellcheck — rolled out across every description field in Mission Control (Tasks, Projects, Checkpoints, Programs, Proposals), not just the one field in the screenshot.
- IMPLEMENTATION: found that the platform already has a full AI backend — `XBOT_AI` (~line 53619), the engine behind the X-Bot chat assistant, with a server-side proxy (`pflx-pathway-portal.vercel.app/api/pflx-ai`, keys live in Vercel env — works for every host on every device, nothing to configure) and a Claude/Gemini/OpenAI/local fallback chain. Built a new, small, reusable module — `PFLX_AI_ASSIST` (~line 54279) — that rides this exact same engine for one-off text completions instead of routing through `XBOT_AI.respond()` (which is chat-oriented: it mutates conversation history and parses `[NAV:]` navigation commands, neither of which belongs in a one-shot "improve this description" call). Three modes, each with its own system prompt: `improve` (expand a short draft into a fuller 2-4 sentence description, matching tone, no invented facts), `fix` (grammar/spelling only, meaning and length unchanged), `generate` (draft a description from just the Title field, for when a host doesn't want to type one at all). `PFLX_AI_ASSIST.toolbarHtml(titleId, descId)` renders the three-button row (Generate button auto-hidden when no title field is wired); `PFLX_AI_ASSIST.run(mode, field, btn)` handles validation (refuses `improve`/`fix` on an empty draft, refuses `generate` on an empty title — no AI call, no data touched), the button's loading/disabled state, writing the result back into the field, and a toast on success or failure (falls back to `console.log` if neither `pflxShowSaveToast` nor `pflxToast` exists, so this can never throw).
- WIRED INTO 8 FIELDS: Task Form (Advanced: `mc-task-title`/`mc-task-desc`; Quick: `mc-qtask-title`/`mc-qtask-desc`), Project Form (Advanced: `mc-project-title`/`mc-project-desc`; Quick: `mc-qproject-title`/`mc-qproject-desc`), Checkpoint Form (Advanced: `mc-cp-name`/`mc-cp-desc`; Quick: `mc-qcp-name`/`mc-qcp-desc`), Program tab (`mc-program-tab-name`/`mc-program-tab-desc` — a single-line input, same toolbar works identically against `.value`), and the player-facing Propose modal (`pp-title`/`pp-desc`). The 7 static forms use a `<div data-ai-toolbar="titleId|descId">` marker filled by a one-time `pflxAIAssistInitToolbars()` sweep on `DOMContentLoaded` (idempotent — checks a `data-ai-toolbar-filled` flag so it's safe to call again); the Propose modal's toolbar is injected directly into its template string instead, since that markup doesn't exist in the DOM until a player opens it. All 8 Description fields also got an explicit `spellcheck="true"` attribute for native browser autocorrect/spell-squiggles — the free, zero-latency layer underneath the AI buttons.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 82 → 83 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `PFLX_AI_ASSIST` and `pflxAIAssistInitToolbars` verbatim (mocking only `XBOT_AI` itself — the true external/network boundary — never the functions under test) — 20 scenarios, all PASS: the toolbar sweep fills every `[data-ai-toolbar]` marker with the right button count and correct wired ids, is idempotent on a second call, and correctly omits the Generate button when no title field is given; `improve` sends both title and draft to the AI and writes the (trimmed) result back into the field; `generate` correctly works from an empty description using only the title, and is correctly BLOCKED (no AI call, no data touched) when the title itself is empty; `fix` is correctly blocked on an empty draft; a real AI failure leaves the field's existing text completely untouched and surfaces an error toast rather than corrupting anything; a "no AI engine configured" state surfaces a clear message without crashing.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately, and there's nothing to configure since it reuses the same server-side AI proxy that already powers X-Bot chat today. Note for Ennis: the AI buttons call the same shared AI backend as X-Bot chat, so if a cohort's X-Bot is ever disabled or rate-limited, these buttons will surface that as a toast rather than silently failing.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.84 — CANVA EMBEDS IN MISSION CONTROL RESOURCES (Aug 18, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "All of the Google Drive Resources attachments should also allow a canva embed." — the 📎 Resources section on Tasks/Projects/Checkpoints (paste-a-link attach flow, `pflxGoogle` module ~line 31244) only recognized Google Docs/Sheets/Slides/Forms/Drive links; Ennis wanted Canva designs attachable the same way.
- IMPLEMENTATION: extended the existing `pflxGoogle` link-parser/attachment system rather than building a parallel one, since its card/Preview/Open/Remove UI and `rec.attachments[]` storage shape were already fully generic over `att.kind`. Added a `canva` entry to `TYPES` (icon 🎨, label "Canva Design") and a new branch in `parseLink()` matching Canva share links — `canva.com/design/<DESIGN_ID>/<SHARE_ID>/(view|edit|watch)` — covering all three link shapes a host might paste (their own edit link, a view-only share link, or a watch link for video/presentation designs). `build()` rebuilds the embed URL as the canonical `.../view?embed` form regardless of which of the three the host pasted, matching Canva's own zero-API-key embed convention. Updated the attach modal's copy, placeholder, and error toast to mention both Google and Canva; updated the Resources button label to "📎 Attach Google Doc / Canva"; added `allowfullscreen`/`allow="fullscreen"` to the shared preview iframe so Canva's native fullscreen control works (harmless no-op for existing Google embeds). `isGoogle()`/`linkCardIfGoogle()` (used to render a rich preview card for player-submitted links) now also recognize Canva links as a side effect of sharing the same parser — a bonus: a student who submits a Canva link now gets the same rich Open/Preview card treatment as a Google Doc submission.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 83 → 84 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxGoogle` verbatim — 16 scenarios, all PASS: Canva `/view`, `/edit`, and `/watch` share links all resolve to `kind:'canva'` with the correct rebuilt `.../view?embed` URL and the original share link preserved for the Open button; existing Google Doc and Drive file parsing is unchanged (regression check); an unrelated URL is correctly not misidentified as either; the rendered card shows the Canva icon and a working Preview button; a Canva submission link now renders through the rich card path via `isGoogle()`/`linkCardIfGoogle()`.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. To attach a Canva design, click "📎 Attach Google Doc / Canva" on any Task/Project/Checkpoint and paste the design's share link (Share → Copy link in Canva); make sure Canva's own sharing/visibility is set so students can open it, same caveat as Google links.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.85 — CANVA TEMPLATE/SHORT LINKS + ANY EMBED CODE IN RESOURCES (Aug 18, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: right after v1.84 shipped Canva support, Ennis reported it didn't actually work for his link: "I am trying to post a canva template link." Rather than guess at the URL shape, asked for the exact failing link before touching code; Ennis then broadened the ask — "And it should allow Attach Google Drive/Canva link. Or any embed code" — and supplied the real link: `https://canva.link/v80x54ovfzbloj5`.
- ROOT CAUSE: v1.84's Canva branch in `parseLink()` (~line 31298) matched ONLY the `canva.com/design/<id>/<id>/(view|edit|watch)` share-link shape. Ennis's link was a `canva.link/xxxx` short link — a different domain Canva's own "Copy link" button sometimes hands out — which the regex never matched, so the attach modal rejected it outright. Canva's public Template Marketplace pages (`canva.com/templates/...`) were also unrecognized. More broadly, the attach flow only ever accepted Google/Canva link patterns — a raw embed-code snippet (e.g. YouTube/Figma/Loom's own "Share → Embed" `<iframe>` HTML) or any other platform's plain share link had no path in at all.
- FIX: `pflxGoogle` (~line 31244). Added two new `parseLink()` branches for `canva.com/templates/<id>` and `canva.link/<id>` — both return `kind:'canva'` with `embedUrl:null` (Open-only; neither format supports Canva's `?embed` convention reliably, and a `canva.link` redirect can't be resolved client-side due to CORS, so no Preview is attempted rather than risk a broken iframe). Added a new function `parseLinkOrEmbed(input)`, layered on top of (not replacing) `parseLink()`: tries the known Google/Canva patterns first, then detects a raw `<iframe src="...">` snippet and extracts the src as `kind:'embed'` (rejects rather than guesses if no readable src is found), then falls back to accepting any bare `http(s)://` URL as a generic `kind:'link'` (Open-only). Deliberately kept `parseLinkOrEmbed()` separate from `parseLink()`/`isGoogle()` — the narrower functions still gate submission-link rich-card rendering elsewhere in the app, so this change doesn't loosen what counts as a "Google/Canva" link there. `attachModal()` now calls `parseLinkOrEmbed()` instead of `parseLink()`, its `<input>` became a `<textarea>` (embed code can be a multi-line snippet), and copy/placeholder/error text updated to mention embed codes explicitly. Also exposed `parseLinkOrEmbed` on `pflxGoogle`'s returned object (was previously closure-only) for consistency with the rest of the module's public surface.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 84 → 85 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxGoogle` verbatim — 29 scenarios, all PASS: Ennis's actual `canva.link` short link and a `canva.com/templates/...` link both resolve to `kind:'canva'` with `embedUrl:null`; the v1.84 design-share-link path is unaffected (still gets a real rebuilt embed URL) — regression check; Google Doc parsing unaffected — regression check; `parseLinkOrEmbed()` resolves known links identically to `parseLink()`, extracts the src from a real `<iframe>` embed snippet, correctly rejects an iframe-looking string with no readable src, accepts a generic valid URL (e.g. a Figma link) as a plain Resource Link, and rejects empty/whitespace/non-URL garbage; `parseLink()`/`isGoogle()`/`linkCardIfGoogle()` themselves still reject the generic URL and iframe code — confirms submission-link rendering elsewhere is unaffected; card rendering shows a Preview button only when an `embedUrl` exists (embed-code cards do, plain-link cards don't) and always shows Open.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. The Attach Resource modal now accepts: Google Docs/Sheets/Slides/Forms/Drive links, any Canva link (design share link, template page, or `canva.link` short link), a pasted `<iframe>` embed snippet from any platform's own "Share → Embed" option, or as a last resort any plain https:// link (Open-only, no live preview, so it's never a dead end).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.86 — VISION STATEMENT NOW SHOWS ON THE PORTFOLIO (Aug 18, Ennis-requested)
- REQUEST: "Also make sure that each Vision Statement generated from the diagnostic, appears on each player's Portfolio."
- ROOT CAUSE / FINDING: the Checkpoint Alpha Diagnostic (CAD) already builds a full 4-part vision statement — create/impact/perspective/future — during onboarding (`cadState.results.visionStatement`, ~line 20218) and persists it onto the player record at signup (`player.visionStatement`, ~line 20561). But that data was write-only: it appeared once, on the one-time "Assessment Complete" onboarding screen (and the downloadable results PNG), then was never read again anywhere in the app — not on the player's own Portfolio, not on the read-only viewer a host or another player sees. The player's own creative-identity statement, which they wrote themselves during signup, was effectively invisible after the day they joined.
- FIX: added a new "🔮 VISION STATEMENT" section to both places the Portfolio renders. (1) The owner's own "MY PORTFOLIO" page (`portfolioRender()`, ~line 56174): new function `portfolioRenderVision(user)` (~line 56544), new container `<div id="portfolio-vision-section">` in the static markup (~line 11534, placed right after Brand Bio, before the stat tiles), and `visionStatement` added to `portfolioGetUserData()`'s returned object (was previously never pulled off the player record at all). (2) The read-only viewer used when a host or another player opens someone else's portfolio (`pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml()`, ~line 57064) — same visual block, sourced directly from `player.visionStatement` since the read-only path already reads other identity fields (pathway, studioId) straight off the target player rather than `activeSession`. Both render the same connective-sentence format already used on the onboarding "Assessment Complete" screen: "I want to create X that will Y. My unique perspective is Z. In two years, I'll be known for W." Both are fully hidden (not an empty card) for any player with no vision statement at all — anyone who signed up before this existed, or skipped the diagnostic via the SKIP button — checked field-by-field so a still-hidden section never leaves a blank "VISION STATEMENT" header floating on the page.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 85 → 86 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting `portfolioRenderVision` and `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml` verbatim (stubbing only the true external boundaries — other renderers like badge/task/project HTML, roster lookups — never the vision-statement logic itself) — 19 scenarios, all PASS: a player with no `visionStatement` at all leaves the section hidden on both surfaces; an all-empty `{create:'',impact:'',...}` object is also correctly treated as "nothing to show" and hidden; a fully-populated vision statement renders the header, all four fields, and the full connective sentence on both the owner's portfolio and the read-only viewer; a *partial* vision statement (only one field ever set) still renders rather than being hidden; HTML/script injected into a custom vision field (a player who typed `<script>` into the "write your own" box) is escaped, not executed, on both render paths; a missing DOM container doesn't throw; the other existing Portfolio sections (stats, badges, projects) render unaffected alongside the new block — regression check.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. Any player who completed the diagnostic's vision step (at signup, or via a later diagnostic re-run) will now see their Vision Statement on their own Portfolio and on their portfolio as viewed by anyone else. Players who signed up before this patch, or who skipped the diagnostic, simply won't have one — nothing to backfill, since the source data never existed for them.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.87 — DRAG-TO-REORDER (PROGRAMS/CHECKPOINTS/PROJECTS) + NUMBERED TASK ORDER TOGGLE (Aug 18, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "Allow changing of the order in Programs, Checkpoints, and Projects." → clarified: "It can be drag and drop." → then, in the same thread: "Also add a toggle to put the tasks ordered. Each topic or project would start the numbering over."
- IMPLEMENTATION (drag-to-reorder): every Mission Control list render already just walks its collection array in display order — `mcCheckpoints.map(...)`, the FLP-status-bucketed `mcProjects.map(...)`, `mcPrograms` grouped by Season — so the array's own order already IS the display order, and reordering the array is the whole feature; no new `sortOrder` field to keep in sync. New shared module (~line 31521, right after the Card Size slider helpers): `mcMoveArrayItem(arr, idKey, draggedId, targetId)` — the pure reorder primitive, splices the dragged item out and re-inserts it immediately before its drop target — plus `mcDragStart/mcDragOver/mcDragEnd/mcDragDrop`, standard HTML5 drag-and-drop wired via a shared `_mcDragAttrs(id, group, kind)` helper dropped into each card's root `<div>`. Reorder is scoped to whatever visual group a card already renders inside, so a drop can only ever reorder, never silently do something bigger: Checkpoints are a flat list (any-to-any); Projects are scoped to the FLP status bucket a card is currently sorted into (dragging across buckets would look like a phase change — refused as a no-op instead); Programs are scoped to their Season section. A cross-group drop just resets the dragged card's opacity and does nothing, rather than erroring. Wired into the three existing card-root divs: `mcRenderCheckpoints` (~line 31813), `mcRenderProjects` (~line 38159, group = that project's own FLP bucket, computed once per card), `mcRenderProgramsTab` (~line 39617, group = the season key already in scope from the existing Season-grouping loop). A small "⤁ Drag cards to reorder" hint renders above each grid when it has more than one item.
- BUG CAUGHT DURING TESTING: the first draft of `_mcDragAttrs` used `JSON.stringify()` to embed the dragged id/group/kind into each `ondragstart`/`ondrop` attribute value — but those attributes are themselves already inside a double-quoted HTML attribute, and `JSON.stringify` produces raw `"` marks, which would have prematurely closed the attribute and corrupted every card's markup on render. Caught by the behavioral test below before shipping; fixed to use the codebase's existing `&quot;`-escaping convention (the same pattern already used for `mcSaveAsTemplate(&quot;checkpoint&quot;,i)` elsewhere).
- IMPLEMENTATION (numbered task order toggle): a per-host display preference (`pflx_mc_tasks_numbered` in localStorage — not synced, same pattern as the Card Size sliders), toggled via a small switch dropped into the "📋 TASKS IN THIS PROJECT" header (Project cards) and the "◆ MISSION CONTENTS" header (Checkpoint cards). When on, `_mcTaskNumberPrefix(idx)` prefixes each task row with its 1-based position. Numbering restarts at 1 for every new group because it's driven purely by each group's own `.map()` index rather than a running total: in the Project panel that's each Topic group (`__topicGroups.map(...)` — a Project with no Topics is one implicit group); in the Checkpoint's Mission Contents panel that's each nested Project's own task list, and separately the "STANDALONE TASKS" list. No new task field or reordering UI for Tasks themselves — the toggle numbers whatever order the tasks already render in (which, for tasks under a Project or Checkpoint, is that same order the collection arrays are already in).
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 86 → 87 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting the full drag-reorder + numbering module verbatim (mocking only the true external boundary — `mcSaveData`/`mcRenderCheckpoints`/`mcRenderProjects`/`mcRenderProgramsTab`, never the reorder or numbering logic itself) — 46 scenarios, all PASS, including: `mcMoveArrayItem` correctly moves an item immediately before its target in both directions, is a no-op when dropping on itself or when either id is unknown (restoring the dragged item to its original slot rather than losing it), and never throws on null/non-array input; the generated drag-attribute markup survives a REAL HTML parse intact (proving the JSON.stringify bug above is actually fixed, not just theoretically) even with an adversarial id containing quotes/HTML/ampersands; a full checkpoint drag-and-drop end-to-end reorders the real array and triggers save+render; a project dropped across FLP status buckets is correctly refused (no reorder, no save, no render) while a same-bucket drop succeeds; a program/checkpoint kind mismatch and a stray drop with no active drag are both safe no-ops; dragend always resets the dragged card's visual opacity; the numbering toggle persists to localStorage, drives `_mcTaskNumberPrefix` correctly (1-based, "10." at index 9), and — the specific behavior asked for — two independently-numbered groups both start at "1." rather than one continuing the other's count.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. Drag any Checkpoint, Project, or Program card onto another to reorder (Projects only reorder within their current status column; Programs only within their Season). Toggle "#" next to "MISSION CONTENTS" or "TASKS IN THIS PROJECT" to see tasks numbered 1, 2, 3... restarting for each Topic or Project.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.88 — CHECKPOINT/PROJECT EDITS COULD SILENTLY REVERT ON SAVE (Aug 18, Ennis-reported)
- SYMPTOM: "I also added new Description for the first 2 checkpoints yet it didn't persist" — Ennis edited the Description field on Checkpoint Alpha and Checkpoint Beta, saved, and the cards kept showing the original seed text instead of what he'd just typed.
- ROOT CAUSE: `mcSaveCPForm`, `mcSaveQuickCPForm` (Checkpoints), `mcSaveProjectForm`, and `mcSaveQuickProjectForm` (Projects) all rebuild their record from scratch as a brand-new object literal on every save — and none of the four ever set `updatedAt`. That field isn't cosmetic: `_mcMergeById` (~line 24667), the merge function EVERY checkpoint/project cloud write and cloud pull runs through (`_mcMergeQueueWithCloud`'s read-merge-write before every push, and `_mcApplyCollection`'s merge on every ingest/Realtime tick), decides which of two copies of the same record survives purely by comparing `_mcTs(item)` — which reads `item.updatedAt`. A freshly-saved record with no `updatedAt` reads as timestamp `0`. Any OLDER cloud copy that happened to carry an actual (even ancient) `updatedAt` — planted once, on some past save, by an unrelated stamp-on-open helper at ~line 32774 that mutates the in-memory record the moment its edit form opens (`cp.updatedAt = cp.updatedAt || Date.now()`) — would then legitimately win the "higher timestamp" comparison and silently overwrite the just-typed edit on the very next push or pull, with no error and no warning. Confirmed by first reproducing the exact failure with the old (unstamped) object shape against a realistically-stale cloud copy — reverted to the original seed description, matching Ennis's report precisely — before verifying the fix.
- FIX: all four save functions now stamp `updatedAt: Date.now()` into the object they build, right alongside `id`, on every single save — so a fresh edit always carries the newest possible timestamp and can never lose a merge to a stale copy, no matter which side of the merge it lands on (push-side, ingest-side, or reversed argument order). Projects were patched identically to Checkpoints even though Ennis only reported Checkpoints — they run through the exact same `_mcMergeById` merge path and were equally exposed; better to close it now than field the same report again for a Project description next.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 87 → 88 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting the real `_mcMergeById`/`_mcTs`/tombstone functions verbatim from the shipped file — 8 scenarios: first reproduces the bug outright with the old unstamped shape (a fresh edit loses to a stale timestamped cloud copy — proves the test harness actually catches the real failure, not a strawman); then with the fix, a fresh Alpha+Beta edit survives the push-side merge-before-write, survives the ingest-side merge, survives with merge argument order reversed, doesn't disturb an unrelated third checkpoint present only on the cloud side, and a genuine later real-device edit still correctly beats a genuine earlier one (proves the fix is a real timestamp comparison, not a "local always wins" shortcut that would break legitimate multi-device syncing). All 8 PASS.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. Re-save the Alpha and Beta descriptions once more (the reverted text was never actually stored anywhere to recover — the last thing written to both localStorage and the cloud row was the old seed text) and they'll stick from here on, for every checkpoint and project going forward.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.89 — REALTIME ECHO LOOP WAS STARVING EVERY CLOUD PUSH, INCLUDING v1.88's OWN FIX (Aug 18, Ennis-reported, same-day escalation)
- SYMPTOM: Ennis re-tested immediately after v1.88 deployed (confirmed hard-refreshed) and reported "The descriptions are not saved" again — same exact failure, unchanged. v1.88's `updatedAt` fix was real and necessary but did not touch the actual mechanism blocking him.
- INVESTIGATION: rather than guess again, reproduced live — logged into his actual production account via browser automation, opened Checkpoint Alpha's edit form, confirmed the description field held stale generic seed text ("Complete objectives for the Prototype/Testing phase of Digital Design" — identical across 7 of the 10 Greek-named checkpoints, clearly never individually authored), typed a real edit, and called `mcSaveCPForm()` directly while watching both the in-memory state and the Supabase `pflx_mc_checkpoints` row. Confirmed: `mcCheckpoints[0].description` and `localStorage['pflx_mc_checkpoints']` updated correctly and instantly (v1.88's `updatedAt` stamp present) — the LOCAL save has never been broken. The Supabase row, checked directly via SQL immediately after, still held the pre-edit text and the OLD `updatedAt` (weeks stale). The edit was never reaching the cloud at all — not reverting later, never arriving.
- ROOT CAUSE: the browser console showed 2,300+ lines of `[roster] ← realtime cohort-group update: 12 groups` logged in under two minutes — an infinite Realtime echo loop. `pflxStartRosterSubscriber()`'s handler for the legacy `cohortGroups` app_data row (~line 64264) unconditionally called `mcSaveData('cohortgroups')` on every incoming realtime event, with no check for whether the merge actually changed anything. `mcSaveData` → `mcCloudSync('cohortgroups')` relays the (possibly identical) list to the X-Coin iframe, which writes `cohortGroups` back to Supabase even when nothing changed — re-firing this exact same Realtime subscription. No dirty-check meant that echo never stopped. Every queued cloud write — checkpoints, projects, players, everything in `_mcCloudQueue` — shares ONE debounce timer (`_mcCloudTimer` in `mcCloudPush`) that gets cleared and restarted on every single queue write. With the cohortGroups loop firing multiple times per second continuously, that shared timer never found a quiet 1-second window to actually flush — so `_mcCloudFlush()` essentially never ran, and nothing new reached Supabase, for ANY collection, the entire time the loop was active. Checkpoint description edits were the symptom Ennis happened to notice; every other host edit (Projects, Players, cohort assignments) was silently exposed to the same starvation the whole time this loop was running.
- FIX: the `cohortGroups` realtime handler now does a dirty-check before touching anything — it computes the merged list, compares it (JSON-stringified) against what's already held locally, and only calls `mcSaveData('cohortgroups')` (and fires the `pflx-cohorts-updated` event) when the merge actually produced a different list. A genuine remote change (a real host adding/editing a cohort group elsewhere) still applies exactly once. An echo of its own prior write — or a duplicate delivery of an already-applied update — is now a silent no-op instead of a fresh write that re-triggers the same subscription. This terminates the loop at its source without touching the Realtime subscription, the X-Coin bridge, or the debounce timer itself.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 88 → 89 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks). Live-code behavioral test extracting the real merge+dirty-check logic verbatim — 10 scenarios, all PASS: a genuine new remote cohort group is merged and saved exactly once; an identical echo payload is correctly rejected (no resave, no event, no state change) — the core loop-breaking behavior; a two-round simulation (real change round 1, its own echo arriving as round 2) confirms the loop terminates after exactly one legitimate save; an empty incoming payload never reaches the merge at all (pre-existing outer guard, confirmed intact). Additionally reproduced and confirmed the underlying bug live against Ennis's real production account before writing the fix: edited Checkpoint Alpha's description through the actual UI, confirmed local state saved correctly and instantly, confirmed via direct Supabase query that the cloud row never received it, and captured the 2,300+-line realtime echo storm in the live console — this is not a theoretical fix, the exact failure was reproduced and root-caused against production data first.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately. This should also resolve any other "my edit didn't show up on another device / after a refresh" reports from around today's date, since the starvation affected every collection, not just Checkpoints — worth keeping an eye out for related FeedForward reports to close out retroactively. Ennis: your Checkpoint Alpha description currently holds a literal "TEST EDIT by Claude diagnostic" string from the live reproduction — worth resetting it to real copy now that saves are confirmed working end-to-end.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.24 — X-BOT 48H RESPONSE-TIME SLA TRACKING (Aug 19, Ennis)
- REQUEST: as part of the "report feature in MC under Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project" ask, Ennis: "it should definitely keep track of response time... If a user is tagged through the channel, everyone, or especially directly tagged then the response time is 48 hours. This is important." Directly followed Ennis confirming he'd flipped Discord's Message Content privileged intent for X-Bot's Application (the one real gap in X-Bot's already-live Discord/Slack read pipeline, found in `pflx-darkcampus` — see the "Phase B" writeup in `PFLX_Integration_Plan_v2.md`) — without that intent, Discord's REST API returns `content: ""` for messages X-Bot didn't author, so a mention/tag couldn't even be read yet.
- IMPLEMENTATION: new `src/app/lib/mentionWatch.ts` in `pflx-darkcampus` — a durable watch list (`dc_mention_watch`), not just a log line. `buildTagResolver()` joins `users` × `dc_member_links` once per scan (same join pattern as `xbot-alerts/route.ts`'s `buildPlayerResolver`); `detectTags()` finds direct `<@id>`/`<@SLACKID>` mentions and REAL `@everyone`/`@here`/`<!channel>` tags per platform (Discord's own `mention_everyone` flag is preferred over text-matching, so a ping without the "Mention @everyone" permission doesn't start a false clock) and fans a broadcast tag out to every currently-linked roster member; `recordTagWatch()` writes pending rows (dedup'd on player+channel+source-message); `resolveTagWatch()` clears any pending row for a player the moment they post again in that same channel; `sweepOverdueTagWatch()` escalates anything still pending past 48h straight into `dc_violations` with `violationType: "unresponsive"` — the SAME queue the existing violation scanner already uses, so it shows up in the Host Control Panel with the existing fine/dismiss actions for free (`xbot-alerts/route.ts` needed zero changes — its `action:"fine"`/`"dismiss_violation"` handlers already operate generically on any `dc_violations` row by id). Nothing here auto-deducts XC; a host still has to click Fine, same as every other violation — deliberately stayed out of the separate "should the inactivity auto-tax gap be fixed" question flagged in the integration plan, since that's a different, not-yet-answered decision.
- WIRED INTO BOTH existing scan paths, since they cover different platforms/cadences and neither alone is sufficient: `api/xbot-scan/route.ts` (the 5x/day Discord-only cron) is what actually catches an overdue tag even if no host ever opens DarkCampus — replaced its old ad hoc `<@id>`-only regex block (which only fed the tag-DM) with `detectTags`/`recordTagWatch`/`resolveTagWatch`, added `mention_everyone?: boolean` to its `RawMessage` type, and calls `sweepOverdueTagWatch()` once per run (pushing an escalation count into the existing `gate[]` digest when >0). `api/messages/route.ts`'s `scanInboundMessages()` (the on-demand scan that fires whenever the DarkCampus UI reads a channel — Discord AND Slack) got the same resolve/record wiring plus its own sweep call, so an open DarkCampus tab catches overdue tags between cron ticks too. A shared `dcChannelId()` helper in the cron matches `buildLiveChannel()`'s id scheme (`dc-<guildId>-<platformChannelId>`) so a tag recorded by one path and resolved by the other land on the same watch row instead of two. Direct `@mentions` still get the existing PFLX Chat DM (`dmTaggedPlayers`, unchanged); `@everyone`/`@here` deliberately does NOT trigger a DM to the whole linked roster (would be spammy) — it silently starts the 48h watch, and the response report is where a broadcast tag shows up. Added `"unresponsive"` to `XBotAlert.violationType` in `lib/types.ts`.
- Files: `pflx-darkcampus` — new `src/app/lib/mentionWatch.ts`; edited `src/app/api/xbot-scan/route.ts`, `src/app/api/messages/route.ts`, `src/app/lib/types.ts`. No `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` changes this patch (DARKCAMPUS track numbers independently from PLATFORM).
- Verified: this checkout of `pflx-darkcampus` has no `node_modules`/`tsconfig.json` (a partial mirror, missing `package.json` and several UI components per earlier session notes), so no local build/typecheck was possible — ran `tsc --noEmit` per-file (syntax-only, ignoring unresolvable-import noise) against all 4 changed files, 0 syntax errors. Real confirmation: committed + pushed to `main` (`f8fc504`), Vercel auto-deploy for `pflx-darkcampus` (which DOES run a full Next.js build, i.e. real typecheck) confirmed `state: READY` before this entry was written.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required to activate — live immediately on both the cron and the on-demand scan. Still open from the integration plan and NOT addressed by this patch: where new LTI/Canva server code should live (`pflx-platform` vs `pflx-pathway-portal`), green light on the Phase A Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project report UI itself (this patch only feeds it data — `dc_violations` rows with `violationType:"unresponsive"` — there's still no report UI in Mission Control reading them yet), whether to also fix the existing inactivity auto-tax risk gap, and the Canva LTI registration approach.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.90 — SCOPE ACTIVITY REPORT (SEASON/PROGRAM/CHECKPOINT/PROJECT) IN PLAYER ANALYTICS (Aug 19, Ennis)
- REQUEST: "add this report feature in MC under each: Season, Program, Checkpoint, Project. The hosts should be able to generate a report based on Feedforward form, Discord/Slack/Darkcampus, Task Submission Frequency, Time spent Online in PFLX. It should highlight all activity with digital badges earned, tax/fines given, and it should definitely keep track of response time... This is important." This is "Phase A" of the Host Reporting feature from `PFLX_Integration_Plan_v2.md` — buildable now, independent of the still-open LTI/Canva architectural decisions, and it consumes the `dc_violations`/`dc_mention_watch` data PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.24 (same day) just started producing. FeedForward Form ingestion is explicitly NOT included — there is still no in-app pipeline reading that Google Form; that piece stays with the separate `pflx-feedforward-triage` skill, unchanged.
- IMPLEMENTATION: new "PLAYER USAGE & REPORTS" scope picker in Mission Control's PLAYER ANALYTICS tab (`host-analytics` panel) — pick a scope type (Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project), the specific node, and a window (7/14/30d), then Run Report or Export CSV. Deliberately reuses existing machinery rather than building a parallel model:
  - **Player-in-scope** (`pflxScopeGetPlayers`) reuses the existing `pflxPlayerCanSeeItem` cohort/hierarchy engine — "in scope" here means exactly what "can see this" already means everywhere else in the app (Player Portal, PflxDataBus.mc.get). `assignedPlayers`/`enrolledPlayers` are unioned in explicitly on top, since `pflxEffectiveAssignees`'s player-fence logic only reads `assignedPlayers`. Confirmed (via the behavioral test, see below) that an item with NO own cohort and NO resolvable parent chain is, correctly, visible to everyone — this is the pre-existing "top of an unfenced chain" convention, not new behavior.
  - **Task-in-scope** (`pflxScopeGetTaskIds`) walks DOWN the hierarchy via both forward (`task.projectId`, `project.checkpointId`) and reverse (`project.taskIds`, `checkpoint.taskIds`/`projectIds`) pointers — the mirror of how `pflxPlayerCanSeeItem` walks up.
  - **Badges + tax/fines** read off `player.activity[]` (`award_granted` entries logged by every `PflxDataBus.award()` call — badge grants AND `xc_deduct` fines alike funnel through the same log), NOT the separate `mcPlayerModifiers` ledger, since that ledger doesn't carry scope/reason correlation for auto-fired modifier fines. A known limit, flagged rather than silently worked around: auto-tax events (e.g. the checkpoint-lateness sweep) don't embed a scope id in their `reason` string, so the report counts "which players in this scope got fined," not "which fines this exact node caused" — direct task/checkpoint/project award calls (which DO embed `reason:'task:'+id` etc.) don't have this limit.
  - **Response-time SLA** bridges DarkCampus's `dc_violations`/`dc_mention_watch` Supabase `app_data` keys via the existing `pflxCloudKvLoad` cross-app bridge (no loader for these keys existed in `preview.html` before this patch), matched by `playerId` first, falling back to a normalized brand-name match — same dual-key pattern DarkCampus's own resolver uses.
  - **Time online** keeps the pre-existing `pflxAnalyticsAggregate` local-device-only session tracker as-is (never synced via `pflxCloudKvPush`) rather than silently rearchitecting it — flagged with a footnote (`*`) in the UI instead of misrepresenting cross-device coverage. A real, pre-existing gap, not introduced by this patch.
  - CSV export (`pflxScopeReportExportCSV`) shares `pflxScopeComputeReport` with the on-screen render so the two can never disagree.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 89 → 90 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (14 non-empty `<script>` blocks, `node --check` on each).
