Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxPlayerCanSeeItem` + its full `ppGet*`/tier-variant dependency chain and all new `pflxScope*` functions verbatim (real fixtures: 4 players across 3 cohorts, a Season → 2 Checkpoints → Project → 3 Tasks hierarchy exercising both forward and reverse FK pointers, submissions spanning a 30-day window boundary) — 17 scenarios, all PASS: player resolution correct at all 4 scope types including cohort-fence enforcement and hierarchy walk-up through unfenced nodes; unknown scopeId returns empty, no throw; task-id collection at each scope level (direct + nested reverse pointers); submission window-vs-all-time counting (a 40-day-old submission correctly excluded from a 30-day window, still counted all-time); badge/tax parsing off `player.activity[]` with window filtering; SLA matching by playerId then brand-name fallback (an unmatched violation correctly attaches to nobody); `Season.allCohorts===true` and explicit `enrolledPlayers` union edge cases; a full DOM-shim end-to-end render; CSV export content.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required — live immediately under PLAYER ANALYTICS. Still open, unchanged from the integration plan: LTI/Canva server-location decision, Canva LTI registration approach, whether to fix the auto-tax risk gap (no per-player cap/appeal flow — this report will make the pattern visible, but doesn't change the underlying policy), and FeedForward Form in-app ingestion (still handled separately by the `pflx-feedforward-triage` skill, not surfaced in this report).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.91 — BADGE-AWARD XC LOGGING, PORTFOLIO BADGE-COUNT SYNC, AND P2P TASK RESUBMISSION REVERTING (Aug 19, Kaitlin-reported via Discord)
- SYMPTOM: Kaitlin (beta) reported three things in the same Discord thread after confirming an earlier badge fix: (1) her 4 badges "should total 1,800 XC" but her activity/total didn't reflect it, expecting 2,075 XC total vs. an actual 1,875; (2) a P2P task she'd submitted "showed as submitted, but the next day it showed 'Submit for Approval' again, as if it had not been submitted" — she had to resubmit; (3) her own Portfolio view showed 4 badges while the X-Coin section showed 5, asking for badge count and XC to be "synced correctly."
- INVESTIGATION: queried Supabase directly rather than trusting the report at face value. Kaitlin's authoritative `pflx_player_<id>` row shows `xc: 1875`, `digitalBadges: 5`, `badgeCounts: {primary:2, signature:2}` (sums to 4 — the badgeCounts/digitalBadges drift this codebase has hit before, per the v1.76/v1.77 Handoff entries). Cross-checked her actual configured rewards in `pflx_mc_checkpoints`: Checkpoint Alpha's `rewardBadges[]` sum to 1800 XC with `xcReward:0` (no separate flat bonus), Checkpoint Beta similarly has no completion bonus configured, and no `xc_multiply`-style flat-bonus modifier exists in `pflx_mc_modifiers`. Her math (1800 + 50 + 225 + 75 = 2075/2150) assumed flat per-checkpoint completion bonuses that were never configured — 1875 (1800 in badges + 75 pending P2P) is the mathematically correct total for what's actually configured. Nothing was missing from her balance; two real bugs were, however, confirmed by reading the code: (a) her balance was right but the REPORTING of it was wrong, and (b) badge count truly was desynced between two display paths.
- ROOT CAUSE 1 (badge-XC reported as 0): `PflxDataBus.award()` captures `deltaXC` from `awardObj.xc` at the very top of the function, before the badge branch runs. The badge branch (further down) correctly adds `b.xcValue` into `changes.xc`/`changes.totalXcoin` — Kaitlin's actual balance was always right — but both `logActivity()`'s payload and the `pflx_award_granted` broadcast used the stale pre-badge-branch `deltaXC`, so every badge-only award (checkpoint reward badges, which never pass a top-level `xc`) logged/broadcast as `xc:0` even when it carried real value. This is exactly why her activity feed never showed the 1800 XC her badges were worth.
- ROOT CAUSE 2 (4 vs 5 badges): `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml` (used when viewing OTHER players' portfolios) already had a v1.77 fix — `Math.max(totalBadgesFromCounts, digitalBadges||0)` — because `badgeCounts` under-counts whenever a badge is pushed onto `badges[]` without going through `award()`'s badgeCounts-increment branch (legacy/onboarding grants). The OWNER's own Portfolio view (`portfolioRender`, a separate function) never got that same fix, so it showed `totalBadges` (from the undercounting `badgeCounts`) while X-Coin's own tile reads `digitalBadges` (the correct raw array length) — hence 4 vs 5 for the same player.
- ROOT CAUSE 3 (P2P submission reverting): traced through every layer of the submit → cloud-sync → merge chain. `mcSubmitToHost`/`mcPostToDarkCampus` (the "Submit Task" modal's handlers) stored `submittedBy: activeSession.name` — a display name — while every one of the 11+ consumers of `task.submission.submittedBy` (approval-gating, the approvals-queue builder, `mcApproveTask`'s XC-payout resolution, checkpoint/project completion sweeps, brand/cohort lookups) expects a player ID, matching `ppSubmitTask`'s own correct convention. Separately and more directly causing the revert: `_mcMergeTasks` (the merge-not-replace function that already explicitly protects `.submissions[]` and `.status` against being overwritten by a stale copy) had NO protection for the legacy singular `.submission` field — `Object.assign({}, loc, newer)` would silently drop a present submission whenever the side picked as "newer" (by `updatedAt`, including on a tie) happened to be a copy that predated it. Neither `mcSubmitToHost` nor `mcPostToDarkCampus` bumped `updatedAt` on submit, making a tie (and therefore a drop) the likely outcome the very next sync.
- FIX:
  1. `PflxDataBus.award()` — added `badgeXcDelta` (from `b.xcValue`, NOT scaled by `grantCount` — deliberately matches the pre-existing crediting behavior exactly, this only fixes what's reported) and a `totalXcDelta = deltaXC + badgeXcDelta`, used in both the `broadcastAll` award event and `logActivity`'s payload.
  2. `portfolioRender()` — added the same `Math.max(totalBadges, user.digitalBadges||0)` guard `pflxRenderPortfolioFullHtml` already used, so the owner's own Portfolio tile can never show fewer badges than X-Coin does.
  3. `mcSubmitToHost` / `mcPostToDarkCampus` — `submittedBy` now stores `activeSession.id` (matching the codebase-wide id convention) instead of `activeSession.name`, and both now stamp `mcTasks[...].updatedAt = Date.now()` on submit.
  4. `_mcMergeTasks` — added explicit protection for the legacy singular `.submission` field, matching the existing pattern for `.submissions[]`/`.status`: an absent submission never wins over a present one; between two present submissions, the one with the later `submittedAt` wins.
  5. `mcApproveTask`'s legacy (non-`submissions[]`) approval branch — added `if (task.status === 'approved') return;` at the top, matching the idempotency guard already used by `mcApprovePlayerSubmission`/the checkpoint payout helper, so a duplicate approval call can't double-pay.
  6. Approvals-queue history panel — `it.submittedBy` now renders through `_pflxPlayerBrandById()` first (falling back to the raw stored value), so switching #3's `submittedBy` to an id doesn't show hosts a raw player-id string in that one display.
- Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 90 → 91 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks, `node --check` on each). Two live-code behavioral test suites extracting the real functions verbatim: `_mcMergeTasks`/`_mcMergeTaskSubs`/`_mcTs` — 7 scenarios all PASS (absent submission never beats present, on a timestamp tie and on incoming-is-newer; two present submissions pick the later `submittedAt` in both directions; `.status` rank-protection and `.submissions[]` approval-is-terminal protection both unaffected — regression check; plain no-submission merge unaffected). `PflxDataBus.award()` + `logActivity` — 8 scenarios all PASS (badge-only award with `xcValue` now logs the correct non-zero xc while the actual balance was already correct; plain XC-only award still logs correctly — regression; combined XC+badge award sums correctly; a badge with no `xcValue` still logs `xc:0` — no false positive). The `submittedBy`/`updatedAt`/idempotency-guard/portfolio-badge-count edits were verified by direct inspection of the shipped lines (mechanical one-line changes, each confirmed present and correct) rather than a separate harness.
- DATA: no Supabase data surgery performed. Kaitlin's existing 1875 XC balance was confirmed mathematically correct and complete for what's actually configured — nothing is missing, so nothing was touched. Her existing pending P2P resubmission was NOT retroactively edited; it should survive normally going forward under this patch, but a host still needs to review/approve it as usual.
- HOST ACTIONS: review and approve Kaitlin's current pending P2P resubmission (this patch fixes the mechanism that dropped it, but doesn't retroactively touch her existing data). Consider replying to Kaitlin in Discord that her 1,875 XC total is correct as configured (1800 badge XC + 75 pending task, no separate flat 50/225 completion bonus exists on Checkpoint Alpha/Beta) — worth confirming with her whether those flat bonuses were ever intended, since if so that's a checkpoint-config change, not a bug.

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.92 — FEEDFORWARD FORM DATA IN THE PLAYER ANALYTICS SCOPE REPORT (Aug 19-20, Ennis-requested)
- REQUEST: after PATCH PLATFORM v1.90 shipped the Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project scope report, Ennis asked for it to also analyze FeedForward Form submissions per player — explicitly gated by "a toggle to turn that on in the season, program, checkpoint, or project," not on everywhere by default. Separately, Ennis asked to switch the Form's "FULL NAME" field to a dropdown of current brand names (matching how the rest of the platform identifies players) rather than free text — see the DARKCAMPUS entry below for why that part shipped in code but not yet on the live Form.
- SCOPE DECISIONS (confirmed with Ennis before building, since each has a real tradeoff): (1) data reaches the Console through a secured server-side proxy, not by publishing the Sheet to the web — the Sheet holds real tester PII (email, name, written notes) and a "publish to web" link would sit reachable indefinitely by anyone with the URL; (2) the toggle is a persistent setting saved on each Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project record's edit form (like the existing numbered-task-order toggle), not a one-off report-time choice; (3) a submission is matched to a report scope by its Checkpoint (the only field the Sheet actually records) and then rolled up through the existing hierarchy-walking logic, same as task-in-scope resolution already does.
- ARCHITECTURE: rather than the Console calling a new public HTTP endpoint directly (CORS surface, an unauthenticated route reachable by anyone who finds the URL), this follows the SAME bridge PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.24's SLA data already uses — a server-side scan in `pflx-darkcampus` (piggybacked onto the existing `xbot-scan` 5x/day cron, see the DARKCAMPUS entry) refreshes a filtered cache (`pflx_feedforward_cache`) in Supabase `app_data`; the Console reads it via the existing `pflxCloudKvLoad` convention, same as `dc_violations`/`dc_mention_watch`. No new public endpoint, no CORS, no credentials anywhere near the client.
- IMPLEMENTATION (`pflx-platform-check/preview.html`):
  - Added a `feedforwardEnabled` checkbox to all four edit forms (Season, Program, Checkpoint, Project) — `mc-season-feedforward-enabled` / `mc-program-tab-feedforward-enabled` / `mc-cp-feedforward-enabled` / `mc-project-feedforward-enabled` — wired into each show function (populate on edit) and each save function (persist), matching the existing `skipCompletionApproval`/`applyEnabled` checkbox pattern in the same forms exactly.
  - `pflxScopeGetCheckpointsInScope(scopeType, scopeId)` — new resolver: a Checkpoint scope is itself; a Project scope walks both `project.checkpointId` (forward) and `checkpoint.projectIds` (reverse) since either can be the populated pointer depending on how the Project was attached; Program/Season scopes filter Checkpoints by `programId`/`seasonId`. Mirrors `pflxScopeGetTaskIds`'s existing dual-pointer convention.
  - `pflxFeedForwardNormalizeCpName(s)` — strips "CHECKPOINT" and non-alphanumerics so "Checkpoint Alpha" (the Console's name) and "ALPHA" (the Sheet's free-text value) match regardless of host/tester wording.
  - `pflxScopeFetchFeedForward` / `pflxScopeGetFeedForwardForNode` — loads the cache (only when the selected node's toggle is actually on, so a report on a toggled-off node never even fetches tester PII into memory) and attributes each in-scope-checkpoint row to a player: brand name first (normalized, matches the new dropdown column once it's live), falling back to email for rows submitted before that column exists. A row matching neither is dropped rather than guessed at.
  - `pflxScopeComputeReport` / `pflxScopeReportRender` / `pflxScopeReportExportCSV` — extended with two more columns (FeedForward submission count, bright-idea count) and a "fetched as of" timestamp in the summary line; shows "—" instead of `0` when the toggle is off so a host can't mistake "not enabled" for "zero submissions."
  - Also fixed while touching `mcSaveSeasonForm`'s object literal (same file, same save-function shape as every other change here): Season was the one save function of the four still missing an `updatedAt` stamp — Checkpoint/Project got this in v1.88, Program already had it. Same exposure class: an unstamped save reads as timestamp 0 in `_mcMergeById` and can silently lose to a stale cloud copy on the next sync.
  - Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 91 → 92 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks, `node --check` on each). Live-code behavioral test extracting `pflxScopeGetCheckpointsInScope`/`pflxFeedForwardNormalizeCpName`/`pflxScopeFetchFeedForward`/`pflxScopeGetFeedForwardForNode` verbatim — 14 scenarios, all PASS: Checkpoint/Project (both forward and reverse pointer)/Program/Season scope resolution; name normalization equates "Checkpoint Alpha" and "ALPHA" and rejects a different Checkpoint; brand-name matching correctly attributes and counts multiple rows to one player with bright-idea counting excluding "n/a"-style non-answers and the latest note tracked correctly; a row whose respondent matches no current player is dropped rather than mis-attributed; email fallback correctly matches a legacy pre-dropdown row; empty cache/no in-scope checkpoints returns cleanly with no crash.
- HOST ACTIONS: this ships OFF everywhere — check "Include FeedForward Form submissions in this [node]'s report" on any Season/Program/Checkpoint/Project you want it for. It also needs the one-time DarkCampus setup step described in the DARKCAMPUS v1.25 entry below before any data will actually show up (a toggled-on node will just show "Loading FeedForward data…" / zero counts until that's done). The Form's name field is still free text as of this patch — see DARKCAMPUS v1.25 for status on the dropdown switch Ennis asked for.

## PATCH DARKCAMPUS v1.25 — FEEDFORWARD FORM → SUPABASE CACHE BRIDGE (Aug 19-20, Ennis-requested)
- PURPOSE: the server-side half of PATCH PLATFORM v1.92 above — the Console can't hold Google credentials (it's a static file with no server), so this scan runs here instead and hands off a filtered, cached copy through Supabase, the same way `dc_violations`/`dc_mention_watch` already reach the Console.
- IMPLEMENTATION: new `src/app/lib/feedforward.ts` — `refreshFeedForwardCache()` mints a Sheets-readonly access token from the SAME Google service-account credentials `api/drive-upload/route.ts` already uses (`GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL`/`GOOGLE_SA_PRIVATE_KEY` — already set on Vercel, no new secrets), fetches the "PFLX FeedForward Form (Responses)" spreadsheet's "Form Responses 1" tab via `spreadsheets.values.get`, parses the header row dynamically (substring-matches "timestamp"/"email"/"brand name"/"full name"/"checkpoint"/"task notes"/"bright idea" rather than hardcoded column letters, so a host reordering or renaming columns doesn't silently break it), and writes up to 2000 rows into `pflx_feedforward_cache` via the existing `saveData()` Supabase helper. The token-minting function is a deliberate small duplication of `drive-upload/route.ts`'s (not a shared import) — touching that already-working route for an unrelated feature carried more risk than 12 duplicated lines.
- WIRED into the existing `xbot-scan` cron (`0 23,4,9,14,18 * * *`, 5x/day) as a new "3b" step rather than a new Vercel Cron entry — unrelated to the pre-existing Discord `#feedforward-board` channel scan already in that route (different thing: this is the actual Google Form). Wrapped in its own try/catch so a Sheets API hiccup never breaks the Discord scan; only a real failure escalates into the gate digest (a quiet success stays quiet, same as everything else on this cron).
- ONE-TIME SETUP STILL NEEDED (not something this session can do): the service account needs read access to the Sheet, which is a separate grant from its existing Drive-folder access. **Ennis: open the "PFLX FeedForward Form (Responses)" sheet → Share → paste the `GOOGLE_SA_EMAIL` value (check it in Vercel → pflx-darkcampus → Settings → Environment Variables — not reproduced here since it's a credential) → Viewer.** Until that's done, `refreshFeedForwardCache()` will fail cleanly (escalates once per cron tick as a `violation` gate item, not silently) and any Console report with the FeedForward toggle on will just show zero data.
- ALSO REQUESTED, NOT YET DONE: switching the Form's "FULL NAME" question to a dropdown of current brand names. Pulled the current roster (134 distinct brand names from `pflx_mc_players`) and attempted the edit via Chrome browser automation, which failed — `screenshot`/`click` both errored with "Cannot access a chrome-extension:// URL of different extension" across two separate tabs and a retry the next day, consistent with a conflicting extension in that Chrome profile rather than a page-load issue. Handed Ennis the exact manual steps + the brand list to paste in himself as a fallback; will retry the automation if asked. The Sheets-scan code above already prefers a "brand name" column over "full name" the moment that header exists, so no further platform/darkcampus code changes are needed once the Form itself is edited — this is purely a manual Google Forms UI step now.
- Verified: `tsc --noEmit` (ad hoc, `@types/node` installed for the check since this checkout has no `node_modules`/`package.json` install) on both changed files — `feedforward.ts` compiles clean; `xbot-scan/route.ts`'s only reported error is the pre-existing, expected "Cannot find module '@supabase/supabase-js'" (the package genuinely isn't installed in this ad hoc checkout, not a real error — same caveat as every prior DARKCAMPUS entry's verification). Real confirmation: committed + pushed to `main`, Vercel auto-deploy for `pflx-darkcampus` (which runs a full Next.js build) confirmed `state: READY` before this entry was written.
- HOST ACTIONS: do the Share-with-service-account step above — nothing else in this patch needs it. First live cache refresh happens on the next `xbot-scan` cron tick after that Share is done (within ~5 hours, or fire it manually via the Vercel dashboard's cron trigger if you want it sooner).

## PATCH PLATFORM v1.93 — MC↔X-COIN XC/BADGE SYNC GAP (Aug 24, Kaitlin-reported via Discord)
- SYMPTOM: Kaitlin, in #welcome-and-rules → moved to a DM thread: "it still shows the same. my task is approved but xc and badges have some problems." Screenshot showed her X-Coin/Portfolio view frozen at 1,875 lifetime XC with the same badge set as the Aug 19 v1.91 investigation, despite reporting a task approval since.
- INVESTIGATION: queried Supabase directly rather than trusting the report at face value. Found TWO live, diverging copies of her player record: `pflx_mc_players` (Mission Control's bulk roster) showed 3,400 XC / 7 badges — including two, `badge-digital-tool-master` and `badge-resilient-learner`, that existed NOWHERE on `pflx_player_player-import-1784088654295-23`, the individual per-id row X-Coin/Portfolio/login actually read. That row's `updatedAt` was frozen at Aug 18 03:52 UTC — nothing had reached it since. Sampled other active testers to size the scope: Nirmal Sudheesh (`player-1784131204461-l0qc4`) showed the same class of drift in the opposite direction (his canonical row correctly held the higher 5,400 XC, but his badge array — 4 — lagged mcPlayers' 6). Confirms this is a general MC↔X-Coin sync gap, not something specific to Kaitlin.
- ROOT CAUSE: `PflxDataBus.award()`/`applyUpdate()` mirror PLAYERS → mcPlayers on every write (`broadcastPlayerChange`), but nothing mirrored the reverse direction. Two concrete mc-side write paths bypass PLAYERS/`pflx_player_<id>` entirely: (1) Mission Control's Player Management "Edit Player" modal (`mcEditPlayer` → `mcSavePlayerForm`'s edit-existing branch) wrote XC/level/name/etc. straight onto `mcPlayers[idx]` and called `mcSaveData('players')` — never touching PLAYERS. (2) Badge revoke in that same modal (`mcRemovePlayerBadge`) spliced `mcPlayers[i].badges` directly, same gap. Either path could leave `pflx_mc_players` ahead of the row every other surface reads from, with no mechanism to ever catch it back up.
- FIX:
  1. `mcSavePlayerForm()` (edit-existing branch) — after updating `mcPlayers[idx]`, now finds the matching PLAYERS record (by id, falling back to brand) and mirrors name/brand/cohort/pathway/email/xc/level/pin/image/studioId onto it, keeping `totalXcoin` monotonic, then calls `persistPlayers([id])` so the individual cloud row updates immediately.
  2. `mcRemovePlayerBadge()` — now recomputes `badgeCounts`/`digitalBadges` from the trimmed badge array (matching the sibling "pm-ed-" edit modal's existing recompute shape) and mirrors the same trimmed `badges`/`badgeCounts`/`digitalBadges` onto the matching PLAYERS record, then `persistPlayers([id])`.
  3. Defense-in-depth: new `_mcReconcilePlayersFromMc()`, hooked into `mcSaveData('players'|'all')` — the single choke point every mc-side player mutation funnels through (including any write path not found in this trace, e.g. CSV import). For every mcPlayers entry with a matching PLAYERS record, pulls `xc`/`totalXcoin` up to mc's value ONLY when mc is numerically ahead, unions `badges` (via new `_pflxUnionBadgeArrays`, same corruption-guard as `_mcMergePlayers`) when mc's array is longer, and raises `badgeCounts` per-category only when mc's count is higher. Deliberately monotonic/one-way: a stale mcPlayers snapshot in some other tab can never use this path to regress a player's real balance, and a genuine host correction (lowering XC, revoking a badge) is handled by fixes #1/#2 above instead, not by this safety net.
  4. Files: `pflx-platform-check/preview.html` only. Bumped `PFLX_PATCH` 92 → 93 (`PFLX_BUILD` unchanged, `2026.08`).
- DATA (Supabase, one transaction, verification SELECT after): manually reconciled the two players already found drifted, applying exactly the values the shipped fix would compute — Kaitlin (`pflx_player_player-import-1784088654295-23`): xc 1875→3400, totalXcoin 1875→3400, digitalBadges 5→7, badgeCounts {primary:2,signature:2}→{primary:7,signature:3}, badges unioned to mcPlayers'7-entry set. Nirmal (`pflx_player_player-1784131204461-l0qc4`): xc/totalXcoin left untouched at the correct 5400 (mc's 2050/5250 was NOT applied — verifies the monotonic guard), digitalBadges 4→6, badgeCounts {primary:2,signature:2}→primary:9,signature:5}, badges unioned to 6. Verified both rows post-write via a follow-up SELECT.
- Verified: syntax gate clean (13 non-empty `<script>` blocks, `node --check` on each). Live-code behavioral test extracting `_mcReconcilePlayersFromMc`/`_pflxUnionBadgeArrays` verbatim from the shipped file — 8 scenarios all PASS: Kaitlin's exact real Supabase drift reproduced and correctly reconciled (xc/totalXcoin/badges/digitalBadges/badgeCounts all pulled up, `persistPlayers` called once with her id); Nirmal's exact real drift reproduced with his correct higher XC confirmed NOT regressed while his badge gap still closes; a no-drift pair is a true no-op (`persistPlayers` never called); brand-only id-mismatch still resolves via the existing brand-fallback convention; an mc-only "ghost" player with no PLAYERS match is a safe no-op, not a crash; admin/host rows (`role !== 'player'`) are skipped entirely; a badge already revoked on the mc side is correctly NOT re-added by the monotonic reconcile (confirms the safety net won't fight a legitimate host correction); the pre-existing "[object Object]" corrupted-literal guard carries through the new union helper. The `mcSavePlayerForm`/`mcRemovePlayerBadge` direct-mirror edits were verified by direct inspection (mechanical, same pattern as the already-tested `broadcastPlayerChange` mirror) rather than a separate harness.
- HOST ACTIONS: none required for Kaitlin/Nirmal specifically (both already corrected in Supabase above) — worth telling Kaitlin her 3,400 XC / 7 badges are now live everywhere, and that her pending P2P chat resubmission (flagged in v1.91) still needs a manual approve. Watch for any other tester reporting "my host awarded me something and it isn't showing" between now and this patch's deploy — the drift class this closes could plausibly explain other FeedForward reports filed as generic "XC/badge mismatch" over the past week.
